Text:—Thus चतुर्षु.
Now, we take up the declension of प्रियचतुर् which may be declined in all numbers (See Note under S. 338). प्रियचतुर् + सु = प्रियचतु + आ + र् + स् (VII. 1. 98. S. 331) = प्रियचत्वाः. In the Voc: Sing. instead of अम् there will be अन् by VII. 1. 99. S. 333. Thus हे प्रियचत्वः । The Nom: Dual and Pl: are प्रियचत्वारौ, प्रियचत्वारः. As चतुर् here is a secondary member of a Compound the augment नुट् required by VII. 1. 55. S. 338 is not added in the formation of the Gen: Pl; Thus we have प्रियचतुराम्. But if the compound be not a Bahuvrihi, and चतुर् be a principal member, then the Genitive Pl. will be परमचतुर्णाम् ॥
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in र्.
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ल्.
Now we take up the declension of कमल. This is derived from the Noun कमलम् or कमला by passing through the चुरादिगण under the rule तत्करोति तदाचष्टे, that is, when the sense is कमलं कमलां वाऽऽचक्षाणः that one speaks of Kamala or Kamalâ. Thus कमल + णिच् (of चुरादिगण). To this we add the affix क्विप् when the णिच् is elided by VI. 4. 51. S. 2313. Thus we get कमल. Its declension is Nom. कमल, कमलौ, कमलाः. Its Loc. Pl. कमलत्सु. (The त् being changed to ल्).
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in ल्.
There is no noun ending in ‹?›. Therefore we take up the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in म्. In the declension of these nouns, the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
341. न् is substituted, at the end of a Pada, for the final म् of a root.
As प्रशान्, this is formed by adding क्विप् to the root शम् ॥ The lengthening takes place by VI. 4. 15. S. 2556. The नत्व being considered as asiddha is not elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236.
The word पदस्य is understood here also. So we have प्रशामौ, प्रशामः where म् is not at the end of a pada.
The Nom: forms are प्रशान्, प्रशामौ, प्रशामः ; The Instr: Dual is प्रशान्भ्याम्, &c.
—:o:—
Now, we take up the declension of किम् सर्ववत् ॥ In its declension, the following rule applies :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
342. √ Kaṭi, Pre. कण्टति । or ‹?› । Caus. काटयति । Per. चकाण्ट । I Fut. कण्टिता । Aor. अकाण्डीत् । Desi. चिकण्टिषति । Inten. चाकण्ट्यते । Yaṅ-luk चाकण्डीति or चाकण्टि । Noun कटकः ॥

Kaṭṭa, Pre. ‹?› । Ger. कटित्वा or काष्ट्ट्वा । Part. कट्टवान् ॥

—इ ३४२ क । गतौ ।
343. A. √ i, to go.
‹?› (VII. 2. 103. S. 2296)
Pre. एति । Per. इयाय, ईयतुः, ईयुः । इययिथ or इयेथ, ईयथुः, ईय, इयाय or इयय, ईयिव, ईयिम । I Fut. एता ॥ II Fut. ‹?› Impera. ‹?› Bene. (VII. 4. 25. S. 2298.) ‹?› Imperf. ऐत् । Pote. इयात् । Aor. अगौत् (+ऐषीत्) ऐष्टाम्, ऐषुः, ऐषीः, ऐष्टम्, ऐष्ट, ऐषम्, ऐष्व, ऐष्म । Cond. ऐष्यत् । Pass. ईयते । Caus. आपयति । Aor. आपिपत् । Desi. ईषिषति (VI. 4. 10. S. 2614) Past Part. इतः, इतवान् ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
343. Heṭha, to be wicked ; (to vex; to trouble; to strike ; to be born; to purify; to cause prosperity.)

Pre. हेठति ।

It is not given here in the Siddhânta. See No. 285.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
344. अय् is substituted for the इद् of इदम् in the Nom. Sing. masculine.

As अयम् ॥

The case ending is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In other cases, sûtra VII. 2. 102. S. 265. would apply and there will be Para-rûpa (VI. 1. 97. S. 191) and so will assume the form इद ॥

At this stage, will apply the following rule.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
345. And म is substituted for the द् of इदम् before a case-affix.

As इमौ, इमे, इमम्, इमौ, इमान् ॥ Thus इदम् + अम् = इद + अम् (VII. 2. 102 S. 265.) = इम + अम् (VII. 2. 109 S. 345) = इमम् (VI. 1. 97, S. 191).

It is a general rule that there is no Vocative case of त्यदादि words.

In forming the Instrumental and other cases, the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
346. अन is substituted for the इद् of इदम् in the Instrumental singular and the cases that follow, provided that the augment akach is not added.

As अनेन, अनयोः ॥ Why do we say "not when क is added by V. 3. 71"? Observe इमकेन, इमकयोः ॥ The word आप् (आपि) in the sûtra is a pratyâhâra, formed with the आ of टा (Ins. Sg.), and प् of सुप् (Loc. Pl.).

Before consonantal affixes, the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
347. The इद् of इदम् is elided before an âp case affix beginning with a consonant, provided that the augment अकच् is not added.

Here applies the maxim—"The rule I. 1. 52. S. 42, by which a substitute should take the place of only the final letter of that which is exhibited in the genitive case, is not valid where what is exhibited in the genitive is meaningless, provided the rule teaching the substitution does not teach a change in a reduplicative syllable."

Having elided इद् of इदम्, the only portion that remains now is म् which is replaced by अ VII. 2. 102 S. 265. Thus we have only अ left. Thus अ + भ्याम् ॥ Now VII. 3. 102 S. 202 declares that a final अ is lengthened before a case affix beginning with यञ् ॥ But the solitary अ is initial and cannot therefore be final and so it should not be lengthened. To remove this doubt, we have the following Sûtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
348. Muṇḍi, (also puḍi and suḍi) to shave; to shear, to crush; Maitreya says 'Some say the root is ‹?›' In some Dhātukoṣas it is given ‹?›

Pre. मुण्डति, पुण्डति । Noun: मुण्डः, मुण्डकः ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
349. This substitution of ऐस् (required by VII. 1. 9 S. 203) does not take place after इदम् and अदस्, except when they end in क ॥

Thus अ + भिः = एभिः (VII. 3. 103 S. 205). The dative forms are thus formed:—अ + ङे = अस्मै (VII. 1. 14 S. 215); अ + भ्याम् = आभ्याम्; अ + भ्यः = एभ्यः ॥ The Abl:, Gen: and Loc: forms are as follow:—अस्मात्, (VII. 1. 15 S. 216); आभ्याम्, एभ्यः; अस्य (VII. 1. 12. S. 201); अनयोः (VII. 3. 104 S. 207 and VII. 2. 112. S. 346); एषाम् (VII. 1. 52. S. 217); अस्मिन् (VII. 1. 15. S. 216); एषु (VIII. 3. 59 S. 212).

When अकच् is added the forms are as follows:—Nom: अयकम्, इमको, इमके; Acc: इमकम्, इमको, इमकान्; Instr: इमकेन, इमकाभ्याम्, इमकेः ॥

By the following rule, when इदम् is used in the second clause of a sentence referring to a man already mentioned in the first clause, the form is different in the Instr: and other cases.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
350. In the room of idam 'this,' in case of its re-employment in a subsequent member of the same sentence and referring to the same thing (anvâdeśa) there is the substitution of अश् which is anudâtta i. e., gravely accented, when the third case-affix and the rest follow.

Note:—The word अन्वादेश means literally saying (âdeśa) 'after' (anu) or after-say or re-employment.

अश् (actually अ) replaces इदम् in all cases except the nominative and the accusative, when anvâdeśa or repetition is implied. अ replaces the whole of इदम् by I. 1. 55 S. 45. and not only the final.

Text:—The substitute अश् will replace इदम्, even when the latter takes the affix अकच् (V. 3. 71.)
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
351. ✓ Vaṭi, to divide; to share. This is not found here in the Siddhānta.
Pre. वण्टति ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
352. (But such न्) is not elided in the Locative and Vocative Singular.
This debars the elision of न्, which otherwise would have taken place by the sûtra VIII. 2. 7. S. 236. The examples of non-elision of न्, in the Locative singular are to be found in the Vedas. As परमे व्योमन् (Rig. I. 164. 39). Here the sign of the Locative, namely, (ङि) is elided by VII. 1. 39 S. 3561. In the Vocative singular the न् is not elided; as हे राजन्, हे तक्षन् ॥
The very fact of the prohibition of the elision of न्, as contained in this aphorism, indicates by implication (jñâpaka), that a word does get the designation of pada, though an affix has been elided after it by using लुक्, yet such elided affix does sometimes produce its effect in spite of I. 1. 63. S. 263.
Vart:— Prohibition of the prohibition must be stated, when the Locative word is followed by another word in a compound. That is, when a compound is a Locative Tatpurusha, the न् is elided: as, चर्माणि तिला अस्य = चर्मतिलः, ब्रह्मणि निष्ठा अस्य = ब्रह्मनिष्ठः ॥
The Nom : Dual and Pl : are राजानौ ; राजानः ।
The Acc. Sing and Dual are राजानम् ; राजानौ ।
The Acc: Pl. is thus formed:—राजन् + शस् । Here राजन् gets the designation of bha by I. 4. 18. S. 231. and therefore the अ of राजन् is elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234. and the न् is changed to ञ् by VIII. 4. 40. S. 111. The elision of अ is not Sthanivat, because it is so prohibited in Sûtra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12.
Nor can the elision be considered asiddha on account of its being bahiranga.
There are two aspects under which संज्ञा or technical terms, and Paribhâshâs may be viewed in Panini's Grammar. One is यथोद्देशपक्ष and the other is कार्यकालपक्ष. The former i e यथोद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् means that "Samjnas and Paribhashas remain where they are taught ;" and the latter, i. e. कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् means that "Samjnâs and Paribhashâs are attracted by, or unite with, the rules that enjoin certain operations, provided that Samjnâs occur or are valid in those rules, and provided the Paribhashâs concern them."
Here we take the first alternative and the change of न् into ञ् being asiddha in the view of the rule I. 1. 94. S. 38., there is no antaranga-hood and so the Paribhasha which declares that "antaranga is stronger than bahiranga" finds no scope for application. Therefore ज् and ञ् combining form ज्ञ. Thus we get the Acc. Pl. राज्ञः; Inst. Sing is राज्ञा ॥
Similarly परमे व्योमन् || Here व्योमन् is in the Locative case. व्योमन् + ङि = व्योमन् + 0 (VII. 1. 39, S. 3561) Here the affix is elided by using the word लुक्, and therefore there will be no pratyaya-lakshana (I. 1. 63 S. 263). The result would be that the word व्योमन् would not get the designation of पद (सुप्तिङन्तं पदं) because it has no सुप् after it, so the rule (VIII. 2. 7. S. 236) will not hold good, and therefore there will be no elision of न् of व्योमन्. But in that case the present Sûtra would have been useless. But the very fact that this sûtra is made, indicates that the rule न लुमता is not nitya, and so, there will be pratyayalakshana. That being the case, the word becomes पद, and so rule VIII. 2. 7 would have applied to it, but for this Sûtra.
Although ‹?› excludes and debars ‹?›, but in this case it has been superseded by the former.
Now we take up the formation of Acc. pl.
Thus राजन् + शस् = राज् + 0 + न् + शस् (अल्लोपोऽनः) Here the zero will be sthânivat (by अचः परस्मिन् I. 1. 57 S. 50) That being the case, न् will not be changed to ञ् and so we could not get the form राज्ञः ॥ But the lopâdeśa is not sthânivat, because of the vârttika पूर्वत्रासिद्धे न स्थानिवत् (See Mahâbhâshya I. 1. 58 and Siddhânta VIII. 4. 1)
If it be said that the lopa rule is Bahiranga, because it takes place on account of the affix which is outside; and the change of न् into ञ् is inside it, or antaranga; and therefore the lopa will be asiddha with regard to ञ्, then we reply that there is no relation of Antaranga and Bahiranga here. The Paribhâshâ &c. is derived from the Jñâpaka of वाह ऊठ् (VI. 4. 132 S. 329) which belongs to the VIth Adhyâya and consequently does not see the vidhi of the VIIIth Adhyâya (VIII. 4. 41 S. 111.) by the sûtra पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् and so there will be no antaranga Bhâva. This proceeds on the view of यथोद्देश Paksha.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
353. ✓ Paṭha, to read or repeat aloud, recite; to study.
Pre. पठति । Per. पपाठ, पेठतुः, पेठुः, पेठिथ । I Fut. पठिता । Aorist अपाठीत् or अपपाठीत् । Caus. पाठयति । Desi. पिपठिषति । Inten. पापठ्यते । यङ्-लुक् । पापठीति or ‹?› ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
354. Of a root ending in र् or व्, the penultimate इ or उ is lengthened, before a consonantal beginning affix.
The lengthening takes place here, the elision of ‹?› is not considered here as sthānivat because of the prohibition in I. 1. 58 S. 57 with regard to दीर्घविधिः and so व् becomes penultimate.
Nor is this elision by VI. 4. 134. S. 234. a bahiraṅga and therefore asiddha, for the purposes of this rule which is an antaraṅga, for the reasons already given above under VIII. 2. 8. S. 352.
Thus Acc : Pl : is प्रतिदीव्यः ॥
Instr: Sg. प्रतिदीव्या &c.
-:0:-
Now we take up the declension of यज्वन् ॥ Its Nom: forms are यज्वा, यज्वानौ, यज्वानः ॥
But in Bha cases there will not be the elision of अ of मन् because of the following prohibition.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
355. The अ in अन् is not elided when the Bha stem ends in a consonant preceding व् or मन् ॥
Thus Acc : Pl : यज्वनः ॥ Instr: Sing and dual यज्वना, यज्वभ्याम् &c. Similar is the declension of ब्रह्मन् ॥ Nom. ब्रह्मा, ब्रह्माणौ, ब्रह्माणः, Acc. ब्रह्माणम्, ब्रह्माणौ, ब्रह्मणः; Ins. ब्रह्मणा, ब्रह्मभ्याम्, ब्रह्मभिः ॥
-:0:-
Now, we take up the declension of वृत्रहन् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
356. The penultimate vowel is lengthened only before the affix शि ( Nominative and Accusative Pl. ), when the stem ends in इन्, or हन्, or पूषन् or अर्यमन् and nowhere else.
To this prohibition is the exception contained in the following sūtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
357. The penultimate vowels of a stem ending in इन्, हन्, पूषन् or अर्यमन् are lengthened before the affix सु of the Nominative Singular, but not in Vocative Singular.
Thus वृत्रहा ॥ The न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7. S. 236, and the case-affix by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. In the Vocative singular we have हे वृत्रहन् ॥
The न is changed to ण by VIII. 4. 12 S. 307. Thus we get the following forms N. D. वृत्रहणौ ; N. Pl : वृत्रहणः, Acc: Sg and Dual : वृत्रहणम् and वृत्रहणौ respectively.
In Acc : Pl : the अ of हन् is elided by VI. 4. 134 S. 234 and the ह् is changed to guttural by the following Sūtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
358. A guttural is substituted for the ह् in हन् before an affix having an indicatory ञ्, or ण् and before न् ॥
The next Sūtra हन्तेरत्पूर्वस्य is divided by the author into two parts, viz., first, हन्तेः and then अत्पूर्वस्य ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
359. The न, in the root हन्, is changed to ण, when the verb is preceded by a preposition competent to cause the change.
As प्रहण्यात् ॥ This requires the न् of वृत्रहन् to be changed to ण । But to this the second half of the above Sūtra makes an exception,
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
360. तृ is diversely substituted for the final of मघवन्.
ऋ of तृ is इत्. And thus we get मघवत्.
Here applies the next Sūtra, showing the force of this indicatory,
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
361. Whatever has an indicatory उ, ऋ and ऌ, (with the exception of a root), and the stem अञ्च्, (मञ्चति) get the augment नुम् in the strong cases.

Thus Nom : Sing. is मघवान्. The penultimate अ is lengthened by VI. 4. 14. S. 425. The affix is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. and the त् is elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54.

The form being मघवन्त, the elision of त् takes place by the Tripadi rule संयोगान्तस्य लोपः VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. and therefore this elision is not perceived by the दीर्घ rule of the Sixth Book of Panini (i.e. VI. 4. 14. S. 425). The a of वन्त् therefore not being penultimate will not be lengthened, as it is not lengthened in Verbal Nouns like ‹?› &c, where also the elision of त् is held to be asiddha. Why do we lengthen it in the case of मघवन् ? Because of the word बहुलं in the last Sutra VI. 4. 128 S. 360.

As this word मघवान् requires the help of बहुल to give us the proper form, the author of Mahābhashya has effected the formation of मघवान् by the Unadi I. 159, and he has also assumed that the affix मतुप् will effect the same form when added to मघ in secular literature, and therefore he has in his commentary stated that the Sūtra मघवा बहुलं is a redundancy. The author of Bhatti Kavya also uses the form in secular literature as:—

‹?›

"That Maghavan eats fearlessly the sacrificial offerings in the sacrifices."

The Nom : Dual and Pl. will be मघवन्तौ, मघवन्तः ॥

The Voc : Sing will be हे मघवन् ॥

The Acc. forms are मघवन्तम्, मघवन्तौ, मघवतः ॥

Instr: forms are मघवता, मघवद्भ्याम् &c.

When तृ is not substituted for the final न् of मघवन्, then the Nom : Sing is मघवा ॥

Vartika:—In the Chhandas, the affixes इनि and वनिप् are added to nouns in the sense of मतुप् (See Sūtra V. 2. 122. S. 3498). Therefore if the word मघवन् be formed with वनिप् added to मघ then the word मघवन् will have acute accent on the middle in the Chhandas alone, but in the secular literature it has acute accent on the final also. This is the difference, as मघवन्.

The Nom : Dual and Pl. are मघवानौ, मघवानः ॥

In the Sarvanāmasthāna affixes, मघवन्, without तृ is declined like राजन्. Thus N. D. मघवानौ, N. Pl. मघवानः; Acc. S. D. are मघवानम् and मघवानौ.

In forming the Acc. Pl, the following rule applies :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
362. The व of श्वन्, युवन् and मघवन् when ending in अन् becomes vocalised, but not before a Taddhita affix.

Thus मघवन् + शस् = मघ् उ अन् + शस् = मघ् उन् + शस् (अ and उ become उ by VI. 1. 108. S. 330) = मघोन + शस् (अ and उ become ओ by VI. 1. 87. S. 69) = मघोनः ॥

Why do we say 'when ending in अन्'? Observe Acc : Pl : मघवतः when the noun is मघवत् and not मघवन् ॥ In this case the Instr : Sg. is मघवता ॥

The feminine form of मघवत् is मघवती । Why do we say 'not before a Taddhita affix'? Observe माघवनम् ॥

The Instr : Sg. and Dual of मघवन् are मघोना, मघवद्भ्याम् &c. Similar is the declension of श्वन् ॥ Thus शुनः (Acc. Pl.), शुना (Instr : S.), श्वभ्याम् (Instr : Dual) &c.

Now we take up the declension of युवन् ॥

युवन् + शस् = यु + उ + न् + शस् ॥

Here the य of युवन् would also require to be vocalised. But this is prevented by the following Sūtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 363. ✓ Satha, to cheat, and also 'to hurt,' 'to feel pain.' Pre. शठति । Per. शशाठ, शेठतुः, शेठुः । I Fut. शठिता । Aorist अशाठीत्, अशठीत् । Caus. शाठयति । Desi. शिशाठिषति । Inten. शाशठ्यते । Yaṅ luk, शाशठीति, ‹?› ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 364. Sutha, to be impeded or hindered. Pre. शोठति, शुण्ठति । Per. शुशोठ, शुशुण्ठ । I Fut. शोठिता, शुण्ठिता । Aorist अशोठीत्, अशुण्ठीत् । Caus. शोठयति, शुण्ठयति । Desi. शुशोठिषति, शुशुण्ठिषति । Inten. ‹?› ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
365. आत् ( आ ) is substituted for the final of 'pathin', 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', before the ending सु (of the Nom. Sg.).
Though the sthānin here is a nasal (i. e. न्), yet the substitute आ is not to be nasalised by the rule of nearness (I. 1. 50. 39) but to be pronounced purely, for the आत् of the sûtra is really आ + आत्, indicating that pure आ is to be taken and not the nasal आँ ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
366. अत् is substituted for the इ of 'pathin', 'mathin' and 'ṛbhukshin', in the strong cases.
Note:—Though the anuvṛitti of आत् was here, the separate mention of अत् is for the sake of VI. 4. 98 S. 354 by which in the case of ऋभुक्षिन् we have two forms, ऋभुक्षाणम् and ऋभुक्षणम् ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 367. √ Suthi, to become dry. Pre. ‹?› । Nouns ‹?› । शुण्ठी ।
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
368. The last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, is dropped in pathin, mathin, and ṛbhukshin, before an affix beginning with a vowel or य (before which the stem is called Bha I. 4. 18).
As पथः, पथा, पथे, मथः, मथा, मथे, ऋभुक्षः, ऋभुक्षा, ऋभुक्षे ॥
In the Feminine the affix ङीप् will be added by IV. 1. 5. as पथिन् + ङीप्, and the इन् is elided before the affix ङीप् by the present Sûtra. Thus सुपथी नगरी, and ऋभुक्षी सेना.
In the Neuter, there is no lengthening of VII. 1. 85. S. 365. because the affix is elided by using the word लुक् (VII. 1. 23. S. 319) and therefore the affix सु leaves no trace behind by I. 1. 63. S. 263. Thus सुपथि वनम्. Thus सुपथिन् + सु = सुपथिन् + 0 = सुपथि (The final न् is elided by VIII. 2. 7, S. 236).
In the Vocative Sing. of the Neuter Noun सुपथिन्, the elision of न् is optional, according to the following Vārtika:—
Vārtika:—In the Voc. Singular of the Neuter nouns, the elision of final न् is optional.
Thus हे सुपथिन् or हे सुपथि.
The short इ of सुपथि is not guṇated (as it is guṇated in हे हरे) because of the prohibition contained in VIII. 2. 2, S. 353 by which the elision of न् is asiddha in the case of case-endings.
In the Nom: Dual, the base being bha, the टि portion of पथिन् is elided before the Dual affix शी. Thus सुपथी ॥
In the Nom: Pl. (शि) which is a Sarvanāmasthāna affix (I. 1. 42. S. 313) there is no elision and the rules VII. 1. 86 and 87 S. 366 and 367 apply and so we get the form सुपन्थानि ॥
The Acc: forms are the same as the Nominative ones, as सुपथि, सुपथी, सुपन्थानि ॥
The Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपथा, सुपथिभ्याम् ॥
The Dative Sing: is सुपथे &c.
Now, we take up the declension of पञ्चन्. It is a षट् word by the following definition.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
369. The Saṅkhyās having ष् or न् as their final are called ṣaṭ.
It is one of the peculiarities of षट् words that they lose their nominative and accusative plural terminations (VII. 1. 22. S. 261). Thus पञ्च, पञ्च ॥
Why do we say संख्या ॥ Observe विप्रुषः and पामानः ॥
Note:—This sûtra defines the term षट् which is a subdivision of the larger group saṅkhyā. Those Saṅkhyās which end in ष् or न् are called षट् । The word saṅkhyā is understood in this sûtra, because the word षट् is in the feminine gender, showing that it qualifies saṅkhyā which is also feminine.
The numerals that end in ष् or न् are six, namely पञ्चन् 'five', षष् 'six', सप्तन् 'seven', अष्टन् 'eight', नवन् 'nine', दशन् 'ten'.
The word अन्तः in the sûtra shows that the letters ष् and न् must be aupadeśika i. e., must belong to the words as originally enunciated and not added afterwards as affix &c. Thus in शतानि 'hundreds', सहस्राणि 'thousands', अष्टानाम् 'of eights' the न् is not radical, but an augment, and therefore they are not षट् and the nominative and accusative plural terminations are not elided; as शतान् + इ = शतानि &c.
In forming Nom: Pl: of शत we have शत + शि. Then we add नुम् by VII. 1. 72. S. 314. Thus we get शतानि. Here the word शत is a saṅkhyā and ends in न्. Why should not this शि be elided by VII. 1. 22. S. 261? This शि is not elided by the maxim संनिपातपरिभाषा ॥ For the maxim, see VII. 1. 13. S. 204. Because it was the presence of शि that caused the insertion of नुम् and now this न् cannot cause the destruction of its originator. Thus we get शतानि ॥ सहस्राणि is also similarly formed.
The Instr, Dative and Abl: plurals are पञ्चभिः, पञ्चभ्यः, पञ्चभ्यः respectively.
The augment नुट् is added by VII. 1. 55. S. 338 in forming the Gen. Pl: Then the following sûtra comes into operation.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
370. In a stem ending in न्, the preceding vowel is lengthened before the affix नाम् ।
Thus पञ्चन् + नाम् (VII. 1. 55, S. 338) = पञ्चान् + नाम् (VI. 4. 7, S. 370) = पञ्चानाम् (न् being elided by VIII. 2. 7, S. 236). The Loc. Pl. is पञ्चसु ।
Similar is the declension of परमपञ्च । Thus N. Pl. परमपञ्च, Gen. Pl. is परमपञ्चानाम् ।
When पञ्च is a secondary member of a compound, there is neither लुक् of Sûtra VII. 1. 22, S. 261, nor the नुट् augment of VII. 1. 55, S. 338. Thus प्रियपञ्चन् is declined as Nom. प्रियपञ्चा, प्रियपञ्चानौ, प्रियपञ्चानः; Acc. प्रियपञ्चानम् ॥
Similar is the declension of सप्तन्, नवन् and दशन् । In the declension of अष्टन् the following rules apply.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
371. √ Adda, to join; to attack; to argue, to apply closely, to be devoted.
Pre. ‹?› । Per. ‹?›, ‹?› । I Fut. ‹?› । Aorist ‹?› । Caus. ‹?› । Aorist ‹?› । Desi. ‹?› (the a is not reduplicated because of VI. 1. 3. S. 2446).
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
372. Kadda, to be harsh or severe; to be hard or rough.
Pre. कड्डति । Per. चकड्ड । I Fut. कड्डिता । Aorist अकड्डीत् । Caus. कड्डयति । Desi. चिकड्डिषति । Inten. चाकड्यते । चाकडीति or ‹?› ।
Noun:— ‹?› compound of कस् + अम् ॥ The three roots चुड्ड, अड्ड and कड्ड have a d as penultimate. Therefore with the affix क्विप् the forms would be चुत्, अट् and कत् respectively.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
373. Kridri, to play; to amuse oneself.
Pre. क्रीडति । Per. चिक्रीड, चिक्रीडतुः । I Fut. क्रीडिता । Aorist अक्रीडीत् । Caus. क्रीडयति । Aorist अचिक्रीडत् । Desi. चिक्रीडिषति । Inten. चेक्रीड्यते । यङ्लुक् चेक्रीडीति or चेक्रेत्ति ।
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
374. √ Tudri, to split, to push; to injure.
Pre. ‹?›, ‹?› । Per. ‹?› or ‹?› । I Fut. ‹?›, ‹?› । Aorist ‹?› । Caus. ‹?›, ‹?› । Desi. ‹?›, ‹?› । Inten. ‹?› । यङ्लुक् ‹?› or ‹?› ।
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
375. There is elision of the affix ‹?› when reduced to the single letter ‹?› ॥

Note:—The affix ‹?› includes ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› &c. In all these, the real affix is ‹?›, which being an apṛkta (I. 2. 41 S. 251), is elided. Thus ‹?›, ‹?› (III. 2. 87 S. 2998). Here the affix क्विप् is elided. So also घृतस्पृक्, तैलस्पृक् (III. 2. 58 S. 432). Here the affix ‹?› is elided. So also अर्धभाक्, पादभाक्, तुरीभाक् (III. 2. 62 S. 2976). Here the affix ‹?› is elided.

Why do we say "of an apṛkta—an affix consisting of a single letter"?

Observe ‹?› formed by the affix ‹?› (‹?› being the real affix ‹?›); so also ‹?› formed by ‹?›, see Uṇādi Sûtras IV. 53, 44. No root can become a noun unless some kṛt affix is added to it (see I. 2. 45 and 46); hence the necessity of these imaginary affixes, in order to raise certain roots bodily, without any change, to the rank of nouns—from Dhâtu to a Prâtipadika the way lies only through an affix. And though these imaginary affixes are after all totally elided, yet by I. 1. 62, they leave their characteristic mark behind, namely, the derivative word becomes a nominal stem &c. Thus ‹?› words are adverbs (Gati) and Indeclinables.

The word ‹?› being a ‹?› word gets the designation of Prâtipadika by I. 2. 46 S. 179 and therefore we add to it the case affixes ‹?› &c. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› ॥ At this stage comes the following sûtra for application.

N. S.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
376. The nominal stem ‹?› gets before the strong cases the augment ‹?›, when it does not stand in a compound.

Thus ‹?› (the ‹?› being elided by VI. 1. 68, S. 252.) = ‹?› (the ‹?› being elided by VIII. 2. 23, S. 54).

Thus we get ‹?›.

Now applies the following sûtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 377. √ Raudri to despise. Pre. — रौडति, रोडति ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
378. A Guttural is substituted for a Palatal, before a jhal letter or at the end of a word.

This requires the change of ज् to a guttural i.e. of क class. The कुत्व ordained by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377 is asiddha or not perceived by the present Sûtra, which is antecedent to VIII. 2. 62. S. 377 in the order of enunciation by Pâṇini. In the case of ‹?› and ‹?›, the ‹?› is not changed to a letter of the ‹?› class even when we take words to be formed by the affix ‹?› under Sûtra VIII. 2. 62 S. 377. The reason for this we shall explain under Sûtra VIII. 2. 68. S. 443 in declining the Neuter noun.

Thus Nom. forms are सुयुक् or सुयुग्, सुयुजौ, सुयुजः ॥

In the Sûtra VII. 1. 71, S. 376, the root is exhibited as युजेः showing that that root of the Dhâtupâṭha should be taken which ends in इ, viz., the root युजिँ the 7th root of the रुधादि class. Therefore it does not apply to the root युज the 10th root of the दिवादि class and is Âtmanepadî. In the latter case, the form will be युक्.

Now we take up the declension of खन्. It is derived from खज् ‘to move' and 'to feel done up' by adding the affix ‹?› ॥

The ‹?› of ‹?› is elided because it is ‹?›, leaving behind ‹?› to which the augment ‹?› is added by VII. 1. 58. S. 2262. Thus we get ‹?›. Then ‹?› is elided by VIII. 2. 23 S. 54. In the N. S. the affix सु is elided by VI. 1. 68. S. 252. Thus the N. S. remains as खन्. The N. Dual and Pl. are खञ्जौ and खञ्जः &c.

Now we take up the declension of राज्. By VIII. 2. 36. S. 294, the ज् of राज् is changed to ष. Then the ष is changed to ड by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84, and VIII. 4. 56. S. 206. Then ड is changed to ट. Thus we get N. S. राट् or राड्. The N. D. and Pl. are राजौ, राजः ॥ Loc. Pl. is राट्सु or राड्सु. Similarly is declined विभ्राज्. So also देवेज्. Its Nom. forms are देवेद् or देवेड्, देवेजौ, देवेजः ॥ The Nom. forms of विश्वसृज् are विश्वसृद् or विश्वसृड्, विश्वसृजौ, विश्वसृजः ॥ With regard to ‹?› and ‹?› there is not gutturalisation as will be further explained under Sûtra VIII. 2. 68. S. 443. The N. S. of परिमृज् is परिमृट् ॥

The word विभ्राज् given above is formed from that root which belongs to फणादि subdivision of भ्वादि gaṇa, i.e. the root डुभ्राज् 'to shine' भ्वादि 875, and not the root भ्राज् number 20 of the भ्वादि where it is exhibited भ्राजृ दीप्तौ. This we do, because the root भ्राज् is read along with root राज् in the subdivision; and as the VIII. 2. 36. S. 294. mentions भ्राज् and राज् together, the भ्राज् here should be taken as the भ्राज् of the फणादि class, where also both are enunciated together and not the other which is shown along with ‹?› and ‹?› (Dhâtupâṭha I. 193, 194 and 195). In the case of this भ्राज् there will be कुत्व and not षत्व. Thus N. S. is विभ्राक् or विभ्राग्. Instr. D. विभ्राग्भ्याम् &c.

Vârtika:—When व्रज् is preceded by upapada परि there comes the affix क्विप् and the ‹?› is lengthened and ज् is changed to ष when it is final in a Pada. Thus N. S. of परिव्राज् is परिव्राट् which means one who has gone out leaving every thing. The N. Dual and Pl are परिव्राजौ and परित्राजः respectively.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
Now, we take up the declension of विश्वराज्. In its declension, the following rule applies :--

379. The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before वसु and राट् (the form assumed by राज्).

Thus विश्वावसुः, i.e. one whose wealth is the whole universe. The rule applies to the राट् form of राज् in the Nominative singular, and not when it retains its own form as विश्वराजौ, विश्वराजः ॥

The राट् is taken in the Sûtra only as an illustration of its Padânta form. It does not mean that the form विश्वाराड् is not valid. Thus N. S. has both forms, i.e. विश्वाराट् and विश्वाराड्.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
380. √ Ada, to try; to exert.
Pre. — अडति । Per. — आड, आदतुः, आडुः । 1st Fut. — अडिता । Aorist — आडीत्, आडिष्टाम्, आडिषुः । Caus. — आडयति । Desi. — अदिडिषति ॥
Noun — आडः 'the sting or tail of a scorpion.' Hence 'sharp.' व्याडः 'peculiarly sharp.' The son of Vyaḍa is व्याडिः ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
381. √ Lada, to dally; to sport; to play. This is Ghaṭādi also.
Pre. — लडति । Per. — ललाड । 1st Fut. — लडिता । Aorist — अलाडीत्, अलडीत् । Caus. — लाडयति । Desi. — लिलडिषति । Inten. — लालाल्यते । यङ्लुक् — लालडीति । लालत्ति ॥
According to Kshirasvamin and others, the ḍ and l being interchangeable and so also v and l, we have the form वलति &c. also.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
382. √ Lala, (to play; to sport; to dally.), to desire. This root is found in the Siddhanta Kaumudi, in the sense of 'to desire.' Madhava says under लड : "Some read lala ipsayam after it." Kshirasvamin and Purushakara do not approve it as a separate root.
Pre. — ललति । Caus. — लालयति । Noun — ललना ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
Then the rule after the following applies, to understand which the following rule is necessary.

383. The substitutions taught hereafter upto VII. 2. 98 take effect with regard to the portions of युष्मद् and अस्मद् upto म् ie the substitutes replace युष्म and अस्म ||

This is an Adhikâra Sûtra and exerts governing influence on all the seven subsequent sûtras in the order of Ashțâdhyâyî.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
385. In the remaining cases where (आ or य is not substituted by VII. 2. 88. and 89. S. 387, 392.) there is elision of the final of yushmad and asmad.

Thus युष्मद् + सु = युष्मद् + अम् (VII. 1. 28. S. 342) = त्वद् (VII. 2. 94. S. 384) + अम् = त्व + अम् (द् is elided by the present sûtra) = त्वम् (by VI. 1. 97. S. 191, and VI. 1. 107. S. 194). Similarly, the N. S. of अस्मद् is अहम् ॥

Why is not टाप् added in the feminine in 'त्वं स्त्री' 'अहं स्त्री'? For त्व + अम् and अह + अम् the pûrvarûpa rule ordained by VI. 1. 97. S. 191 and VI. 1. 107. S. 194, though subsequent, is after all bahiranga, and would be set aside by the antaranga rule ordaining टाप् to be added to त्व and अह?

True. But युष्मद् and अस्मद् have no genders, and therefore they have no feminine forms and consequently would not give occasion to the addition of the affix टाप्.

Or, in order to avoid all this difficulty about टाप्, some would elide the अद् (or remaining portion) of युष्मद् and अस्मद् under this sûtra. They argue that by the previous sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 the portions 'yushm' and 'asm', namely the portions upto म of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are replaced by substitutes. The portion that remains (शेष) is अद्, and it is this अद् which is to be elided.

According to their view, the word शेष does not refer to the vibhakti or case affix, but the force of Locative in शेषे is that of a genitive, meaning “of the remaining” and to point out the particular sthânî which is to be replaced. Therefore in युष्मद् and अस्मद्, the युष्म् and अस् portions have been already operated upon by other rules, the द् that remains is a portion.

In this view, the Sûtra should be translated as "in the remaining cases (i. e. where आ is not substituted as by VII. 2. 88. S. 387, nor य as by VII. 2. 89. S. 392) there is elision of the remaining (अद्) portion (I. 1. 64. S. 79) of these two (युष्मद् and अस्मद्)".

In the feminine, there is one more point to be considered even in the light of the second explanation. In युष्मद् + अम् = त्व + अद् + अम् if we follow the ordinary rule of ‹?› the अद् should be elided first by शेषे लोपः; then should apply the rule of अतो गुणे if at all. Then the form will be त्व + अम् ॥ Here त्व ends with अ, and so would require टाप् in the feminine, and the same difficulty again recurs. To clear up this point, we state that the rule of elision (शेषे लोपः) is bahiranga, because its efficient cause lies outside in the affix अम्, while the अतो गुणे rule is antaranga, because the occasion for its application or the efficient cause is within the very form त्व + अद्. Therefore अतो गुणे will apply first, we get त्वद् + अम्. Then शेषे लोपः produces its effect i. e. अद् is elided, and we get त्व् + अम् ॥ As there is no अ in त्व्, it would not require टाप् ॥ Thus we get त्वम् in the feminine also.

So also परमत्वम्, परमाहम्, अतित्वम् and अत्यहम्. In forming the N. Dual, the following rules apply.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 386. युव is substituted for युष्म् and आव for अस्म्, when the bases themselves denote duality.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
387. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before the ending of the Nom. Du. in the spoken language.

As युवाम्, आवाम् ॥ It would have been better had the Sûtra been enunciated as “औङि” only. Why in the “spoken language”? Observe युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे in the Veda, so also आवाम् ॥

Why 'upto म'? Observe युवकाम्, आवकाम् ॥ The क (V. 3. 71. S. 2026), is not replaced. Similarly VII. 2. 97. S. 389 teaches that त्व and म replace 'yushmad' and 'asmad' in the singular; by the sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 'yushm' and 'asm' are only replaced. Thus त्वया, मया the अद् portion remains for which य is substituted by VII. 2. 89. S. 392. Had the whole been replaced, then the अ of त्व and म would have been replaced by य (VII. 2. 89. S. 392), and given us undesired forms like त्या and म्या ॥ Similarly the forms युवकाभ्याम् and आवकाभ्याम् would not have been evolved.

In forming the N. Pl. the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 388. ✓ Shtepri. Pre. स्तेपते । Per. तिष्टेपे । I Fut. स्तेपिता । II Fut. स्तेपिष्यते । Imperative स्तेपताम् । Imper. अस्तेपत । Pote. स्तेपेत । Bene. स्तेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अस्तेपिष्ट । Condi. अस्तेपिष्यत । Caus. स्तेपयते । Desi. तिस्तेपिषते । Inten. तेष्टेप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
389. ✓ Tepri, to tremble, shake. By the force of च it means also to sprinkle.

Pre. तेपते । Per. तितेपे । I Fut. तेपिता । II Fut. तेपिष्यते । Impera. तेपताम् । Imper. अतेपत । Pote. तेपेत । Bene. तेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अतेपिष्ट । Condi. अतेपिष्यत । Caus. तेपयते । Desi. तितेपिषते । Inten. तेतेप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 390. ✓ Glepri, to be poor. Pre. ग्लेपते । Per. जिग्लेपे । I Fut. ग्लेपिता । Bene. ग्लेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अग्वेपिष्ट । Caus. ग्लेपयते । Desi. जिग्लेपिषते । Inten. जेग्लेप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
391. ✓ Tuvepri, to shake, to tremble.

Pre. वेपते । Per. विवेपे । I Fut. वेपिता । Aorist अवेपिष्ट । Caus. वेपयति (The Causative is Parasmaipadi because the verb has the sense of motion I. 3. 87. S. 2753). Desi. विवेपिषते । Inten. वेवेप्यते ॥

Nouns:— वेपथुः 'trembling.' (III. 3. 89 S. 3267 because of टु) । विप्रुथः (Uṇ. II. 52), वेपनः (with ल्युट् III. 2. 148 S. 3128).
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
392. ✓ Kepri, 393. ✓ Gepri, 394. ✓ Glepri, to tremble, and to move. By the force of च, both the senses of trembling and moving are taken. This is done by yoga-vibhāga according to Swāmī. According to Maitreya, the sense of trembling would be understood by context even without च. His meaning is that these roots could well have been read with चेप, but they are not done, because traditionally they are read separately. The ✓ Glep is repeated because it has a different meaning here.

Pre. केपते । Per. चिकेपे । I Fut. केपिता । Bene. केपिषीष्ट । Aorist अकेपिष्ट । Caus. केपयति (I. 3. 87 S. 2753). Desi. चिकेपिषते । Inten. चेकेप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
393. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending, beginning with a consonant, when it is not a substitute.
The substitute case-endings are given in VII. 1. 27-33. S. 399 &c.
Thus युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्, युष्माभिः, अस्माभिः ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
394. In the Dative Singular तुभ्य is substituted for युष्म and मह्य for अस्म ॥
The affix अम् is substituted for ङे by VII. 1. 28. S. 382 the तू is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385.
Thus तुभ्यम्, मह्यम्, परमतुभ्यम्, परममह्यम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतिमह्यम्, युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम् ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
395. ✓ Mepri, to move. According to Maitreya it means to serve, to attend upon. The reading of Kshirasvami is mepri, repri, lepriygatau. But Maitreya reads it as meprillepti sevane; repri plavagatau. Some texts have धेपु and धेषु ॥

Pre. मेपते । Per. मिमेपे । I Fut. मेपिता । Bene. मेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अमेपिष्ट । Caus. मेपयति । Desi. मिमेपिषते । Inten. मेमेप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 396. ✓ Repri, to go. According to Maitreya it means 'to leap, jump, swim'. Pre. रेपते । Per. रिरेपे । I Fut. repitā । Bene. repishīshṭa । Aorist अरेपिष्ट । Caus. रेपयति । Desi. रिरेपिषते । Inten. रेरेप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
397. अत् is substituted for the Ablative भ्यस् after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥
As युष्मत्, अस्मत् ॥
The द् is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385 before the case-ending भ्यस् and युष्म + अत् = युष्मत् by VI. 1. 97. S. 191.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
398. ✓ Dhepri. Pre. धेपते । Per. दिधेपे । I Fut. धेपिता । Aorist अधेपिष्ट । Caus. धेपयति । Desi. दिधेपिषते । Inten. देधेप्यते ॥

त्रपूष ३९९ लज्जायाम् । त्रपते ॥

The Present is त्रपते । In forming the Perfect, the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
399. ✓ Trapash, to be ashamed, abashed.

Pre. त्रपते । Per. त्रेपे । I Fut. त्रपिता or त्रप्ता । II Fut. त्रपिष्यते or त्रप्स्यते । Imperative त्रपताम् । Imper. अत्रपत । Pote. त्रपेत । Bene. त्रपिषीष्ट or त्रप्सीष्ट । Aorist अत्रपिष्ट or अत्रप्त । Condi. अत्रपिष्यत or अत्रप्स्यत । Caus. त्रपयति । Aorist अतित्रपत् । Being a Ghaṭādi root also (see 859) it is mit (VI. 4. 92. S. 2568) and hence the shortening in the Causative. Desi. तित्रपिषते or तित्रप्सते । Inten. तात्त्रप्यते । यङ्लुक् तात्त्रपीति or तात्त्रप्ति ॥ Past Part. Pass. त्रप्तः । Past Part. Act. त्रप्तवान् । Ger. त्रपित्वा or त्रप्त्वा । Infini. त्रपितुम् । त्रप्तुम् । Nouns:— त्रपिष्णुः (III. 2. 136 S. 3116). त्रपु 'Tin.'
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
400. ✓ Kapi, to move; to tremble.

Pre. कम्पते । Per. चकम्पे । I Fut. कम्पिता । Caus. कम्पयति । (I. 3. 87 S. 2753). Desi. चिकम्पिषते । Inten. चाकम्प्यते । Nouns:— काम्पुः (III. 2. 157 S. 3147). कम्पनः (III. 2. 148 or 149 S. 3128 or 3129). कपिः (Uṇ. IV. 144) वृषाकपिः "Vishnu or Rudra." कपिञ्जलः (See however Uṇ. I. 55).
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
401. Upto VIII. 3. 54, inclusive, should be always supplied in every subsequent sutra, the phrase "of a word," or "to the whole of a word."

Note:—This is an adhikara sutra, and extends up to VIII. 3. 55, in order of enunciation of Pânini's Ashtâdhyâyî.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 402. ✓ Labi, to sound. Pre. लम्बते । Per. ललम्बे । I Fut. लम्बिता । Aorist अलम्बिष्ट । Caus. लम्बयते । Desi. लिलम्बिषते । Inten. लालम्ब्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 403. ✓ Abi, to sound: Pre. अम्बते । Per. आनम्बे । I Fut. अम्बिता । Caus. अम्बयति । Aorist आन्बिवत् । Desi. अम्बिविषते । Nouns:— त्र्यम्बकः "The father of the three worlds," अम्बरीषः । अम्बा 'mother.'
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
404. For the Genitive, Dative and Accusative Dual of yushmad and asmad are substituted वाम् and नौ respectively, when a word precedes it and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta.

All the three sûtras पदस्य, पदात् and अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ are applicable here.

Note:—These two वाम् and नौ come in the Dual only, because other substitutes have been taught for the Singular and Plural in the two subsequent sûtras.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 405. For (the Genitive, Dative, and Accusative) plural of yushmad and asmad are substituted वस् and नस् respectively, (when a word precedes, and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta).\n\nThis Sûtra debars the substitutes वाम् and नौ taught in the previous Sûtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 406. For the Genitive and Dative Singular (of yushmad and asmad are substituted) ते and मे respectively, (when a word precedes and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse and these are anudâtta).
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
407. ✓ Kshībrī, to be drunk or intoxicated.

Pre. क्षीबते । Per. चिक्षीबे । I Fut. क्षीबिता । Caus. क्षीबयति । Aorist अचिक्षीबत् । Desi. चिक्षीबिषते । Noun:— क्षीबः ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
408. ✓ Śībhri, to boast.

Pre. शीभते । Per. शिशीभे । I Fut. शीभिता । Caus. शीभयते । Aorist अशिशीभत् । Desi. शिशीभिषते । Inten. शेशीभ्यते । यङ्लुक् शेशीब्धि । (त् changed to ध् by VIII. 2. 40. S. 2280, and भ् changed to ब् by VIII. 4. 53. S. 52). Noun:— शीभरः ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
409. The above substitutions do not take place also in connection with verbs having the sense of "seeing" when physical seeing is not denoted, but "knowing" is meant.\n\nNote:—The word पश्यार्थाः is equivalent to दर्शनार्थाः, and दर्शन means 'knowledge', i. e. verbs denoting 'to know'. आलोचन means perception obtained through sight i. e. physical 'seeing' opposed to metaphorical "seeing" or "knowing". The substitutions of त्वा and मा &c. for युष्मद् and अस्मद् do not take place when these pronouns are employed in connection with verbs denoting 'seeing' (metaphorically) but not 'looking' (physically).
Thus तथा त्वां समीक्षते भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति ॥ Why do we say when not meaning 'to look'? Observe भक्तस्त्वा पश्यति चक्षुषा ॥
Ishti :—With regard to verbs of "Seeing" the rule should apply even where the connection is not direct : as,
भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
410. When the pronoun follows after a Nominative which itself is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions may take place optionally even in anvâdesa.
Thus भक्तस्त्वमप्यहं तेन हरिस्त्वां त्रायते स माम् ॥ Here the alternative forms त्वा and मा are admissible.
We have already said that युष्मद् and अस्मद् substitutions do not take place when they are in the beginning of a pada. To this, however, there is an exception, when the first word is a Vocative, technically called आमन्त्रित which is defined in the next sutra, then also though युष्मद् and अस्मद् may not really be in the beginning of a pada, yet the substitutions will not take place by the sûtra after next.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 411. The word ending with the first case-affix, in the sense of addressing, is called Amantrita or Vocative.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
412. A preceding Vocative is considered as non-existent, (for the purposes of the accent of the following word, and the enclitic forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्) ||
Thus अग्ने ! तव ॥ देव ! अस्मान्पाहि ॥ अग्ने ! नय ॥ अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! ॥ Here तव and अस्मान् cannot get the shorter form, though they are not at the beginning of a hemistich, because they are preceded by the आमन्त्रित words अग्ने and देव ||
Similarly in अग्ने नय the verb नय does not become accentless as it would otherwise have become by VIII. 1. 28. S. 3935.
In अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! the rule VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654 does not apply.
Note:—Such a Vocative is treated as if not at all existing, it is simply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not existed. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-existent? They are (1) the absence of the accent-less-ness of the subsequent Vocative which the first, taken as a पद, would have caused under VIII. 1. 19. S. 3654. As देवदत्त ! यज्ञदत्त ! Here the first Vocative देवदत्त does not cause the second Vocative to lose its accent, but it remains first acute by VI. 1. 198. S. 3653. (2) The accent-less-ness of the verb required by VIII. 1. 28 S. 3935 is prevented : as, देवदत्त पचसि ॥ (3) The substitution of the shorter forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्, required by VIII. 1. 20-28 S. 404 &c. is prevented, as देवदत्त तव (not ते) ग्रामः स्वम्, देवदत्त मम (not मे) ग्रामः । (4) The application of VIII. 1. 37. S. 3944 takes place, in spite of the intervention of the Vocative between the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything from the immediateness (व्यवधान) of the Particle from the verb : as, अहो देवदत्त पचसि ॥ (5) For the purposes of VIII. 1. 47, S. 3954 though a Vocative may precede, the latter is still considered as non-existent and VIII. 1. 47 applies, as देवदत्त जातु पचसि । (6) So also in the case of VIII. 1. 49, S. 3956 as अहो देवदत्त पचसि, अहो देवदत्त जल्पसि, no option is allowed here by VIII. 1. 50. S. 3957.
In 'सर्वदा रक्ष देव नः' although the word देव is non-existent, yet taking रक्ष as a preceding word, नः is used.
In इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि the first Vocative गङ्गे is considered as non-existent with regard to मे, and, therefore, यमुने is considered as following immediately after the pada मे and thus यमुने becomes anudâtta, not because of गङ्गे, but because of मे. In other words, the intervention of the Vocatives does not stop the action of मे. This nighâta or accentlessness is heard in Pada-Pâtha only, i. e. when the words are read separately, and not in Sanhitâ-reading. In Sanhitâ there will be eka-sruti of I. 2. 39 S. 3668.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
413. A preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as if non-existent, for the purposes of the subsequent Vocative, which stands in apposition with the former.
Thus हरे दयालो नः पाहि "O Hari ! O Merciful! protect us." अग्ने तेजस्विन् "O Agni! O powerful!" Here दयालो is all anudâtta by VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654, because it is preceded by a word, though that word is Vocative.
Note:—Why do we say सामान्यवचनम् 'which is a generic word'? The rule will not apply when the Vocatives are synonyms. Thus ‹?› All these Vocatives are synonyms of Saraswati, and hence all retain their accent of the Vocative (VI. 1. 198). According to Padamanjari the reading given in Taittirîya Br. is :— ‹?› सामान्यवचनम् means 'a generic term'. When the first is a generic term, and the second is a specific term, (विशेषवचन) qualifying the first, and both are in the singular number, there the present rule will apply.
This sutra prevents the operation of the last sûtra in the particular case when the two Vocatives are in apposition, and the second qualifies the first. Thus अग्ने गृहपते, माणवक जटिलकाध्यापक ॥ The first vocative being considered as existing, the second vocative loses its accent.
Why do we say 'the vocative subsequent'? Observe देवदत्त पचसि here the verb does not lose its accent. Why do we say 'standing in apposition or सामानाधिकरण्ये'?
Observe देवदत्त पण्डित यज्ञदत्त, here the word पण्डित qualifies यज्ञदत्त, and is not in apposition with देवदत्त, and hence it retains its accent.
Then applies Sûtra VIII. 1. 74. S. 3655 which for the sake of convenience we repeat here.

४१३ (क) । विभाषितं विशेषवचने । ८ । १ । ७४ ॥
अत्र भाष्यम् । बहुवचनमिति वक्ष्यामीति । बहुवचनान्तं विशेष्यं समानाधिकरणे आमन्त्रिते विशेषणे परे अविद्यमानवद्वा । यूयं प्रभवः । देवाः शरण्याः । युष्मान् भजे वो भजे इति वा । इहान्वादेशेऽपि वैकल्पिका आदेशाः । सुपात् । सुपाद । सुपादौ । सुपादः । सुपादम् । सुपादौ ।

413. A. When the preceding Vocative is in the plural number, it is optionally considered as non-existent, if the subsequent Vocative, in apposition with it, is a specific term.
Here the author of the Mahabhashya states :— "The word bahuvachanam should be added to the sûtra to complete the sense." That is the sûtra should run as विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् ॥ We have therefore translated the sûtra with this emendation of Patanjali.
Thus यूयं प्रभवः, देवाः शरण्याः । युष्मान् भजे or वो भजे ॥ Here even in anvâdesa there is optional substitution of वः for युष्मान् ॥
Now, we take up the declension of सुपाद्. In the strong, i. e. in the first five cases it is declined as :—
Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom : सुपात् or सुपाद, सुपादौ सुपादः
Ac. सुपादम्, सुपादौ.
In the formation of the Acc. Pl. and the rest, the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
414. For पाद् is substituted पद् when the former is Bha.
Note:—The substitute replaces the whole form पाद् and not only the final, on the maxim निर्दिश्यमानस्यादेशा भवन्ति "substitutes take the place of that which is actually enunciated in a rule."
Thus the Acc. Pl. is सुपदः ॥
Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपदा, सुपाद्भ्याम् &c.
Now we take up the declension of अग्निमथ् meaning 'kindling fire'. It is declined as:
Nom. Sing. अग्निमत् or अग्निमद् Dual अग्निमथौ Pl. अग्निमथः
Instr: Dual is अग्निमद्भ्याम् &c.
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in थ.
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in च्.
Now we take up the declension of प्राञ्च्.
According to Sūtra III. 2. 59. S. 373, the affix क्विन् is employed after the verb अञ्च् to make it a Prātipadika, before the case terminations.
Thus having got the noun प्राञ्च्, in its declension, the following rules apply.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
415. In a root-stem ending in a consonant preceded by न्,—this न not being added to the root owing to its having an indicatory इ (VII. 1. 58)—the न is elided when an affix having an indicatory क or ङ् follows.
By Sūtra VII. 1. 70. S. 361, the stem अञ्च् gets the augment नुम् in the strong cases.
Then by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54, the last consonant is dropped. By VIII. 2. 62. S. 377, which says that 'a stem formed with the affix क्विन् substitutes at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant' we get the N. S. as प्राङ् thus:—
प्राञ्च् + सु = प्राच् (VI. 4. 24 S. 415) + सु = प्रा + न् (VII. 1. 70. S. 361) + च् + सु = प्रान् च् + ० (सु is elided by VI. 1. 68 S. 252) = प्रान् च् = प्रान् (च् being elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54) = प्राङ् (न् turned to ङ् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377).
The N. Dual &c. are formed by changing the न into anuswāra, and then the anuswāra into ञ् by VIII. 4. 58. S. 124.
Thus प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः Acc. प्राञ्चम्, प्राञ्चौ.
In forming the Acc. Pl. &c. the following rules apply.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
416. The अ of अच् (when अञ्च् loses its nasal,) is elided at the end of a Bha stem.
The lengthening of the first member takes place by VI. 3. 138: S. 417.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
417. The final vowel of the preceding member is lengthened before अच, when it assumes the form च, having lost its nasal and the vowel अ ॥
Thus Acc: Pl is प्राचः; Instr: Sing or Dual are प्राचा, प्राग्भ्याम् &c.
Now we take up the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् ॥ In strong cases, it is declined as प्रत्यङ्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, प्रत्यञ्चः ॥ प्रत्यञ्चम्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, in weak cases, अ is elided by VI. 4. 138 S. 416, and though this lopa is a bahiraṅga process, while the yaṇ or semivowel Sandhi is an antaraṅga process, yet this lopa is not considered asiddha for the purposes of this sandhi. This proceeds on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. See under Sūtra I. 3. 11 S. 46. Thus Acc: Pl: is प्रतीचः, Instr: Sing is प्रतीचा ॥ &c. प्रति + अञ्च् + शस् = प्रति + च् + अस् ॥ Here two sūtras simultaneously appear for application, viz. इको यणचि and अचः ॥ Now इको यणचि is antaraṅga, because the efficient cause अ of अञ्च् is inside that of शस्; and the efficient cause शस् by which अ of अञ्च् would be elided is outside; therefore yaṇ ādeśa should take place first, thus प्रति + अ + शस् = प्रत्य् + अच् + शस् ॥ After this अ should be elided as प्रत्य् + च् + अस् ॥ This however gives us no form, and so relying on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. the antaraṅga yaṇ substitution is set aside. Now, we take up the declension of अञ्च् as compounded with the pronoun अदस् meaning अमुम् अञ्चति ॥ Thus we have अदस् + अञ्च् + क्विन् । Here applies the following sūtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
418. In the room of the last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of a Pronoun and of the words विष्वक् and देव, is substituted अद्रि, when अञ्च् has no visible affix following it.
Thus अदस् + अञ्च् = अदद्रि + अञ्च् = अदद्य् + अञ्च्. At this stage, applies the following sūtra.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
419. When the pronoun अदस् does not end in स्, then there is substituted उ or ऊ for the vowel after द्, and म् for द् ॥
The short u in the sūtra is a samāhāra dvandva compound including both the short u and long ऊ. By the rule of antartama I. 1. 50 S. 39, the short vowel and the consonant following it will be replaced by the short u; and the long vowel with the consonant following it will be replaced by the long ū.
Thus अदद्य् + अञ्च् = अमुमुद्य् + अञ्च् : the first द् and अ are changed to म् and उ, and the second द् and य् are also changed to म् and उ; so the declension is:—
Nom. Sing. अमुमुयङ् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुयञ्चः
Acc. Sing. अमुमुयञ्चम् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुचः
Ins. Sing. अमुमुचा Dual अमुमुयग्भ्याम् &c. &c.
The mutva being considered as asiddha, there is no sandhi in
in æg, for the Sandhi rule is contained in the Sixth Book of Panini, while this g substitute is ordained in the Tripadi portion of Ashtadhyayi. Hence the Sutra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12 applies.
Some, by applying the following maxim, get the form
Paribhasha "When a modification is ordained with regard to something which is not final, the operation takes place on that only which is in proximity to the final." The second class apply this maxim and make g change only for which stands in proximity to the final.
There is a third form, which is obtained by explaining the असेः in the Sutra as मः सेर्यस्य सोऽयमसिः, तत्र सकारस्य मकारः क्रियते ॥ "The word असेः in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and means that in which अस् is substituted for ‹?›" The sutra is thus confined to the form derived by changing the द् into म् by VII. 2. 102. and not to any other.
Thus there are three views with regard to the application of the present sutra:—
(1) the d of adas, and of adri are both changed to m by the present sutra; (2) the first is not changed, but only the second; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) अमूमुयङ् (VII. 1. 70, VI. 1. 68, VIII. 2. 23 and 62), अमूमुयञ्चौ, अमूमुयञ्चः ॥ (2) Secondly, अदमुयङ्, अदमुयञ्चौ, अदमुयञ्चः ॥ (3) Lastly अद्रिर्यङ्, अद्रियञ्चौ, अद्रियञ्चः ॥ The above verse summarises this:
Verse:—Some ordain that m should come separately for both adas and adri, as there is double d (in see sutra VIII. 2. 80 and VII. 4. 90 S. 2644); others would have m only for the last portion which stands in proximity to the final, (i.e. for adri); while a third class would have m nowhere, because they explain असेः of the sutra by confining it to Tyadadi VII. 2. 102."
Note:—Thus उदङ् = विष्वक्. This form is thus evolved. अञ्च् + क्विन् = अञ्च् + ० = अञ्च् + नुम् (VII. 1. 70). Then there is elision of the final conjunct consonant, then the final dental is changed to guttural because of the क्विन् affix (VIII. 2. 62), i.e. च् is changed to क् and we have ‹?› which with ङि, gives the above form.
प्राङ्, प्रत्यङ्, उदङ् ॥ प्राची and प्रतीची (VI. 3. 95) have acute on the final irregularly (nipatana) in order to prevent the krit-accent, and when ई is changed into य् the following vowel becomes svarita (VIII. 2. 4).
Observe अश्वाव्री—अश्वमञ्चति, the अ of अञ्च् is elided by VI. 4. 138.
Why 'when an affix follows'? Observe प्राची ॥ The न् is totally elided by VI. 4. 24, feminine ङीप् being added by IV. 1. 6 Vart. The अ is elided by VI. 4. 138, and the final of प्र is lengthened by VI. 3. 138.
Why do we say of क्विन् and अनप्रत्यये? Observe अञ्चनम् ॥
Another reading of the sutra is अनवप्रत्यये (नावप्रत्यये) ॥ It would give the same result, the meaning then being when no affix follows. The word अनप्रत्यये or अनवप्रत्यये indicates by implication that in other places where simply a verb is mentioned, it means a word-form beginning with that verb which ends with some affix. For had अनप्रत्यये not been used, then the rule would have applied not only when anch followed, but when anchana ending in ल्युट् also followed. The maxim धातुग्रहणे तदादिविधिरिष्यते is illustrated in अयस्कृते and अयस्कारः; for VIII. 3. 46 teaches that visarga is changed into स् when कृ follows. There the कृ denotes not only the root कृ but a word derived from कृ, therefore which begins with कृ such as कारः and कृतः ॥ Therefore the rule applies to forms like अयस्कृत् which is followed merely by the verb कृ; as well as to forms like अयस्कृतः ॥
Now we take up the declension of उदञ्च्. It is declined in the Nominative as उदङ् (S), उदञ्चौ (Dual) उदञ्चः (Pl).
Before the weak cases the following rule applies:—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
420. Long ई is substituted for the अ of that (अञ्च्) where the nasal is elided after the word उद्, when the stem is Bha.
As उदीचः, उदीचा, उदग्भ्याम् ॥
Now we take up the declension of सम्यञ्च् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
421. समि is substituted for सम्, before this अञ्च् when no visible affix follows.
Thus सम्यक् सम्यङ्, सम्यञ्चौ, सम्यञ्चः ॥
Ac : Pl: समीचः Instr: Sing समीचा ॥
Now we take up the declension of सह + अञ्च् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies —
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
422. सधि is the substitute of सह, before अञ्च् followed by no visible affix.
Thus सध्यङ्, सध्यञ्चौ, सध्यञ्चः; and सध्रीचः, सध्रीचा ॥ See VI. 3. 138 for long vowel.
Now, we take up the declension of तिर्यञ्च् ॥ In its declension, the following rule applies :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
423. तिर्य is substituted for तिरस् before this अञ्च् when no visible affix follows, provided that the अ of अञ्च् is not elided.
Thus तिर्यङ्, तिर्यञ्चौ, तिर्यञ्चः ॥ Why do we say 'when there is no elision'? Observe तिरश्चा, तिरश्चे ॥ Here अ is elided by VI. 4. 138. The word अलोपे in the sutra is ambiguous. It may mean either (1) "where अ is elided" or (2) "where there is no elision." The latter meaning should be taken however.
Now, we take up the declension of प्र + अञ्च् when अञ्च् means 'to honor'. There are two roots (अञ्चु), both belong to the Bhvadi class, one meaning 'to honor' and the other 'to move'. The declension of 'अञ्चु' meaning 'to move' has already been exhibited above. But when it means 'to honor' its declension is governed by the following rule :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
424. The nasal of अञ्च् is not elided when the meaning is 'to honor'.
And as the nasal is not elided by VI. 4. 24. S. 415 there is no नुम् augment. Thus:
Singular Dual Plural
Nominative प्राङ् प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः
As न् is not elided, so there is no elision of अ also by VI. 4. 138. S. 416. Thus the weak forms are Ac : Pl : प्राञ्चः ॥ Inst : Sing and dual are प्राञ्चा, प्राङ्भ्याम् ॥ Loc. Plural is प्राङ्क्षु or प्राक्षु ॥
Similar is the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् when 'अञ्च्' means 'to honor'. Thus Acc: Plu : is प्रत्यञ्चः and not प्रतीचः ॥ Similarly the Acc : Plural of अदमुयञ्च् is अदमुयञ्चः and not अदमुयीचः ॥
Similarly the Acc plural of उदञ्च् is उदञ्चः and not उदीचः ॥
Now, we take up the declension of ‹?›. This word, as already mentioned in sûtra III. 2. 59 S. 373 is irregularly formed by adding the affix ‹?› to the root meaning "to curve or make crooked" or "to be or become small". Thus it is declined :—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›

Instr. Dual is ‹?› &c.

Now, we take up the declension of पयोमुच्. In Nom. Sing. the ‹?› is changed to the guttural, by Sutra VIII. 2. 30 S. 378. It is declined as follows:—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. पयोमुक् or पयोमुग् पयोमुचौ पयोमुचः &c.

Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› in the sense of ‹?›. It is thus formed :— सु + ‹?› meaning 'that which cuts well'. The ‹?› being vocalised by VI. 1. 16 S. ‹?›, it becomes सु + वृ + श्च. By VIII. 2. 36 S. 294, the श् is changed to ष्. By VIII. 2. 29 S. 380, the initial ‹?› is elided. Thus we get सु + वृट् and finally to ड् by VIII. 2. 39 S. 84 and VIII. 4. 56 S. 206. Thus its declension is as follows:—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. सुवृट् or सुवृड् ‹?› ‹?›

The Loc. Pl. is सुवृत्सु or सुवृट्सु.

*Note:—This would be true in the view that the original root was व्रश्च्, with a dental त् which becomes ट् by ष्टुना ष्टुः VIII. 4. 40 S. 111. This ष्टुत्व substitution is asiddha for VIII. 2. 29.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्.

Now, we take up the declension of महत्. This word is formed by the Unadi affix (Unadi sutra II. 84) which means that the words ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?› are irregularly formed with the affix ‹?› with the force of the present tense and are operated upon as if they were followed by a ‹?› affix. Since महत् is to be treated as if it was formed by the ‹?› affix, therefore, the rule VII. 1. 70 S. 361 would cause the insertion of नुम् and the sutra VI. 4. 10 S. 317 would cause the lengthening of आ. Thus.

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. महान् महान्तौ महान्तः
Voc. हे महन् " "
Acc. महान्तम् " महतः
Instr. महता महद्भ्याम् महद्भिः
&c. &c. &c.

-:0:-

Now we take up the declension of धीमत्. It is formed with the affix मतुप्.

-----

In its declension, the following rule applies :—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
425. In the Nominative Singular (with the exception of the Vocative Singular) the penultimate vowel is lengthened in a stem ending in अतु, and अस् when the consonant (अस्) does not belong to a root.

The नुम् (न्) is added to the above by VII. 1. 70, after the elongation has taken place, for if added before elongation, the vowel no longer being penultimate, will not be lengthened at all. This is because of the force of this sûtra, which though precedent in the order of enunciation in Panini's Ashtadhyayi, and therefore ought to have been superseded by the subsequent and nitya sutra (VII. 1. 70 S. 361) ordaining नुम्, yet is not so. Thus its declension is

Nominative
Singular धीमान्
Dual धीमन्तौ
Plural धीमन्तः

Vocative
हे धीमन्

Before the weak case terminations, it is declined like महत्.

Note:—अस् :— as सुपयाः, सुयशाः, सुश्रोताः ॥ Why do we say 'not belonging to a dhātu'? Observe पिण्डग्रसः where स् belongs to the root ग्रस् (पिण्डं ग्रसते), so also चर्मवः (चर्म वस्ते) ॥ The अस् having no significance as an affix &c. is also included here, on the strength of the maxim "whenever अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by I. 1. 72, something that ends with these, there they represent these combination of letters, both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning". (अनिन्नस्मन्ग्रहणेष्वर्थवताऽप्यनर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति) ॥ The word अतु in the sûtra indicates whatever ends in अतु whether when first enunciated (उपदेश), such as वतु, क्तवतु &c. or which assumes the form अतु in grammatical inflection, such as डवतु, which in upadesa ends in अतु, but becomes अतु in प्रयोग or application. In Vocative singular we have हे गोमन्, हे सुपयः, this rule not applying there.

Even in the case of Denominative roots, the lengthening will take place. The prohibition of अधातु in this sûtra applies to original roots and not to derivative roots from nouns. Thus — "He wishes to have cows." The affix क्यच् is added to गोमत् in forming the derivative root by III. 1. 8. or III. 1. 10. with the force of "wishing" or "behaving." The root is गोमत्य. It is a derivative root, and so it does not fall within the prohibition of this sûtra. Now गोमत्य् + क्विप् = गोमत् (अ is dropped by VI. 4. 48, and य् by VI. 4. 50). "One wishing to have cows." Here ends with अत् (which was part of the original affix मतुप् added to गो) and here we will have lengthening as well as नुम् ॥

The नुम् will be added for the following reason:—
In the sûtra उगिदचां VII. 1. 70. S. 361 the root अञ्चु is taken for the sake of niyama or restriction, that is, the operations dependent upon ugit, when applied to roots, will apply to the root añchu only, and not to any other root having an ugit. Thus in स्रंसु and ध्वंसु there is no ugit operation. Therefore, we could have easily inferred that no other root except अञ्चु would take नुम् under that sutra. The specific mention of अधातुः in that sutra would have become redundant. But the fact, that Panini has mentioned अधातुः in that sutra, indicates that by धातु is meant the original root and not a derivative root.

Thus we have
Singular गोमान्
Dual गोमन्तौ
Plural गोमन्तः
"One who wishes to be possessed of cows."

Now we take up the declension of भवत् not derived from भू, but from भा meaning 'to shine'. (see Unâdi sutra I. 63) with the affix डवतु । Thus भा + डवतु = भवत् (the आ is elided by VI. 4. 143 and I. 4. 18 because the affix has an indicatory ड). It is declined as

Nominative
Singular भवान्
Dual भवन्तौ
Plural भवन्तः &c.

But when it is derived from the root भू with the affix शतृ, as it does not then end with the affix अतु, the penultimate is not lengthened. Thus in this case, the Nominative Singular is भवन्.

Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› formed from the root ‹?› with the affix ‹?›. The root is reduplicated. The reduplication is technically
called अभ्यस्त as defined below, and because it is अभ्यस्त, it does not get the augment नुम्, for the sûtra after next prohibits it.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 426. Where reduplication is treated in the Sixth Book of Panini's Ashtadhyayi, the two which are directed, both are collectively called Abhyasta.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
427. The Participial-affix शतुँ (अत्-अन्त), does not take the augment नुम् after a reduplicate stem.

Thus, ददत्, ददतः ॥

Note:—This is an exception to VII. 1. 70, and applies of course to sarvanâmasthâna or strong cases. The नुम् is to be read into this sûtra, from VII. 1. 70; for the negation of this sûtra cannot apply to ई taught in the preceding sûtra for ई is never ordained after śatṛ: therefore, though several other operations intervene, yet नुम् is to be read here.

Now, we take up the declension of जक्षत्, formed with the affix शतुँ added to the root जक्ष्. Its declension is governed by the following Sûtra:—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
428. So also the six roots, with jakshi itself as the seventh, are called abhyasta.

Note:—The word abhyasta is understood here. The verb jakshi and the six verbs that follow it in the Dhatupatha, in all seven verbs, get this designation. These are जक्ष, जागृ, दरिद्रा, चकास्, शास्, दीधी and वेवी ॥ (Panini has overlooked वेवी and mentions only the first six.) By getting the designation of Abhyasta, the participles derived from these verbs are declined like ददत् ॥

Thus जक्षत् or जक्षद् (N. S.); जक्षतौ (N. Dual); जक्षतः (N. Plural).
Similar is the declension of जागृत्, दरिद्रत्, शासत्, चकासत् ॥ दीधी and वेवी though exhibited in the Dhâtupâṭha as दीधीङ् and वेवीङ् with an indicatory ङ् and therefore, they ought to be आत्मनेपदी by I. 3. 12. S. 2158, yet they are परस्मैपदी because of the Vaidic irregularities. These form their Nominative Singulars as दीध्यत् and वेव्यत्.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्. Now we take up the declension of गुप् which is formed from the चुरादि root गुप् with the affix क्विप्. The आम् of the चुरादि class is optionally elided by III. 1. 31. S. 2305. It is declined as:

Nom: गुप् or गुब्, गुपौ, गुपः; Instr: Dual गुब्भ्याम् &c.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in श.

Now, we take up the declension of तादृश् formed according to the following Sûtra:—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
429. The affix कञ् as well as क्विन् comes after the verb दृश् ‘to see’ when it is in combination with त्यद् &c. which precede it, and when it does not signify perception.

Note:—The force of 'च' is that the क्विन् also comes under similar circumstances. त्यद् &c. are pronouns, for a list of which see I. 1. 27. Thus तादृश् ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
430. आ is substituted for the final of the Pronouns (I. 1. 27) before these words दृग्, दृश् and the affix वतु ॥

Thus तद् + दृश् + क्विन् (by the present sûtra) = ता + दृक् (the श् is changed to क् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377). This is not perceived (असिद्ध) for the purposes of change by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. Thus we have तादृश् = तादृष् = तादृड् (VIII. 2. 39. S. 84) = तादृग् (VIII. 2. 62. S. 377) = तादृक् (optionally by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206).

Thus Nom. forms are तादृक् or तादृग्, तादृशौ, तादृशः. According to the opinion of Kaiyaṭa and Haradatta &c. the form would be तादृख् but never तादृग्, in the alternative when it is not तादृक्. Because they apply the कुत्व rule as an apavâda to व्रश्च rule and by कुत्व they get ख in the place of श (See Padamanjarî p. 953): and ख will never become ग् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84; because ख obtained by क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः VIII. 2. 62. is asiddha or not perceived by the जश्त्व rule VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. Or we may say that ख is not asiddha for Panini himself has changed ख् into ग् in the word दिगादि (See IV. 4. 54. S. 1429).

Now, we take up the declension of विशू. This is formed by the affix क्विप् added to the root विश् 'to enter'. The श् is changed to ष् by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. which is changed to ड् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. and optionally to ट् by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206.

Thus it is declined as:
Sing.	Dual.	Pl.
Nom.	विट् or विड्	विशौ	विशः
Acc.	विशम्	विशौ	विशः
&c.	&c.

Now, we take up the declension of नश्. In its declension, the following rule applies.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
431. The final of नश् at the end of a word is optionally changed to a guttural.

Note:—Here the root नश् has taken क्विन् in denoting 'condition or state'; by considering it as belonging to संपदादि class.

Thus there are four forms in the Nominative Singular namely:—नक् or नग् or नट् or नड् ॥

Nominative Dual and Plural are नशौ, नशः.

Instr: Dual is नग्भ्याम् and नड्भ्याम् &c.

Now, we take up the declension of घृतस्पृश्. Its declension is governed by the following rule:—
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 432. √ tumpa, To injure, to hurt. Pre. तुम्पति । Per. तुतुम्प । I Fut. तुम्पिता । II Fut. तुम्पिष्यति । Imperative तुम्पतु । Imperf. अतुम्पत् । Pot. तुम्पेत् । Bene. तुप्यात् । Aorist अतुम्पीत् । Condi. अतुम्पिष्यत् । Caus. तुम्पयति । Aorist अतितुम्पत् । Desi. तुतुम्पिषति । Inten. तोतुम्प्यते । यङ्-लुक् तोतोम्पीति or तोतर्म्पीति ।
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
Declension of Masculines ending in स्.

We take up the declension of पिपठिस् (meaning 'wishing to read'). It is derived from the root पिपठिस् with the affix क्विप्. The अ of स is elided by VI. 4. 48. S. 2308. The स् was changed to ष् by VIII. 3. 39. S. 153. But this is not perceived by the Sūtra requiring the substitution of स् into रुँ for it is precedent in the order of enumeration in Pāṇini's Ashṭādhyāyī, (VIII. 2. 66. S. 162). Thus पिपठिष् + सु = पिपठिष् + ० (by VI. 1. 68. S. 252). Now पिपठिष् gets the name of a pada though the affix सु is elided after it (I. 1. 62. S. 262). Therefore the ष् which is really स् becomes रुँ. Thus पिपठिष् becomes पिपठिर्. At this stage applies the following Sūtra.

433. A penultimate ik is lengthened, when the final r or v of a root can stand at the end of a Pada.
Thus पिपठिर् becomes पिपठीः.
The Nominative Dual and Plural are पिपठिषौ and पिपठिषः.
The Inst: Dual is पिपठीर्भ्याम्.
In forming the Locative Plural the sūtra VIII. 3. 36 S. 151 as well as the following comes into operation.
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 434. √ trumpa, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुम्पति । Per. तुत्रुम्प । I Fut. त्रुम्पिता । Bene. त्रुप्यात् । Aorist अत्रुम्पीत् । Caus. त्रुम्पयति । Aorist अतित्रुम्पत् । Desi. तुत्रुम्पिषति । Inten. तोत्रुप्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 435. √ tupha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. तोफति । Per. तुतोफ । I Fut. तोफिता । Imperative तोफतु । Imperf. अतोफत् । Pot. तोफेत् । Bene. तुफ्यात् । Aorist अतोफीत् । Caus. तोफयति । Desi. तुतुफिषति । Inten. तोतोफ्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
436. असुङ् ( अस् ) is substituted for the final of पुंस् when the sarvanāmasthāna affixes are to be added.
The उ in असुङ् is for the sake of pronunciation and not to indicate that नुम् should be added under VII. 1. 70 S. 361 because the नुम् will be added in strong cases by the very fact that the word पुंस् is formed from पा ( to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178 ) and as the affix डुम्सुन् is an उगित् affix, it will produce its effect under VII. 1. 70 by causing नुम् pari passu as it does in causing ङीप् to be added to in the feminine, in forming बहुपुंसी, by the sūtra उगितश्च ( IV. 1. 6 S. 455 ) Thus it is declined as follows:--
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. पुमान् पुमांसौ पुमांसः
Voc. हे पुमन्
Acc. पुंसः
Inst. पुंसा पुंभ्याम् पुम्भिः
Loc. पुंसु
Kāśikā:--
The word is derived from पा (to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178), the न् being changed to anusvāra. So when ‹?› of पुंस् is replaced by असुङ् we get the form पुमस्, the उ of असुङ् indicates that नुम् should be added in the strong cases after म ( VII. 1. 70 ), so we have पुमान्, पुमांसौ, पुमांसः ॥
This substitution must take place in its incipient stage before the affixes are added, (अङ्गस्य) : otherwise the accent will be wrong. The compounds have acute on the final, (VI. 1. 223 ), therefore, परमपुंस् has acute on पुं, and in the Nominative Singular the acute will remain on पु, but it is intended that it should be on मा, thus परमपुमान् ॥ The simple word पुंस्, of course, has accent on पु.
Now, we take up the declension of उशनस्. By VII. 1. 94. S. 276, अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Nom. Sing: Thus Nom. forms are उशना, उशनसौ, उशनसः ॥
In forming the Voc: Sing: the following Vārtika will apply :—
Vārt :— अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Voc. S. also, as an alternative, the final न् not being elided (See VIII. 2. 8). Otherwise we have three forms in the Vocative Singular: as हे उशनन्, हे उशन, and हे उशनः ॥
The Instr Dual is उशनोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of अनेहस् meaning 'time'.
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. अनेहा अनेहसौ अनेहसः
Voc. हे अनेहः
Instr. अनेहोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of वेधस् meaning 'the Creator'.
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. वेधाः वेधसौ वेधसः
Voc. हे वेधः
Instr. वेधोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of सुवस् meaning 'one who wears well'. Here वस् belongs to a root and so in the Nom: S. its vowel is not lengthened because of the prohibition of अधातु in VI. 4. 14. S. 425.
Hence its Nom forms are सुवः, सुवसौ, सुवसः ॥
Now we take up the declension of पिण्डग्रस् and पिण्डग्रसस् ॥ The verbs ग्रस् and ग्रसु mean 'to swallow'; the Nominative singular forms of these are पिण्डग्रः and पिण्डग्रसः meaning 'a lump eater'.
Now, we take up the declension of अदस्. In its declension the following rules apply :--
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 437. √ trupha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुफति । त्र्रोफति । Per. तुत्रोफ । I Fut. त्र्रोफिता । Aorist अच्रोफीत् । Caus. त्र्रोफयति । Desi. तुत्रुफिषति । Inten. तोत्रूफ्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 438. √ trumpha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुम्फति । Per. तुत्रुम्फ । I Fut. त्रुम्फिता । Aorist अत्रुम्फीत् । Caus. त्रुम्फयति । Desi. तुत्रुम्फिषति । Inten. तोत्रुम्फ्यते । Note:—The nasal in the above roots is not elided in the Perfect because the affixes are here added to a root ending in a conjunct consonant, and they are not kit (I. 2. 5. S. 2242). Therefore we have the forms तुतुम्प &c. For the rule of elision of nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415) applies to kit or ṅit affixes. In the Benedictive, the affixes being kit by III. 4. 104 S. 2216, there is elision of the nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415). Thus तुप्यात् from तुम्प ॥ When preceded by प्र the root तुम्प adds a sibilant in its beginning, because of the following vārtika to be found in the Pāraskarādi class (VI. 1. 157 S. 1071):— Gaṇa Vārtika:—The augment सुट् is added to the root तुम्प when preceded by the preposition प्र provided the agent of the notion is a cow. Thus प्रस्तुम्पति गौः ॥ (प्रस्तुम्पति इति प्रवृत्ते सुट् Padamañjarī.) Since the root is exhibited in the above Vārtika as प्रस्तुम्पति with शितप्, therefore when this root is conjugated in यङ्-लुक् the sibilant is not added (VII. 2. 10 S. 2646). Thus प्रतोतुम्पीति ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text:
439 to 453 पर्प &c. to चर्व &c.
The first parpa ends with the first labial p प; the next two raph and raphi end with the second labial ph फ; the remaining eleven all end in the third labial b ब । Except the second and third raph and raphi, all these roots have a penultimate r.

439. Parpa, to go. Pre. पर्पति । Per. पपर्प । I Fut. पर्पिता । Aorist अपर्पीत् । Caus. पर्पयति । Desi. पिपर्पिषति । Inten. पापर्प्यते । Nouns : पर्पः, पर्पिकः ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

items.sanskrit_text: 440. Rapha, to go. Pre. रफति । Per. रराफ । I Fut. रफिता । Caus. रफयति । Desi. रिरफिषति । Inten. रारफ्यते ॥
items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu
