To clear up this point, we state that the rule of elision (शेषे लोपः) is bahiranga, because its efficient cause lies outside in the affix अम्, while the अतो गुणे rule is antaranga, because the occasion for its application or the efficient cause is within the very form त्व + अद्. Therefore अतो गुणे will apply first, we get त्वद् + अम्. Then शेषे लोपः produces its effect i. e. अद् is elided, and we get त्व् + अम् ॥ As there is no अ in त्व्, it would not require टाप् ॥ Thus we get त्वम् in the feminine also.

So also परमत्वम्, परमाहम्, अतित्वम् and अत्यहम्. In forming the N. Dual, the following rules apply.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 386. युव is substituted for युष्म् and आव for अस्म्, when the bases themselves denote duality.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
387. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before the ending of the Nom. Du. in the spoken language.

As युवाम्, आवाम् ॥ It would have been better had the Sûtra been enunciated as “औङि” only. Why in the “spoken language”? Observe युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे in the Veda, so also आवाम् ॥

Why 'upto म'? Observe युवकाम्, आवकाम् ॥ The क (V. 3. 71. S. 2026), is not replaced. Similarly VII. 2. 97. S. 389 teaches that त्व and म replace 'yushmad' and 'asmad' in the singular; by the sûtra VII. 2. 91. S. 383 'yushm' and 'asm' are only replaced. Thus त्वया, मया the अद् portion remains for which य is substituted by VII. 2. 89. S. 392. Had the whole been replaced, then the अ of त्व and म would have been replaced by य (VII. 2. 89. S. 392), and given us undesired forms like त्या and म्या ॥ Similarly the forms युवकाभ्याम् and आवकाभ्याम् would not have been evolved.

In forming the N. Pl. the following rule applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 388. ✓ Shtepri. Pre. स्तेपते । Per. तिष्टेपे । I Fut. स्तेपिता । II Fut. स्तेपिष्यते । Imperative स्तेपताम् । Imper. अस्तेपत । Pote. स्तेपेत । Bene. स्तेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अस्तेपिष्ट । Condi. अस्तेपिष्यत । Caus. स्तेपयते । Desi. तिस्तेपिषते । Inten. तेष्टेप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
389. ✓ Tepri, to tremble, shake. By the force of च it means also to sprinkle.

Pre. तेपते । Per. तितेपे । I Fut. तेपिता । II Fut. तेपिष्यते । Impera. तेपताम् । Imper. अतेपत । Pote. तेपेत । Bene. तेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अतेपिष्ट । Condi. अतेपिष्यत । Caus. तेपयते । Desi. तितेपिषते । Inten. तेतेप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 390. ✓ Glepri, to be poor. Pre. ग्लेपते । Per. जिग्लेपे । I Fut. ग्लेपिता । Bene. ग्लेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अग्वेपिष्ट । Caus. ग्लेपयते । Desi. जिग्लेपिषते । Inten. जेग्लेप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
391. ✓ Tuvepri, to shake, to tremble.

Pre. वेपते । Per. विवेपे । I Fut. वेपिता । Aorist अवेपिष्ट । Caus. वेपयति (The Causative is Parasmaipadi because the verb has the sense of motion I. 3. 87. S. 2753). Desi. विवेपिषते । Inten. वेवेप्यते ॥

Nouns:— वेपथुः 'trembling.' (III. 3. 89 S. 3267 because of टु) । विप्रुथः (Uṇ. II. 52), वेपनः (with ल्युट् III. 2. 148 S. 3128).
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
392. ✓ Kepri, 393. ✓ Gepri, 394. ✓ Glepri, to tremble, and to move. By the force of च, both the senses of trembling and moving are taken. This is done by yoga-vibhāga according to Swāmī. According to Maitreya, the sense of trembling would be understood by context even without च. His meaning is that these roots could well have been read with चेप, but they are not done, because traditionally they are read separately. The ✓ Glep is repeated because it has a different meaning here.

Pre. केपते । Per. चिकेपे । I Fut. केपिता । Bene. केपिषीष्ट । Aorist अकेपिष्ट । Caus. केपयति (I. 3. 87 S. 2753). Desi. चिकेपिषते । Inten. चेकेप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
393. आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending, beginning with a consonant, when it is not a substitute.
The substitute case-endings are given in VII. 1. 27-33. S. 399 &c.
Thus युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्, युष्माभिः, अस्माभिः ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
394. In the Dative Singular तुभ्य is substituted for युष्म and मह्य for अस्म ॥
The affix अम् is substituted for ङे by VII. 1. 28. S. 382 the तू is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385.
Thus तुभ्यम्, मह्यम्, परमतुभ्यम्, परममह्यम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतिमह्यम्, युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
395. ✓ Mepri, to move. According to Maitreya it means to serve, to attend upon. The reading of Kshirasvami is mepri, repri, lepriygatau. But Maitreya reads it as meprillepti sevane; repri plavagatau. Some texts have धेपु and धेषु ॥

Pre. मेपते । Per. मिमेपे । I Fut. मेपिता । Bene. मेपिषीष्ट । Aorist अमेपिष्ट । Caus. मेपयति । Desi. मिमेपिषते । Inten. मेमेप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 396. ✓ Repri, to go. According to Maitreya it means 'to leap, jump, swim'. Pre. रेपते । Per. रिरेपे । I Fut. repitā । Bene. repishīshṭa । Aorist अरेपिष्ट । Caus. रेपयति । Desi. रिरेपिषते । Inten. रेरेप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
397. अत् is substituted for the Ablative भ्यस् after युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥
As युष्मत्, अस्मत् ॥
The द् is elided by VII. 2. 90. S. 385 before the case-ending भ्यस् and युष्म + अत् = युष्मत् by VI. 1. 97. S. 191.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
398. ✓ Dhepri. Pre. धेपते । Per. दिधेपे । I Fut. धेपिता । Aorist अधेपिष्ट । Caus. धेपयति । Desi. दिधेपिषते । Inten. देधेप्यते ॥

त्रपूष ३९९ लज्जायाम् । त्रपते ॥

The Present is त्रपते । In forming the Perfect, the following rule applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
399. ✓ Trapash, to be ashamed, abashed.

Pre. त्रपते । Per. त्रेपे । I Fut. त्रपिता or त्रप्ता । II Fut. त्रपिष्यते or त्रप्स्यते । Imperative त्रपताम् । Imper. अत्रपत । Pote. त्रपेत । Bene. त्रपिषीष्ट or त्रप्सीष्ट । Aorist अत्रपिष्ट or अत्रप्त । Condi. अत्रपिष्यत or अत्रप्स्यत । Caus. त्रपयति । Aorist अतित्रपत् । Being a Ghaṭādi root also (see 859) it is mit (VI. 4. 92. S. 2568) and hence the shortening in the Causative. Desi. तित्रपिषते or तित्रप्सते । Inten. तात्त्रप्यते । यङ्लुक् तात्त्रपीति or तात्त्रप्ति ॥ Past Part. Pass. त्रप्तः । Past Part. Act. त्रप्तवान् । Ger. त्रपित्वा or त्रप्त्वा । Infini. त्रपितुम् । त्रप्तुम् । Nouns:— त्रपिष्णुः (III. 2. 136 S. 3116). त्रपु 'Tin.'
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
400. ✓ Kapi, to move; to tremble.

Pre. कम्पते । Per. चकम्पे । I Fut. कम्पिता । Caus. कम्पयति । (I. 3. 87 S. 2753). Desi. चिकम्पिषते । Inten. चाकम्प्यते । Nouns:— काम्पुः (III. 2. 157 S. 3147). कम्पनः (III. 2. 148 or 149 S. 3128 or 3129). कपिः (Uṇ. IV. 144) वृषाकपिः "Vishnu or Rudra." कपिञ्जलः (See however Uṇ. I. 55).
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
401. Upto VIII. 3. 54, inclusive, should be always supplied in every subsequent sutra, the phrase "of a word," or "to the whole of a word."

Note:—This is an adhikara sutra, and extends up to VIII. 3. 55, in order of enunciation of Pânini's Ashtâdhyâyî.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 402. ✓ Labi, to sound. Pre. लम्बते । Per. ललम्बे । I Fut. लम्बिता । Aorist अलम्बिष्ट । Caus. लम्बयते । Desi. लिलम्बिषते । Inten. लालम्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 403. ✓ Abi, to sound: Pre. अम्बते । Per. आनम्बे । I Fut. अम्बिता । Caus. अम्बयति । Aorist आन्बिवत् । Desi. अम्बिविषते । Nouns:— त्र्यम्बकः "The father of the three worlds," अम्बरीषः । अम्बा 'mother.'
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
404. For the Genitive, Dative and Accusative Dual of yushmad and asmad are substituted वाम् and नौ respectively, when a word precedes it and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta.

All the three sûtras पदस्य, पदात् and अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ are applicable here.

Note:—These two वाम् and नौ come in the Dual only, because other substitutes have been taught for the Singular and Plural in the two subsequent sûtras.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 405. For (the Genitive, Dative, and Accusative) plural of yushmad and asmad are substituted वस् and नस् respectively, (when a word precedes, and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse, and these substitutes are anudâtta).\n\nThis Sûtra debars the substitutes वाम् and नौ taught in the previous Sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 406. For the Genitive and Dative Singular (of yushmad and asmad are substituted) ते and मे respectively, (when a word precedes and if it does not stand at the beginning of a foot of a verse and these are anudâtta).
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
407. ✓ Kshībrī, to be drunk or intoxicated.

Pre. क्षीबते । Per. चिक्षीबे । I Fut. क्षीबिता । Caus. क्षीबयति । Aorist अचिक्षीबत् । Desi. चिक्षीबिषते । Noun:— क्षीबः ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
408. ✓ Śībhri, to boast.

Pre. शीभते । Per. शिशीभे । I Fut. शीभिता । Caus. शीभयते । Aorist अशिशीभत् । Desi. शिशीभिषते । Inten. शेशीभ्यते । यङ्लुक् शेशीब्धि । (त् changed to ध् by VIII. 2. 40. S. 2280, and भ् changed to ब् by VIII. 4. 53. S. 52). Noun:— शीभरः ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
409. The above substitutions do not take place also in connection with verbs having the sense of "seeing" when physical seeing is not denoted, but "knowing" is meant.\n\nNote:—The word पश्यार्थाः is equivalent to दर्शनार्थाः, and दर्शन means 'knowledge', i. e. verbs denoting 'to know'. आलोचन means perception obtained through sight i. e. physical 'seeing' opposed to metaphorical "seeing" or "knowing". The substitutions of त्वा and मा &c. for युष्मद् and अस्मद् do not take place when these pronouns are employed in connection with verbs denoting 'seeing' (metaphorically) but not 'looking' (physically).
Thus तथा त्वां समीक्षते भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति ॥ Why do we say when not meaning 'to look'? Observe भक्तस्त्वा पश्यति चक्षुषा ॥
Ishti :—With regard to verbs of "Seeing" the rule should apply even where the connection is not direct : as,
भक्तस्तव रूपं ध्यायति ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
410. When the pronoun follows after a Nominative which itself is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions may take place optionally even in anvâdesa.
Thus भक्तस्त्वमप्यहं तेन हरिस्त्वां त्रायते स माम् ॥ Here the alternative forms त्वा and मा are admissible.
We have already said that युष्मद् and अस्मद् substitutions do not take place when they are in the beginning of a pada. To this, however, there is an exception, when the first word is a Vocative, technically called आमन्त्रित which is defined in the next sutra, then also though युष्मद् and अस्मद् may not really be in the beginning of a pada, yet the substitutions will not take place by the sûtra after next.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 411. The word ending with the first case-affix, in the sense of addressing, is called Amantrita or Vocative.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
412. A preceding Vocative is considered as non-existent, (for the purposes of the accent of the following word, and the enclitic forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्) ||
Thus अग्ने ! तव ॥ देव ! अस्मान्पाहि ॥ अग्ने ! नय ॥ अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! ॥ Here तव and अस्मान् cannot get the shorter form, though they are not at the beginning of a hemistich, because they are preceded by the आमन्त्रित words अग्ने and देव ||
Similarly in अग्ने नय the verb नय does not become accentless as it would otherwise have become by VIII. 1. 28. S. 3935.
In अग्ने ! इन्द्र ! वरुण ! the rule VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654 does not apply.
Note:—Such a Vocative is treated as if not at all existing, it is simply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not existed. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-existent? They are (1) the absence of the accent-less-ness of the subsequent Vocative which the first, taken as a पद, would have caused under VIII. 1. 19. S. 3654. As देवदत्त ! यज्ञदत्त ! Here the first Vocative देवदत्त does not cause the second Vocative to lose its accent, but it remains first acute by VI. 1. 198. S. 3653. (2) The accent-less-ness of the verb required by VIII. 1. 28 S. 3935 is prevented : as, देवदत्त पचसि ॥ (3) The substitution of the shorter forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्, required by VIII. 1. 20-28 S. 404 &c. is prevented, as देवदत्त तव (not ते) ग्रामः स्वम्, देवदत्त मम (not मे) ग्रामः । (4) The application of VIII. 1. 37. S. 3944 takes place, in spite of the intervention of the Vocative between the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything from the immediateness (व्यवधान) of the Particle from the verb : as, अहो देवदत्त पचसि ॥ (5) For the purposes of VIII. 1. 47, S. 3954 though a Vocative may precede, the latter is still considered as non-existent and VIII. 1. 47 applies, as देवदत्त जातु पचसि । (6) So also in the case of VIII. 1. 49, S. 3956 as अहो देवदत्त पचसि, अहो देवदत्त जल्पसि, no option is allowed here by VIII. 1. 50. S. 3957.
In 'सर्वदा रक्ष देव नः' although the word देव is non-existent, yet taking रक्ष as a preceding word, नः is used.
In इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि the first Vocative गङ्गे is considered as non-existent with regard to मे, and, therefore, यमुने is considered as following immediately after the pada मे and thus यमुने becomes anudâtta, not because of गङ्गे, but because of मे. In other words, the intervention of the Vocatives does not stop the action of मे. This nighâta or accentlessness is heard in Pada-Pâtha only, i. e. when the words are read separately, and not in Sanhitâ-reading. In Sanhitâ there will be eka-sruti of I. 2. 39 S. 3668.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
413. A preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as if non-existent, for the purposes of the subsequent Vocative, which stands in apposition with the former.
Thus हरे दयालो नः पाहि "O Hari ! O Merciful! protect us." अग्ने तेजस्विन् "O Agni! O powerful!" Here दयालो is all anudâtta by VIII. 1. 19 S. 3654, because it is preceded by a word, though that word is Vocative.
Note:—Why do we say सामान्यवचनम् 'which is a generic word'? The rule will not apply when the Vocatives are synonyms. Thus ‹?› All these Vocatives are synonyms of Saraswati, and hence all retain their accent of the Vocative (VI. 1. 198). According to Padamanjari the reading given in Taittirîya Br. is :— ‹?› सामान्यवचनम् means 'a generic term'. When the first is a generic term, and the second is a specific term, (विशेषवचन) qualifying the first, and both are in the singular number, there the present rule will apply.
This sutra prevents the operation of the last sûtra in the particular case when the two Vocatives are in apposition, and the second qualifies the first. Thus अग्ने गृहपते, माणवक जटिलकाध्यापक ॥ The first vocative being considered as existing, the second vocative loses its accent.
Why do we say 'the vocative subsequent'? Observe देवदत्त पचसि here the verb does not lose its accent. Why do we say 'standing in apposition or सामानाधिकरण्ये'?
Observe देवदत्त पण्डित यज्ञदत्त, here the word पण्डित qualifies यज्ञदत्त, and is not in apposition with देवदत्त, and hence it retains its accent.
Then applies Sûtra VIII. 1. 74. S. 3655 which for the sake of convenience we repeat here.

४१३ (क) । विभाषितं विशेषवचने । ८ । १ । ७४ ॥
अत्र भाष्यम् । बहुवचनमिति वक्ष्यामीति । बहुवचनान्तं विशेष्यं समानाधिकरणे आमन्त्रिते विशेषणे परे अविद्यमानवद्वा । यूयं प्रभवः । देवाः शरण्याः । युष्मान् भजे वो भजे इति वा । इहान्वादेशेऽपि वैकल्पिका आदेशाः । सुपात् । सुपाद । सुपादौ । सुपादः । सुपादम् । सुपादौ ।

413. A. When the preceding Vocative is in the plural number, it is optionally considered as non-existent, if the subsequent Vocative, in apposition with it, is a specific term.
Here the author of the Mahabhashya states :— "The word bahuvachanam should be added to the sûtra to complete the sense." That is the sûtra should run as विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् ॥ We have therefore translated the sûtra with this emendation of Patanjali.
Thus यूयं प्रभवः, देवाः शरण्याः । युष्मान् भजे or वो भजे ॥ Here even in anvâdesa there is optional substitution of वः for युष्मान् ॥
Now, we take up the declension of सुपाद्. In the strong, i. e. in the first five cases it is declined as :—
Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom : सुपात् or सुपाद, सुपादौ सुपादः
Ac. सुपादम्, सुपादौ.
In the formation of the Acc. Pl. and the rest, the following rule applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
414. For पाद् is substituted पद् when the former is Bha.
Note:—The substitute replaces the whole form पाद् and not only the final, on the maxim निर्दिश्यमानस्यादेशा भवन्ति "substitutes take the place of that which is actually enunciated in a rule."
Thus the Acc. Pl. is सुपदः ॥
Instr: Sing and Dual are सुपदा, सुपाद्भ्याम् &c.
Now we take up the declension of अग्निमथ् meaning 'kindling fire'. It is declined as:
Nom. Sing. अग्निमत् or अग्निमद् Dual अग्निमथौ Pl. अग्निमथः
Instr: Dual is अग्निमद्भ्याम् &c.
Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in थ.
Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in च्.
Now we take up the declension of प्राञ्च्.
According to Sūtra III. 2. 59. S. 373, the affix क्विन् is employed after the verb अञ्च् to make it a Prātipadika, before the case terminations.
Thus having got the noun प्राञ्च्, in its declension, the following rules apply.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
415. In a root-stem ending in a consonant preceded by न्,—this न not being added to the root owing to its having an indicatory इ (VII. 1. 58)—the न is elided when an affix having an indicatory क or ङ् follows.
By Sūtra VII. 1. 70. S. 361, the stem अञ्च् gets the augment नुम् in the strong cases.
Then by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54, the last consonant is dropped. By VIII. 2. 62. S. 377, which says that 'a stem formed with the affix क्विन् substitutes at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant' we get the N. S. as प्राङ् thus:—
प्राञ्च् + सु = प्राच् (VI. 4. 24 S. 415) + सु = प्रा + न् (VII. 1. 70. S. 361) + च् + सु = प्रान् च् + ० (सु is elided by VI. 1. 68 S. 252) = प्रान् च् = प्रान् (च् being elided by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54) = प्राङ् (न् turned to ङ् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377).
The N. Dual &c. are formed by changing the न into anuswāra, and then the anuswāra into ञ् by VIII. 4. 58. S. 124.
Thus प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः Acc. प्राञ्चम्, प्राञ्चौ.
In forming the Acc. Pl. &c. the following rules apply.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
416. The अ of अच् (when अञ्च् loses its nasal,) is elided at the end of a Bha stem.
The lengthening of the first member takes place by VI. 3. 138: S. 417.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
417. The final vowel of the preceding member is lengthened before अच, when it assumes the form च, having lost its nasal and the vowel अ ॥
Thus Acc: Pl is प्राचः; Instr: Sing or Dual are प्राचा, प्राग्भ्याम् &c.
Now we take up the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् ॥ In strong cases, it is declined as प्रत्यङ्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, प्रत्यञ्चः ॥ प्रत्यञ्चम्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, in weak cases, अ is elided by VI. 4. 138 S. 416, and though this lopa is a bahiraṅga process, while the yaṇ or semivowel Sandhi is an antaraṅga process, yet this lopa is not considered asiddha for the purposes of this sandhi. This proceeds on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. See under Sūtra I. 3. 11 S. 46. Thus Acc: Pl: is प्रतीचः, Instr: Sing is प्रतीचा ॥ &c. प्रति + अञ्च् + शस् = प्रति + च् + अस् ॥ Here two sūtras simultaneously appear for application, viz. इको यणचि and अचः ॥ Now इको यणचि is antaraṅga, because the efficient cause अ of अञ्च् is inside that of शस्; and the efficient cause शस् by which अ of अञ्च् would be elided is outside; therefore yaṇ ādeśa should take place first, thus प्रति + अ + शस् = प्रत्य् + अच् + शस् ॥ After this अ should be elided as प्रत्य् + च् + अस् ॥ This however gives us no form, and so relying on the maxim अकृतव्यूहाः &c. the antaraṅga yaṇ substitution is set aside. Now, we take up the declension of अञ्च् as compounded with the pronoun अदस् meaning अमुम् अञ्चति ॥ Thus we have अदस् + अञ्च् + क्विन् । Here applies the following sūtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
418. In the room of the last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of a Pronoun and of the words विष्वक् and देव, is substituted अद्रि, when अञ्च् has no visible affix following it.
Thus अदस् + अञ्च् = अदद्रि + अञ्च् = अदद्य् + अञ्च्. At this stage, applies the following sūtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
419. When the pronoun अदस् does not end in स्, then there is substituted उ or ऊ for the vowel after द्, and म् for द् ॥
The short u in the sūtra is a samāhāra dvandva compound including both the short u and long ऊ. By the rule of antartama I. 1. 50 S. 39, the short vowel and the consonant following it will be replaced by the short u; and the long vowel with the consonant following it will be replaced by the long ū.
Thus अदद्य् + अञ्च् = अमुमुद्य् + अञ्च् : the first द् and अ are changed to म् and उ, and the second द् and य् are also changed to म् and उ; so the declension is:—
Nom. Sing. अमुमुयङ् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुयञ्चः
Acc. Sing. अमुमुयञ्चम् Dual अमुमुयञ्चौ Pl. अमुमुचः
Ins. Sing. अमुमुचा Dual अमुमुयग्भ्याम् &c. &c.
The mutva being considered as asiddha, there is no sandhi in
in æg, for the Sandhi rule is contained in the Sixth Book of Panini, while this g substitute is ordained in the Tripadi portion of Ashtadhyayi. Hence the Sutra VIII. 2. 1. S. 12 applies.
Some, by applying the following maxim, get the form
Paribhasha "When a modification is ordained with regard to something which is not final, the operation takes place on that only which is in proximity to the final." The second class apply this maxim and make g change only for which stands in proximity to the final.
There is a third form, which is obtained by explaining the असेः in the Sutra as मः सेर्यस्य सोऽयमसिः, तत्र सकारस्य मकारः क्रियते ॥ "The word असेः in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and means that in which अस् is substituted for ‹?›" The sutra is thus confined to the form derived by changing the द् into म् by VII. 2. 102. and not to any other.
Thus there are three views with regard to the application of the present sutra:—
(1) the d of adas, and of adri are both changed to m by the present sutra; (2) the first is not changed, but only the second; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) अमूमुयङ् (VII. 1. 70, VI. 1. 68, VIII. 2. 23 and 62), अमूमुयञ्चौ, अमूमुयञ्चः ॥ (2) Secondly, अदमुयङ्, अदमुयञ्चौ, अदमुयञ्चः ॥ (3) Lastly अद्रिर्यङ्, अद्रियञ्चौ, अद्रियञ्चः ॥ The above verse summarises this:
Verse:—Some ordain that m should come separately for both adas and adri, as there is double d (in see sutra VIII. 2. 80 and VII. 4. 90 S. 2644); others would have m only for the last portion which stands in proximity to the final, (i.e. for adri); while a third class would have m nowhere, because they explain असेः of the sutra by confining it to Tyadadi VII. 2. 102."
Note:—Thus उदङ् = विष्वक्. This form is thus evolved. अञ्च् + क्विन् = अञ्च् + ० = अञ्च् + नुम् (VII. 1. 70). Then there is elision of the final conjunct consonant, then the final dental is changed to guttural because of the क्विन् affix (VIII. 2. 62), i.e. च् is changed to क् and we have ‹?› which with ङि, gives the above form.
प्राङ्, प्रत्यङ्, उदङ् ॥ प्राची and प्रतीची (VI. 3. 95) have acute on the final irregularly (nipatana) in order to prevent the krit-accent, and when ई is changed into य् the following vowel becomes svarita (VIII. 2. 4).
Observe अश्वाव्री—अश्वमञ्चति, the अ of अञ्च् is elided by VI. 4. 138.
Why 'when an affix follows'? Observe प्राची ॥ The न् is totally elided by VI. 4. 24, feminine ङीप् being added by IV. 1. 6 Vart. The अ is elided by VI. 4. 138, and the final of प्र is lengthened by VI. 3. 138.
Why do we say of क्विन् and अनप्रत्यये? Observe अञ्चनम् ॥
Another reading of the sutra is अनवप्रत्यये (नावप्रत्यये) ॥ It would give the same result, the meaning then being when no affix follows. The word अनप्रत्यये or अनवप्रत्यये indicates by implication that in other places where simply a verb is mentioned, it means a word-form beginning with that verb which ends with some affix. For had अनप्रत्यये not been used, then the rule would have applied not only when anch followed, but when anchana ending in ल्युट् also followed. The maxim धातुग्रहणे तदादिविधिरिष्यते is illustrated in अयस्कृते and अयस्कारः; for VIII. 3. 46 teaches that visarga is changed into स् when कृ follows. There the कृ denotes not only the root कृ but a word derived from कृ, therefore which begins with कृ such as कारः and कृतः ॥ Therefore the rule applies to forms like अयस्कृत् which is followed merely by the verb कृ; as well as to forms like अयस्कृतः ॥
Now we take up the declension of उदञ्च्. It is declined in the Nominative as उदङ् (S), उदञ्चौ (Dual) उदञ्चः (Pl).
Before the weak cases the following rule applies:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
420. Long ई is substituted for the अ of that (अञ्च्) where the nasal is elided after the word उद्, when the stem is Bha.
As उदीचः, उदीचा, उदग्भ्याम् ॥
Now we take up the declension of सम्यञ्च् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
421. समि is substituted for सम्, before this अञ्च् when no visible affix follows.
Thus सम्यक् सम्यङ्, सम्यञ्चौ, सम्यञ्चः ॥
Ac : Pl: समीचः Instr: Sing समीचा ॥
Now we take up the declension of सह + अञ्च् ॥ In its declension the following rule applies —
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
422. सधि is the substitute of सह, before अञ्च् followed by no visible affix.
Thus सध्यङ्, सध्यञ्चौ, सध्यञ्चः; and सध्रीचः, सध्रीचा ॥ See VI. 3. 138 for long vowel.
Now, we take up the declension of तिर्यञ्च् ॥ In its declension, the following rule applies :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
423. तिर्य is substituted for तिरस् before this अञ्च् when no visible affix follows, provided that the अ of अञ्च् is not elided.
Thus तिर्यङ्, तिर्यञ्चौ, तिर्यञ्चः ॥ Why do we say 'when there is no elision'? Observe तिरश्चा, तिरश्चे ॥ Here अ is elided by VI. 4. 138. The word अलोपे in the sutra is ambiguous. It may mean either (1) "where अ is elided" or (2) "where there is no elision." The latter meaning should be taken however.
Now, we take up the declension of प्र + अञ्च् when अञ्च् means 'to honor'. There are two roots (अञ्चु), both belong to the Bhvadi class, one meaning 'to honor' and the other 'to move'. The declension of 'अञ्चु' meaning 'to move' has already been exhibited above. But when it means 'to honor' its declension is governed by the following rule :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
424. The nasal of अञ्च् is not elided when the meaning is 'to honor'.
And as the nasal is not elided by VI. 4. 24. S. 415 there is no नुम् augment. Thus:
Singular Dual Plural
Nominative प्राङ् प्राञ्चौ प्राञ्चः
As न् is not elided, so there is no elision of अ also by VI. 4. 138. S. 416. Thus the weak forms are Ac : Pl : प्राञ्चः ॥ Inst : Sing and dual are प्राञ्चा, प्राङ्भ्याम् ॥ Loc. Plural is प्राङ्क्षु or प्राक्षु ॥
Similar is the declension of प्रत्यञ्च् when 'अञ्च्' means 'to honor'. Thus Acc: Plu : is प्रत्यञ्चः and not प्रतीचः ॥ Similarly the Acc : Plural of अदमुयञ्च् is अदमुयञ्चः and not अदमुयीचः ॥
Similarly the Acc plural of उदञ्च् is उदञ्चः and not उदीचः ॥
Now, we take up the declension of ‹?›. This word, as already mentioned in sûtra III. 2. 59 S. 373 is irregularly formed by adding the affix ‹?› to the root meaning "to curve or make crooked" or "to be or become small". Thus it is declined :—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. ‹?› ‹?› ‹?›

Instr. Dual is ‹?› &c.

Now, we take up the declension of पयोमुच्. In Nom. Sing. the ‹?› is changed to the guttural, by Sutra VIII. 2. 30 S. 378. It is declined as follows:—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. पयोमुक् or पयोमुग् पयोमुचौ पयोमुचः &c.

Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› in the sense of ‹?›. It is thus formed :— सु + ‹?› meaning 'that which cuts well'. The ‹?› being vocalised by VI. 1. 16 S. ‹?›, it becomes सु + वृ + श्च. By VIII. 2. 36 S. 294, the श् is changed to ष्. By VIII. 2. 29 S. 380, the initial ‹?› is elided. Thus we get सु + वृट् and finally to ड् by VIII. 2. 39 S. 84 and VIII. 4. 56 S. 206. Thus its declension is as follows:—

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. सुवृट् or सुवृड् ‹?› ‹?›

The Loc. Pl. is सुवृत्सु or सुवृट्सु.

*Note:—This would be true in the view that the original root was व्रश्च्, with a dental त् which becomes ट् by ष्टुना ष्टुः VIII. 4. 40 S. 111. This ष्टुत्व substitution is asiddha for VIII. 2. 29.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्.

Now, we take up the declension of महत्. This word is formed by the Unadi affix (Unadi sutra II. 84) which means that the words ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› and ‹?› are irregularly formed with the affix ‹?› with the force of the present tense and are operated upon as if they were followed by a ‹?› affix. Since महत् is to be treated as if it was formed by the ‹?› affix, therefore, the rule VII. 1. 70 S. 361 would cause the insertion of नुम् and the sutra VI. 4. 10 S. 317 would cause the lengthening of आ. Thus.

Sing. Dual. Pl.
Nom. महान् महान्तौ महान्तः
Voc. हे महन् " "
Acc. महान्तम् " महतः
Instr. महता महद्भ्याम् महद्भिः
&c. &c. &c.

-:0:-

Now we take up the declension of धीमत्. It is formed with the affix मतुप्.

-----

In its declension, the following rule applies :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
425. In the Nominative Singular (with the exception of the Vocative Singular) the penultimate vowel is lengthened in a stem ending in अतु, and अस् when the consonant (अस्) does not belong to a root.

The नुम् (न्) is added to the above by VII. 1. 70, after the elongation has taken place, for if added before elongation, the vowel no longer being penultimate, will not be lengthened at all. This is because of the force of this sûtra, which though precedent in the order of enunciation in Panini's Ashtadhyayi, and therefore ought to have been superseded by the subsequent and nitya sutra (VII. 1. 70 S. 361) ordaining नुम्, yet is not so. Thus its declension is

Nominative
Singular धीमान्
Dual धीमन्तौ
Plural धीमन्तः

Vocative
हे धीमन्

Before the weak case terminations, it is declined like महत्.

Note:—अस् :— as सुपयाः, सुयशाः, सुश्रोताः ॥ Why do we say 'not belonging to a dhātu'? Observe पिण्डग्रसः where स् belongs to the root ग्रस् (पिण्डं ग्रसते), so also चर्मवः (चर्म वस्ते) ॥ The अस् having no significance as an affix &c. is also included here, on the strength of the maxim "whenever अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by I. 1. 72, something that ends with these, there they represent these combination of letters, both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning". (अनिन्नस्मन्ग्रहणेष्वर्थवताऽप्यनर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति) ॥ The word अतु in the sûtra indicates whatever ends in अतु whether when first enunciated (उपदेश), such as वतु, क्तवतु &c. or which assumes the form अतु in grammatical inflection, such as डवतु, which in upadesa ends in अतु, but becomes अतु in प्रयोग or application. In Vocative singular we have हे गोमन्, हे सुपयः, this rule not applying there.

Even in the case of Denominative roots, the lengthening will take place. The prohibition of अधातु in this sûtra applies to original roots and not to derivative roots from nouns. Thus — "He wishes to have cows." The affix क्यच् is added to गोमत् in forming the derivative root by III. 1. 8. or III. 1. 10. with the force of "wishing" or "behaving." The root is गोमत्य. It is a derivative root, and so it does not fall within the prohibition of this sûtra. Now गोमत्य् + क्विप् = गोमत् (अ is dropped by VI. 4. 48, and य् by VI. 4. 50). "One wishing to have cows." Here ends with अत् (which was part of the original affix मतुप् added to गो) and here we will have lengthening as well as नुम् ॥

The नुम् will be added for the following reason:—
In the sûtra उगिदचां VII. 1. 70. S. 361 the root अञ्चु is taken for the sake of niyama or restriction, that is, the operations dependent upon ugit, when applied to roots, will apply to the root añchu only, and not to any other root having an ugit. Thus in स्रंसु and ध्वंसु there is no ugit operation. Therefore, we could have easily inferred that no other root except अञ्चु would take नुम् under that sutra. The specific mention of अधातुः in that sutra would have become redundant. But the fact, that Panini has mentioned अधातुः in that sutra, indicates that by धातु is meant the original root and not a derivative root.

Thus we have
Singular गोमान्
Dual गोमन्तौ
Plural गोमन्तः
"One who wishes to be possessed of cows."

Now we take up the declension of भवत् not derived from भू, but from भा meaning 'to shine'. (see Unâdi sutra I. 63) with the affix डवतु । Thus भा + डवतु = भवत् (the आ is elided by VI. 4. 143 and I. 4. 18 because the affix has an indicatory ड). It is declined as

Nominative
Singular भवान्
Dual भवन्तौ
Plural भवन्तः &c.

But when it is derived from the root भू with the affix शतृ, as it does not then end with the affix अतु, the penultimate is not lengthened. Thus in this case, the Nominative Singular is भवन्.

Now, we take up the declension of ‹?› formed from the root ‹?› with the affix ‹?›. The root is reduplicated. The reduplication is technically
called अभ्यस्त as defined below, and because it is अभ्यस्त, it does not get the augment नुम्, for the sûtra after next prohibits it.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 426. Where reduplication is treated in the Sixth Book of Panini's Ashtadhyayi, the two which are directed, both are collectively called Abhyasta.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
427. The Participial-affix शतुँ (अत्-अन्त), does not take the augment नुम् after a reduplicate stem.

Thus, ददत्, ददतः ॥

Note:—This is an exception to VII. 1. 70, and applies of course to sarvanâmasthâna or strong cases. The नुम् is to be read into this sûtra, from VII. 1. 70; for the negation of this sûtra cannot apply to ई taught in the preceding sûtra for ई is never ordained after śatṛ: therefore, though several other operations intervene, yet नुम् is to be read here.

Now, we take up the declension of जक्षत्, formed with the affix शतुँ added to the root जक्ष्. Its declension is governed by the following Sûtra:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
428. So also the six roots, with jakshi itself as the seventh, are called abhyasta.

Note:—The word abhyasta is understood here. The verb jakshi and the six verbs that follow it in the Dhatupatha, in all seven verbs, get this designation. These are जक्ष, जागृ, दरिद्रा, चकास्, शास्, दीधी and वेवी ॥ (Panini has overlooked वेवी and mentions only the first six.) By getting the designation of Abhyasta, the participles derived from these verbs are declined like ददत् ॥

Thus जक्षत् or जक्षद् (N. S.); जक्षतौ (N. Dual); जक्षतः (N. Plural).
Similar is the declension of जागृत्, दरिद्रत्, शासत्, चकासत् ॥ दीधी and वेवी though exhibited in the Dhâtupâṭha as दीधीङ् and वेवीङ् with an indicatory ङ् and therefore, they ought to be आत्मनेपदी by I. 3. 12. S. 2158, yet they are परस्मैपदी because of the Vaidic irregularities. These form their Nominative Singulars as दीध्यत् and वेव्यत्.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in त्.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्. Now we take up the declension of गुप् which is formed from the चुरादि root गुप् with the affix क्विप्. The आम् of the चुरादि class is optionally elided by III. 1. 31. S. 2305. It is declined as:

Nom: गुप् or गुब्, गुपौ, गुपः; Instr: Dual गुब्भ्याम् &c.

Here ends the declension of Masculine Nouns ending in प्.

Declension of Masculine Nouns ending in श.

Now, we take up the declension of तादृश् formed according to the following Sûtra:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
429. The affix कञ् as well as क्विन् comes after the verb दृश् ‘to see’ when it is in combination with त्यद् &c. which precede it, and when it does not signify perception.

Note:—The force of 'च' is that the क्विन् also comes under similar circumstances. त्यद् &c. are pronouns, for a list of which see I. 1. 27. Thus तादृश् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
430. आ is substituted for the final of the Pronouns (I. 1. 27) before these words दृग्, दृश् and the affix वतु ॥

Thus तद् + दृश् + क्विन् (by the present sûtra) = ता + दृक् (the श् is changed to क् by VIII. 2. 62. S. 377). This is not perceived (असिद्ध) for the purposes of change by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. Thus we have तादृश् = तादृष् = तादृड् (VIII. 2. 39. S. 84) = तादृग् (VIII. 2. 62. S. 377) = तादृक् (optionally by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206).

Thus Nom. forms are तादृक् or तादृग्, तादृशौ, तादृशः. According to the opinion of Kaiyaṭa and Haradatta &c. the form would be तादृख् but never तादृग्, in the alternative when it is not तादृक्. Because they apply the कुत्व rule as an apavâda to व्रश्च rule and by कुत्व they get ख in the place of श (See Padamanjarî p. 953): and ख will never become ग् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84; because ख obtained by क्विन्प्रत्ययस्य कुः VIII. 2. 62. is asiddha or not perceived by the जश्त्व rule VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. Or we may say that ख is not asiddha for Panini himself has changed ख् into ग् in the word दिगादि (See IV. 4. 54. S. 1429).

Now, we take up the declension of विशू. This is formed by the affix क्विप् added to the root विश् 'to enter'. The श् is changed to ष् by VIII. 2. 36, S. 294. which is changed to ड् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84. and optionally to ट् by VIII. 4. 56. S. 206.

Thus it is declined as:
Sing.	Dual.	Pl.
Nom.	विट् or विड्	विशौ	विशः
Acc.	विशम्	विशौ	विशः
&c.	&c.

Now, we take up the declension of नश्. In its declension, the following rule applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
431. The final of नश् at the end of a word is optionally changed to a guttural.

Note:—Here the root नश् has taken क्विन् in denoting 'condition or state'; by considering it as belonging to संपदादि class.

Thus there are four forms in the Nominative Singular namely:—नक् or नग् or नट् or नड् ॥

Nominative Dual and Plural are नशौ, नशः.

Instr: Dual is नग्भ्याम् and नड्भ्याम् &c.

Now, we take up the declension of घृतस्पृश्. Its declension is governed by the following rule:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 432. √ tumpa, To injure, to hurt. Pre. तुम्पति । Per. तुतुम्प । I Fut. तुम्पिता । II Fut. तुम्पिष्यति । Imperative तुम्पतु । Imperf. अतुम्पत् । Pot. तुम्पेत् । Bene. तुप्यात् । Aorist अतुम्पीत् । Condi. अतुम्पिष्यत् । Caus. तुम्पयति । Aorist अतितुम्पत् । Desi. तुतुम्पिषति । Inten. तोतुम्प्यते । यङ्-लुक् तोतोम्पीति or तोतर्म्पीति ।
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
Declension of Masculines ending in स्.

We take up the declension of पिपठिस् (meaning 'wishing to read'). It is derived from the root पिपठिस् with the affix क्विप्. The अ of स is elided by VI. 4. 48. S. 2308. The स् was changed to ष् by VIII. 3. 39. S. 153. But this is not perceived by the Sūtra requiring the substitution of स् into रुँ for it is precedent in the order of enumeration in Pāṇini's Ashṭādhyāyī, (VIII. 2. 66. S. 162). Thus पिपठिष् + सु = पिपठिष् + ० (by VI. 1. 68. S. 252). Now पिपठिष् gets the name of a pada though the affix सु is elided after it (I. 1. 62. S. 262). Therefore the ष् which is really स् becomes रुँ. Thus पिपठिष् becomes पिपठिर्. At this stage applies the following Sūtra.

433. A penultimate ik is lengthened, when the final r or v of a root can stand at the end of a Pada.
Thus पिपठिर् becomes पिपठीः.
The Nominative Dual and Plural are पिपठिषौ and पिपठिषः.
The Inst: Dual is पिपठीर्भ्याम्.
In forming the Locative Plural the sūtra VIII. 3. 36 S. 151 as well as the following comes into operation.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 434. √ trumpa, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुम्पति । Per. तुत्रुम्प । I Fut. त्रुम्पिता । Bene. त्रुप्यात् । Aorist अत्रुम्पीत् । Caus. त्रुम्पयति । Aorist अतित्रुम्पत् । Desi. तुत्रुम्पिषति । Inten. तोत्रुप्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 435. √ tupha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. तोफति । Per. तुतोफ । I Fut. तोफिता । Imperative तोफतु । Imperf. अतोफत् । Pot. तोफेत् । Bene. तुफ्यात् । Aorist अतोफीत् । Caus. तोफयति । Desi. तुतुफिषति । Inten. तोतोफ्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
436. असुङ् ( अस् ) is substituted for the final of पुंस् when the sarvanāmasthāna affixes are to be added.
The उ in असुङ् is for the sake of pronunciation and not to indicate that नुम् should be added under VII. 1. 70 S. 361 because the नुम् will be added in strong cases by the very fact that the word पुंस् is formed from पा ( to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178 ) and as the affix डुम्सुन् is an उगित् affix, it will produce its effect under VII. 1. 70 by causing नुम् pari passu as it does in causing ङीप् to be added to in the feminine, in forming बहुपुंसी, by the sūtra उगितश्च ( IV. 1. 6 S. 455 ) Thus it is declined as follows:--
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. पुमान् पुमांसौ पुमांसः
Voc. हे पुमन्
Acc. पुंसः
Inst. पुंसा पुंभ्याम् पुम्भिः
Loc. पुंसु
Kāśikā:--
The word is derived from पा (to protect ) + डुम्सुन् ( Un. IV. 178), the न् being changed to anusvāra. So when ‹?› of पुंस् is replaced by असुङ् we get the form पुमस्, the उ of असुङ् indicates that नुम् should be added in the strong cases after म ( VII. 1. 70 ), so we have पुमान्, पुमांसौ, पुमांसः ॥
This substitution must take place in its incipient stage before the affixes are added, (अङ्गस्य) : otherwise the accent will be wrong. The compounds have acute on the final, (VI. 1. 223 ), therefore, परमपुंस् has acute on पुं, and in the Nominative Singular the acute will remain on पु, but it is intended that it should be on मा, thus परमपुमान् ॥ The simple word पुंस्, of course, has accent on पु.
Now, we take up the declension of उशनस्. By VII. 1. 94. S. 276, अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Nom. Sing: Thus Nom. forms are उशना, उशनसौ, उशनसः ॥
In forming the Voc: Sing: the following Vārtika will apply :—
Vārt :— अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Voc. S. also, as an alternative, the final न् not being elided (See VIII. 2. 8). Otherwise we have three forms in the Vocative Singular: as हे उशनन्, हे उशन, and हे उशनः ॥
The Instr Dual is उशनोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of अनेहस् meaning 'time'.
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. अनेहा अनेहसौ अनेहसः
Voc. हे अनेहः
Instr. अनेहोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of वेधस् meaning 'the Creator'.
Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. वेधाः वेधसौ वेधसः
Voc. हे वेधः
Instr. वेधोभ्याम् &c.
Now, we take up the declension of सुवस् meaning 'one who wears well'. Here वस् belongs to a root and so in the Nom: S. its vowel is not lengthened because of the prohibition of अधातु in VI. 4. 14. S. 425.
Hence its Nom forms are सुवः, सुवसौ, सुवसः ॥
Now we take up the declension of पिण्डग्रस् and पिण्डग्रसस् ॥ The verbs ग्रस् and ग्रसु mean 'to swallow'; the Nominative singular forms of these are पिण्डग्रः and पिण्डग्रसः meaning 'a lump eater'.
Now, we take up the declension of अदस्. In its declension the following rules apply :--
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 437. √ trupha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुफति । त्र्रोफति । Per. तुत्रोफ । I Fut. त्र्रोफिता । Aorist अच्रोफीत् । Caus. त्र्रोफयति । Desi. तुत्रुफिषति । Inten. तोत्रूफ्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 438. √ trumpha, To injure, to hurt. Pre. त्रुम्फति । Per. तुत्रुम्फ । I Fut. त्रुम्फिता । Aorist अत्रुम्फीत् । Caus. त्रुम्फयति । Desi. तुत्रुम्फिषति । Inten. तोत्रुम्फ्यते । Note:—The nasal in the above roots is not elided in the Perfect because the affixes are here added to a root ending in a conjunct consonant, and they are not kit (I. 2. 5. S. 2242). Therefore we have the forms तुतुम्प &c. For the rule of elision of nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415) applies to kit or ṅit affixes. In the Benedictive, the affixes being kit by III. 4. 104 S. 2216, there is elision of the nasal (VI. 4. 24. S. 415). Thus तुप्यात् from तुम्प ॥ When preceded by प्र the root तुम्प adds a sibilant in its beginning, because of the following vārtika to be found in the Pāraskarādi class (VI. 1. 157 S. 1071):— Gaṇa Vārtika:—The augment सुट् is added to the root तुम्प when preceded by the preposition प्र provided the agent of the notion is a cow. Thus प्रस्तुम्पति गौः ॥ (प्रस्तुम्पति इति प्रवृत्ते सुट् Padamañjarī.) Since the root is exhibited in the above Vārtika as प्रस्तुम्पति with शितप्, therefore when this root is conjugated in यङ्-लुक् the sibilant is not added (VII. 2. 10 S. 2646). Thus प्रतोतुम्पीति ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
439 to 453 पर्प &c. to चर्व &c.
The first parpa ends with the first labial p प; the next two raph and raphi end with the second labial ph फ; the remaining eleven all end in the third labial b ब । Except the second and third raph and raphi, all these roots have a penultimate r.

439. Parpa, to go. Pre. पर्पति । Per. पपर्प । I Fut. पर्पिता । Aorist अपर्पीत् । Caus. पर्पयति । Desi. पिपर्पिषति । Inten. पापर्प्यते । Nouns : पर्पः, पर्पिकः ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 440. Rapha, to go. Pre. रफति । Per. रराफ । I Fut. रफिता । Caus. रफयति । Desi. रिरफिषति । Inten. रारफ्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 441. Raphi, to go. Pre. रंफति । Per. ररंफ । I Fut. रंफिता । Bene. रंफ्यात् । Aorist अरंफीत् । Caus. रंफयति । Desi. रिरंफिषति । Inten. रारंफ्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
442. त् is substituted for the final of the stem अप् before a case-ending beginning with भ् ॥

Thus we have अद्भिः and in the Dat. and Abl. Plural अद्भ्यः in the Gen. and Loc. Plural अपाम् and अप्सु respectively.

Now we come to the declension of words ending in श् such as दिश् ॥ Thus in the Nominative S. we have दिक् or दिग् by III. 2. 59. S. 373 and VIII. 2. 62 S. 377 ; in the Nominative Dual दिशौ and Plural दिशः ; in the Inst. Dual दिग्भ्याम् and Loc. Plural दिक्षु ॥

Now we take up the declension of the word दृश् ॥ By the rule III. 2. 60. S. 429 दृश् takes the affix क्विन् when in combination with the pronoun त्यद् &c. But we infer from this that the root दृश् will take the affix क्विन् even when it is not in combination also. Thus in the Nominative S. we have दृक् or दृग् Nominative D. दृशौ, Plural दृशः ॥

So also त्विष् : Its Nominative S. is त्विट् or त्विड् by VIII. 2. 39. S. 84., in the Nominative D. ‹?›, Nominative Plural ‹?›, Inst. D. त्विड्भ्याम् and the Loc. Plural त्वित्सु or त्विट्त्सु with the optional augment ‹?› by VIII. 3. 29. S. 131.

The word सजुष्, "a friend". By the rule VIII. 2. 66. S. 162, रु is substituted for its final and by VIII. 2. 23. S. 54. there is the elision of उ ; then by applying the rules VIII. 2. 76. S. 433. and VIII. 3. 15. S. 76. we have ‹?› in the Nominative S. The Nominative D. ‹?› and Plural सजुषः ; similarly in the Inst. D. ‹?› and Loc. Plural सजुष्षु or सजूःषु, the change of ‹?› to ‹?› caused by VIII. 4. 41. S. 113 being not perceived by VIII. 2. 66. S. 162, causing र् ॥

In the same way the word आशिस् is declined. Thus we have आशीः, आशिषौ and आशिषः respectively ; the Nominative S., D. and Plural ‹?› and ‹?› ; In Inst. D. we have आशीर्भ्याम् and Plural आशीर्भिः ॥

Now we take up the declension of the pronoun अदस् :

Singular. Dual. Plural.
Nom. असौ (VII. 2. 102. S. 265) अमू (VIII. 2. 80. S. 419) अमूः
Acc. अमूम् अमू अमूः
Inst. अमुया अमूभ्याम् अमूभिः
Dat. अमुष्यै (VII. 3. 114. S. 291) अमूभ्याम् अमूभ्यः
Abl. अमुष्याः अमूभ्याम् अमूभ्यः
Gen. अमुष्याः अमुयोः अमूषाम् (VII. 1. 52)
Loc. अमुष्याम् अमुयोः अमूषु

Here end the declensions of Feminines ending in Consonants.

—:0:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 443. Parba, to go. Pre. पर्बति । Per. पपर्ब । I Fut. पर्बिता । Aorist अपर्बीत् । Caus. पर्बयति । Desi. पिपर्बिषति । Inten. पापर्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 444. Larba, to go. Pre. लर्बति । Per. ललर्ब । I Fut. लर्बिता । Aorist अलर्बीत् । Caus. लर्बयति । Desi. लिलर्बिषति । Inten. लालर्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 445. Barba, to go. Pre. बर्बति । Per. बबर्ब । I Fut. बर्बिता । Aorist अबर्बीत् । Caus. बर्बयति । Desi. बिबर्बिषति । Inten. बाबर्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 446. Marba, to go. Pre. मर्बति । Per. ममर्ब । I Fut. मर्बिता । Aorist अमर्बीत् । Caus. मर्बयति । Desi. मिमर्बिषति । Inten. मामर्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 447. Karba, to go. Pre. कर्बति । Per. चकर्ब । I Fut. कर्बिता । Aorist अकर्बीत् । Caus. कर्बयति । Desi. चिकर्बिषति । Inten. चाकर्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 448. And the words ending in taddhita or secondary affixes (IV. 1. 76. S 530) which are not declined in all the cases are also Indeclinables. An enumeration of these affixes should be made. They are the affixes beginning with ‹?› (V. 3. 7. S 1953) and ending with ‹?› (V. 3. 47. S 1993); by the affixes beginning with ‹?› (V. 4. 42. S. 2109) and ending with समासान्तः (V. 4. 68 S 676) by the affixes अम्, आम्, where meaning ‹?› by the affixes तसि and वति and न or नाञ् ॥ Hence पचतिकल्पम् and पचतिरूपम् are not indeclinables. Note:—Taddhitas or secondary affixes are certain affixes, by which nouns are derived from other nouns, such as, from ‹?› we have ‹?›, asarva-vibhaktis are those which do not take all vibhaktis but some only. Thus the adverb ‹?› is declined in the singular ablative only, and does not take the dual and plural terminations. Those derivative words which do not take all the case-terminations, but only some of them and which are formed by the addition of Taddhita affixes are indeclinables. As ‹?› 'thence,' ‹?› 'there'. Both these words are formed by taddhita affixes from the pronoun 'that,' the one is used in the ablative case only and the other in the locative. So also यतः, यत्र, ततः, तत्र, ‹?›, &c.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 449. Garba, to go. Pre. गर्बति । Per. जगर्ब । I Fut. गर्बिता । Aorist अगर्बीत् । Caus. गर्बयति । Desi. जिगर्बिषति । Inten. जागर्ब्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 450. The words, ending with ktvâ (III. 4. 18. S. 3316) tosun (III. 4. 16. S. 3443) and kasun (III. 4. 9. S. 3436) are Indeclinables. As कृत्वा 'having done,' उदेतोः 'having risen,' विसृपः 'having spread'.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 451. Sarba, to go. Pre. सर्बति । Per. ससर्ज । I Fut. सर्जिता । Aorist असर्बीत् । Caus. सर्बयति । Desi. सिसर्बिषति । Inten. सासर्य्यते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 452. Charba, to go. Pre. चर्बति । Per. चचर्ब । I Fut. चर्बिता । Aorist अचर्बीत् । Caus. चर्बयति । Desi. चिचर्बिषति । Inten. चाचर्ब्यते ।
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
453. When feminine nature is to be indicated, the affixes taught hereinafter must be employed.

Note:—This is an adhikāra sûtra pure and simple. The phrase 'when feminine nature is to be indicated,' must be read in all the following aphorisms upto IV. 1. 81 inclusive. The anuvṛitti of the word 'prātipadika' should be read into this sûtra, from the sûtra, IV. 1. 1. S. 182, not so, however the anuvṛitti of the words 'ङ्याप्' ; for we are now going to form words by the application of ङी and आप् affixes.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 454. Lubi, to torment, harass. Pre. लुम्बति । Per. लुलुम्ब । I Fut. लुम्बिता । Aorist अलुम्बीत् । Caus. लुम्बयति । Desi. लुलुम्बिषति । Inten. लोलुम्ब्यते । Noun ‹?› 'a gourd.'
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
455. And after what has an indicatory 'uk' the affix is employed, in denoting the feminine.
Note :—The ‹?› is a pratyāhāra meaning ‹?›, and wherever it is possible to make these letters indicatory, in whatever way it may be, that word-form is called ‹?›. That which ends with such a word is meant here. The prātipadika pure and simple not formed by an affix may be ‹?›, thus the pronoun ‹?› among the sarvanāmas : an affix may be ‹?› as the affixes ‹?› and ‹?› and therefore, the words formed by these affixes will be ‹?› ; similarly a letter may be ‹?›, as ‹?› meaning ‹?› in VI. 4. 127 § 364. ; ("is the substitute of the final of an inflective base ending in so")
Thus, ‹?› 'honored sir',—‹?› 'madam'. Applying the rule of tadantavidhi, we have ‹?› 'most exalted lady'. Similarly ‹?› (formed by adding ‹?› III. 2. 124 § 3100), forms the feminine ‹?›, the नुम् comes by VII. 1. 82 § 446. So also ‹?› and दीव्यन्ती ॥
Prohibition must be stated in the case of verbal roots having an indicatory 'uk.' Thus the roots ‹?› 'to fall down' ‹?› 'to fall down' have indicatory ‹?› and we get from these roots the prātipadikas like ‹?› and पर्णध्वत्, (III. 2. 76 § 2983) The उखासत् ब्राह्मणी, पर्णध्वत् ब्राह्मणी ॥ Here, the feminine is not formed by adding ‹?›.
The prātipadikas ending with the verb 'añchu', however, take the affix ङीप् ॥ As, प्राची, प्रतीची ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
456. Chubi, to kiss. Pre. चुम्बति । Per. चुचुम्ब । I Fut. चुम्बिता । Aorist अचुम्बीत् । Caus. चुम्बयति । Desi. चुचुम्बिषति । Inten. चोचुम्ब्यते ॥
(The three roots lumb, tumb, and chumb are found in the Churádi also).
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
457. Shribhu, 458. Shrimbhu, to injure. According to Maitreya the roots are सेभु and सिम्भु also. According to Tarangini, these are षिभु and षिम्भु also.
457. Shribhu, Pre. सर्भति । Per. ससर्भ । I Fut. सर्भिता । Caus. सर्भयति । Aorist अससर्भत् or असीसभत् । Desi. सिसर्भिषति or सिसर्भीषति. According to Tarangini there is never ‹?› । Inten. सरीसृभ्यते । यङ्-लुक्, सरीसृभीति or ‹?› Past Part. Pass. ‹?› । Ger. सर्भित्वा or ‹?› । Adjective ‹?›
457A. ‹?›, to injure. Pre. सेभति । Per. सिसेभ । I Fut. सेभिता or ‹?› । Caus. सेभयति । Desi. सिसेभिषति । Int. ‹?› ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
458. The affix डाप् is employed in the feminine, after a Nominal-stem ending with the word 'pâd', when the word denotes a verse of the Rig-veda.

This debars ‹?›. Thus द्विपदा ऋक् 'a Rik verse consisting of two quarter verses', similarly एकपदा ऋक् or त्रिपदा ऋक्, or चतुष्पदा ऋक् ॥

458 A. The feminine affixes are not employed after the stems called 'षट्' (I. 1. 24 S. 369), and स्वसृ &c.

This prohibits all feminine affixes that would otherwise have presented themselves. Thus, पञ्च 'the five Brāhmaṇī ladies'. So also सप्त, नव, दश &c. are feminine as well as masculine.

Note:—In पञ्च, though the न् of पञ्चन् is elided, yet the elided न् is asiddha for the purposes of षट् and the word पञ्चन् though not ending in न् will get the designation षट् by I. 1. 24 S. 369, because the elided न् is asiddha by VIII. 2. 2. S. 358 and so there is no affix after पञ्च by the present Sûtra.

संज्ञाविधिः—As पञ्च ब्राह्मण्याः, दश ब्राह्मण्याः ॥ The elision of न् being asiddha, the words पञ्च and दश are still called shash, though they no longer end in न्. Being called षट् (ष्णान्ता षट् I. 1. 24), they do not take affixes in the feminine (IV. 1. 10 S. 308).

According to the Vartikakâra, there is no necessity of using the word संज्ञा in the sutra VIII. 2. 2. S. 2330 (संज्ञाग्रहणानर्थक्यं च तन्निमित्तत्वाल्लोपस्य), because the elision of न् is caused by reason of its having such a designation (as षट्). Thus without its having the name of षट् there would be no elision of जस् and शस्, without such elision there is no pada sanjñâ of these words, and unless these words get Pada designation, there can be no elision of न् by VIII. 2. 7, S. 366. The shash designation, however, would not be retained by these words after taking plural affixes, when feminine affixes are to be added to them, but for this sûtra. The पञ्चन् and दशन् ending in न् would require ङीप् in the feminine, which is however prohibited, for when जस् and शस् are elided, the words end in अ and require टाप् for their feminine, which is also prohibited, because, by the present sutra the word still retains its designation of षट्.

How can this be the purpose of this sûtra? There are two views as to definitions (संज्ञा), the one is that a particular name is given to a thing once for all prior to any operations; and operations are performed afterwards upon it, as occasions arise. This view is embodied in the maxim यथाद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् ‘Sanjñās and Paribhāshās remain where they are taught.’ The other view is that the sanjñâ sûtra is to be read with every particular operative sûtra, and the sanjñâ given to the word afresh, with every new operation. In other words, the sanjñâ sûtra becomes identified with a vidhi sûtra, every time that a rule is to be applied. This is embodied in the maxim कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् ‘Sanjñās and Paribhāshās are attracted by or unite with the rules that enjoin particular operations’. In the first view, the sanjñâ will be good throughout, both for the purposes of eliding जस् and शस् and for prohibiting टाप्. Hence this sûtra is not necessary in that view. But in the other view, the sûtra is necessary. For if the view be taken that a sanjñâ is to be applied with regard to each operation, then that sanjñâ which had taken effect for the purposes of eliding जस् and शस्, will no longer hold good for the purposes of preventing the application of the feminine affix. Hence, the word संज्ञा is taken in this sûtra, to prevent the application of the second view.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
459. The affix ङीप् is not employed after a Nominal-stem ending in the syllable मन्.

Thus सीमन् is both masculine and feminine, declined as सीमा, सीमानौ &c.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
460. The affix ङीप् is not employed to denote the feminine, after a Bahuvrîhi compound ending in अन् ॥

This refers to those Bahuvrîhi compounds, in which the penultimate अ is not elided. Of the Bahuvrîhi compounds which lose their penultimate अ, it is optional to employ this affix or not; as it will be taught in IV. 1. 28. S. 462. Thus बहुयज्वन् is of both genders and is declined as masculine, N. s. बहुयज्वा, N. d. बहुयज्वानौ &c. The penultimate अ of बहुयज्वन् is not elided because of the prohibition of नलोप &c. (VI. 4. 137 S. 355).
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
461. The affix डाप् comes optionally after both viz. the Nominal-stem ending in मन्, and a Bahuvrîhi compound ending in अन्, as mentioned in the preceding two Sûtras.

Of the affix डाप्, the letter ड् indicates that the affix is to be added after the elision of the टि (I. 1. 64 S. 79) of the base. Thus दामन् + डाप् = दाम् + आ = दामा ॥ This being an optional rule we have 1. दामा, d. दामे or दामानौ, 2. दामाः or दामानः; similarly with सीमा, as, सीमा, सीमे or सीमानौ, सीमाः or सीमानः ॥

So also in Bahuvrîhi compounds ending in अन् ॥ As:—
बहुराजा, बहुराजे or बहुराजानौ, बहुराजाः or बहुराजानः ॥
बहुतक्षा, बहुतक्षे or बहुतक्षाणौ, बहुतक्षाः or बहुतक्षाणः ॥
बहुयज्वा, बहुयज्वे or बहुयज्वानौ, बहुयज्वाः or बहुयज्वानः ॥

Why do we say 'optionally'? So that the option may apply to sûtra IV. 1. 7 S. 456 also; i. e. when a prâtipadika ending in वन्, which can be regarded as ending in अन्, in a Bahuvrîhi compound, then the change of न into र् and the application of ङीप् are optional: we may apply the affix डाप् instead. As:—बहुधीवा or बहुधीवरी; बहुपीवा or बहुपीवरी ॥

By IV. 1. 5, S. 306 prâtipadikas ending in मन् would have taken the affix ङीप्, inasmuch as they end in न्; but the present sûtra prohibits that. Thus दामन् 'a string' is both neuter and feminine; and is declined as follows:—
1s. दामा, d. दामानी, pl. दामानि ॥ Similarly पामा, पामानी, पामानि ॥ The word दामन् is never masculine according to Amarakoṣa.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
462. The affix ङीप् optionally comes after that Bahuvrîhi compound, which ending in the syllable अन् loses its penultimate अ ॥

Thus बहुराजन् is a Bahuvrîhi compound ending in अन्; in applying ङीप्, it loses its penultimate अ by VI. 4. 134 S. 234, (अल्लोपोऽनः there is elision of penultimate अ of अन् when a bha affix follows). Thus बहुराज्ञी 'having many kings'. In the alternative, when ङीप् is not added, we may add the affix डाप् by IV. 1. 13. S. 461. Thus बहुराजा, बहुराजे, बहुराजाः ॥ Or we may apply the prohibition contained in IV. 1. 12 S. 460 and have बहुराजा, बहुराजानौ, बहुराजानः ॥

Note:—When the penultimate is not elided we cannot apply the affix ङीप् at all; in cases of such compounds there are only two forms of the feminine noun as सुपर्वा, सुपर्वे, सुपर्वाः or सुपर्वा, सुपर्वाणौ, सुपर्वाणः ॥ That is to say we apply IV. 1. 13 and 12 only; for in the case of सुपर्वन् &c rule VI. 4. 137 S. 355 prevents
the elision of the penultimate न्; संयोगासननन्तात्, there is not elision of the अ of छन् when it comes after a conjunct consonant ending in ‹?› or ‹?›) ॥

In forming the feminines of words ending in ‹?› the affix will be added after the change of ‹?› to ‹?› by the following Sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
463. इ is substituted for the अ which stands before the क् belonging to an affix, when the Feminine-ending आप् follows, provided that, it does not come after a case-affix (i. e. when such a word in क् does not stand at the end of a Bahuvrîhi).

That which stands in an affix is called प्रत्ययस्थ i. e. क् must be the part of the affix. The अ is changed into इ in the feminine in आप्. As सर्विका, कारिका, &c. Why do we say अतः? The क् must be preceded by short अ, therefore, not here नौका. Why do we say belonging to an affix? The क् must belong to the affix therefore, not in शका from शक्नोतीति शका ॥ The स्थ in प्रत्ययस्थ is for the sake of distinctness, there is no affix which is only क् ॥

Why do we say 'provided that the feminine affix does not come after a case affix'? Observe बहवः परिव्राजका अस्यां नगर्याम् = बहुपरिव्राजका नगरी ॥ Here आप् comes after the noun परिव्राजक which ends in a case-affix, and hence the अ of कारक is not changed to इ. The case affix is elided by II. 4. 71, S. 650 and it still exerts its influence by I. 1. 62 S. 272. Why do we say after असुपः? The rule applies to असुप्, therefore, not to नञ्. Why do we say "which stands before"? The इ is substituted for the अ which precedes (पूर्वस्य) क्, and not the अ which follows क्, as कटुका, मुटुका ॥ Why do we say short अ? Observe राका. Why do we say when आप् follows? क् should be followed by आप्, see कारकः. The substitution takes place when आप् follows, therefore, not in कारकम्. The word आप् qualifies क्.

Vårt :— मामक and नरक should be enumerated, for the क् of these is not part of the affix as मामिका, नरिका ॥ Here ‹?› is substituted for ‹?› before the affix अण् (IV. 3. 3. S. 1372), to which आप् is then added. The word मामक takes long ‹?› in the feminine only when it is a Name or in the Vedas (IV. 1. 30 S. 488) therefore though it ends in ‹?›, it does not take ङीप् (IV. 1. 15 S. 470) but टाप् (IV. 1. 4 S. 454), नरान् कायति = नरक formed with the affix क (III. 2. 3 S. 2915).

Vårt :— The rule applies to the words ending in त्यक् (IV. 2. 98) and त्यप्, (IV. 2. 104 S. 1324) in spite of the prohibition in VII. 3. 46. S. 2915. As दाक्षिणात्यिका, ऐहत्यिका ॥

Note :— The word in the sûtra is कात् the fifth case of क ending in अ ॥ If then this be the condition, that the affix must end in ka क and not in k क्, then the rule will not apply to एतिका ॥ Because here the augment is अकच् (अक् with क् : the final अ in अक is for euphony only, and not a portion of the affix, as we find in भिन्धकि, छिन्धकि, रुन्धकि ॥ The word कात् therefore, is construed to mean ending in the consonant क् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
464. The इ is not substituted for the अ of य and त, with the augment क, when the feminine आप् follows.

As यका, सका; यकाम्, तकाम् ॥

Note :— The या and सा simply stand for यद् and तद्, and the prohibition is not confined to the nominative case only, as the forms या and सा may lead one to think. यत्तदोः would have been a better sûtra. The prohibition applies in every case, as यकामधीमहे, तां पचामहे ॥ Or यकां यकामधीमहे (i. e. कशां गाथां वा), and तकां तकाम्पचामहे (i. e. ओषधीं शाकिनीं वा) ॥

Vårt :— Prohibition with regard to the affix त्यक् (V. 3. 34 S. 1983) should be stated also :— As अधित्यका, उपत्यका ॥

Vårt :— So also in the affix वुन् used in benediction as जीवताद् जीवका and भवतात् भवका. See III. 1. 150. S. 2912.

Note :— The feminine of पावक &c. in the Veda does not take इ for अ ॥ As हिरण्यवर्णाः शुचयः पावकाः, यासु लोमकाः कक्षकाः &c. But पाविकाः, अलोमिकाः in secular literature.

Vårt :— So also when the second member is elided in a compound : as देवका, यज्ञका, the second member दत्त is elided, the fuller forms being देवदत्तिका, यज्ञदत्तिका (अनजादौ विभाषा लोपो वक्तव्यः ) See V. 3. 83 Vart S. 2035.

Vårt :— क्षिपका &c. should be enumerated in this prohibition as क्षिपका, ध्रुवका, पुत्रका, चटका, कन्यका ॥

Vårt :— तारका is formed when it means 'stars', but तारिका 'a maid-servant' from तारयति ॥

Vårt :— वर्णका is formed when it means 'a mantle or mask', but वर्णिका 'an expounder' : as वर्णिका भागुरी लोकायते 'Bhaguri is a commentary of Lokayata'.

Vårt :— वर्तका 'a bird' according to the Eastern grammarians, but वर्तिका according to the Northern authorities. Why do we say 'when meaning a bird'? Observe वर्तिका खारी लोकायतस्य ॥

Vårt :— अष्टका when meaning a पितृदेवत्य ceremony, but अष्टिका खारी ॥ The ceremony related to Pitridevata is called Pitridaivatya, the affix is यत् ॥ The former is derived from the root अश् with affix तकन् (अश्नन्ति ब्राह्मणा अस्याम् ), the other is derived from the numeral अष्टन् by the affix कन् (V. 1. 22 S. 1687).

Vårt :— Optionally सूतका, पुत्रका and वृन्दारका, the other forms are सूतिका, पुत्रिका, and वृन्दारिका ॥

Note :— The word वेति of this vartika should be analysed as वा अ इति and not वेति; and it means that अ is optionally substituted for the vowel that precedes क ॥ Therefore in पुत्रिका the short इ which is not the अ of this sûtra, but of ङीन् of पुत्री shortened to इ, this is replaced by अ. In other examples इ is replaced by अ ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
465. According to the opinion of Northern grammarians, इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the long आ of the feminine (under VII. 4. 13 S. 834 before the affix क ), which is preceded by a य् or a क् ॥

The mention of 'northern grammarians' makes this an optional rule. As आर्यका or आर्यिका, चटकका or चटकिका ॥ Why do we say 'of long आ'? Observe सांकाश्ये भवा सांकाश्यिका ॥ The word सांकाश्य is formed from संकाश by the affix ण्य (संकाशे निर्वृत्तम्) ॥ Then is added the affix वुञ् (IV. 2. 121 S. 1345). Here there is no shortening of a long आ, and hence no option is allowed.

Why do we say preceded by य् or क? Observe अश्विका only (from अश्वा) ॥ Why do we say the आ of the Feminine affix? The word पूर्वायाः is exhibited in the feminine, in order to indicate that the rule applies when the feminine affix आप् is shortened to अ ॥

Therefore not here
‹?› from ‹?› ( शुभं याति ) ॥ So also ‹?› from भद्रया where आ is part of the root या ( see III. 2. 74 S. 3118 ).

Vârt :—Prohibition must be stated of the y and v being finals of a root. When the y or v preceding this â, is the final of the root, the prohibition contained in the sûtra, does not apply : as सुनयिका, सुपाकिका ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
466. According to the opinion of Northern grammarians, इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the आ (before क by VII. 4. 13 S. 834), of भस्त्रा, एषा, अजा, ज्ञा, द्वा (VII. 2. 102 S. 265 ), and स्वा ; even not then, when the negative particle precedes them.

The word भस्त्राजाज्ञाद्वास्वाम् of the Sûtra has no case affix, but we must interpret it as having the genitive case affix elided after it; the word नञ्पूर्वाणामपि is used in the Sûtra merely for the sake of clearness, for even without these words, the rule would have applied, when the negative particle preceded ; because as we have already shown, the rule of tadanta vidhi applies here. The word भस्त्रा is mentioned in the Sûtra to indicate that the rule would apply to it even then when it is an upasarjana. When it is not an upasarjana, the form would be evolved by the next Sûtra.

Note :—भस्त्रा is a word which has no corresponding masculine form and as such, by the following rule VII. 3. 48 it would not have taken इ ; its special mention here indicates that it should be the secondary member of the compound here as अविद्यमाना भस्त्रा यस्याः - अभस्त्रा, the Diminutive of which is अभस्त्रका or अभस्त्रिका ॥ Here first the आ is shortened, as it is a secondary member ( upasarjana ), then when the Bahuvrîhi is made, the feminine affix टाप् is added to this अभाषितपुंस्क word, then this आ is shortened before क by VII. 4. 13. This short अ (VII. 4. 13 ) does not come in the room of the आ which is ordained to come after a word having no corresponding masculine.

But of the two words एषा and द्वा, the addition of इ would be prohibited, when they are preceded by another word; because in a compound the elided case affix is considered to be present, and therefore the prohibition of असुपः of Sûtra VII. 3. 44 S. 463 would have applied to these. Thus अनेषका, परमेषका, अद्वके, परमद्वके ॥

Note :—The mention of these two words in the Sûtra from this point of view, would be rather redundant, while in the case of the other four words, भस्त्रा, अजा, ज्ञा, and स्वा, there would be इत्त्व, by the option allowed by this Sûtra, even when they are the last members in a compound and in spite of the prohibition of असुपः ॥

By this process of elimination, we come to the conclusion stated above, that the words नञ्पूर्वाणामपि qualify स्वा only. For this word alone is ambiguous. For when स्वा is a Sarvanâma meaning one's own, i. e., when it is not an upasarjana, then it is capable of taking अकच् by V. 3. 71. S. 2026. Thus स्वा+अकच् अ + आ = स्वका ॥ Here the अ before क is not an अ in the room of a long आ; and so the present sûtra will not apply to this स्वा. All the same the अ of स्वक will be changed to इ by VII. 3. 44 ante, and it will be स्विका always. So also परमास्विका ॥

But when स्व means agnate, soul, or property, then it is never in the feminine originally. Therefore, it must be either a sañjñâ (Name) or an upasarjana (secondary member of a compound) in order to give scope to this sûtra. For then it can become feminine in long आ, which can take the affix कन् with which it will be स्वका or स्विका by the present sûtra.

Thus when स्वा is a Proper Name, the feminine will be ‹?› and so ‹?›. So also निर्भस्त्रका or निर्भस्त्रिका, एषका or एषिका, अजका or अजिका, ज्ञाका or ज्ञिका, द्वके or द्विके, निःस्वका or निःस्विका ॥

The word त्यद् is read in the sûtra with अत् and it shows that the option of this sûtra does not apply when the त्यद् is not changed to अ, as एतिके and एतिकाः, for in the dual and plural there is no substitution.

Note :—Of एषा and द्वा there are no examples with the negative particle. For if the compounding with the नञ् takes place after the addition of the अकच्, or on the contrary, if first अकच् be added and then the compounding takes place, in both alternatives, the case-affixes must be added in order to substitute अ for the final by VII. 2. 102 S. 265 and it is only when this अ is substituted that the feminine आप् can come. So that the case-affix is the principal ingredient, and आप् comes after सु, and therefore by the prohibition of असुपः in VII. 3. 44, there can arise no occasion for the substitution of इ. Therefore अनेषका and अद्वका are the invariable forms of these words with the negative particle नञ् ॥

‹?› may mean ‹?› or ‹?› or ‹?› or ‹?› ॥

The word स्वा is taken in the Sûtra not as a Sarvanâma but in the sense of agnates and property, for the sake of implying that the rule will apply to it when it is a sañjñâ, (i. e. when it means agnates or property and not self) and when it is an upasarjana.

Note :—compare I. 1. 27. S. 213 for the Sarvanâma स्व ॥

The anuvṛtti of "आत स्थाने," which we read into this aphorism from the last sûtra, qualifies the long of स्वा only and not of the sarvanâmans एषा and द्वा ; because the sarvanâmans take the affix अकच् ( V. 3. 71. S. 2026 ) where other words would have taken कन् or अज्ञात क or कुत्सित क &c. Thus स्वा + अकच् अ + आ ( because this अकच् comes always before the टि portion of a word). Here the अ of स्वक before क is not a substitute in the place of long आ of स्वा, but it is a portion of the affix अकच् ॥ Therefore the words आत स्थाने can not qualify it.

As regards the other words भस्त्रा and अजा there is no necessity of qualifying them by आत स्थाने because they being invariably feminine, will always shorten their आ before क ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
467. According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians, इ is not substituted for an अ obtained from the shortening of the Feminine आ (VII. 4. 13 S. 834), when to the feminine in long आ there is no equivalent masculine, even when the Negative particle precedes.

अभाषितपुंस्क means a noun which is always feminine and has no corresponding masculine form. When a short अ is ordained to replace the long आ of such a feminine, there may be optionally इ in place of such a short अ in forming a secondary feminine. Thus ‹?› is such a word. It has no corresponding masculine form. When we form a derivative noun from such a word, by the affix कन् before which आ is shortened by VII. 4. 13, such as, ‹?›, then the feminine of this word may be either ‹?› or ‹?›. But the addition of इ is not optional, but compulsory, after a Bahuvrîhi compound, though such a compound may have as its member an अभाषितपुंस्क word. The reason of this is, that a Bahuvrîhi compound is always a भाषितपुंस्क i. e., it has always a corresponding masculine form. Therefore, where a short अ is ordained to come in the place of a long आ of a word which though अभाषितपुंस्क singly is a member of a Bahuvrîhi compound, the substitution in the place of such अ is compulsory and not optional. Thus the word खट्वा is always feminine and has no corresponding masculine form. We can form a Bahuvrîhi compound from it such as अखट्वः meaning ‘a man who has no bedstead’. The feminine of this will be अखट्विका ‘a woman who has no bedstead’. This need not take the Samâsânta affix कप् as V. 4. 154. S. 891. is optional.

Now, this
word ‹?› may take the affix ‹?› by V. 3. 73. S. 2028 when the sense is want of knowledge, such as ‹?› will be ‹?› || Before this the long ‹?› will be shortened to ‹?› by VII. 4. 13 S. 834 Here the option of the present sûtra will not apply. Thus we shall have only one form ‹?› by VII. 3. 44. S. 463 meaning 'who is this woman without a bedstead?' or 'is it really so that this woman has no bedstead.' But when the samâsânta affix ‹?› of sûtra V. 4. 154 S. 891 is added then the option of the present sûtra will apply. For when ‹?› is added, we have the Bahuvrîhi compounds as ‹?› or ‹?› (VII. 4. 15 S. 892) 'a man who has no bedstead.' The Feminine of the second form ‹?› will be ‹?› or ‹?› ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
468. According to the opinion of other Teachers, â is substituted for the ‹?›, which arose from the shortening of the feminine of a word, which has no corresponding masculine form.
Thus गङ्गाका or गङ्गिका ॥
But if a word has a corresponding masculine form, then there is no option, as शुभिका ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
469. The following rules apply to a Nominal-stem, which is not a subordinate term in a compound.
This is an adhikâra aphorism pure and simple, and has governing force upto IV. 1. 77: S. 531 and prohibits the application of affixes to 'upasarjanas.' That is to say, whatever we shall treat of hereafter, is to be understood to apply to such terms only which are not upasarjana or a subordinate term in a compound. (I. 2. 43 S. 653).
Note:— As a general rule, tadanta-vidhi (I. 1. 72 S. 26) does not apply to compounds; but the present sûtra indicates by implication that the tadanta-vidhi applies to compounds, for the purposes of the application of feminine affixes. For had it not been so, there would have been no necessity of making the present sûtra; for a rule applicable to a simple word as such, would not have applied to it, when it was part of a compound—whether subordinate (upasarjana), or principal (pradhâna). But the present sûtra indicates that the tadanta-vidhi does apply, if the word does not become a subordinate member, but is regarded as the principal member, of a compound.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
470. The affix ङीप् is added, in the feminine, after a Nominal-stem ending in short a, if the affix with which it ends has an indicatory ट्, or if the affix be ढ or अण्, or अञ् or द्वयसच्, or दघ्नच्, or मात्रच्, or तयप्, or ठक्, or ठञ्, or कञ् or क्वरप् ॥
The word अदन्तात् 'ending in short a' is understood here by anuvṛtti from IV. 1. 4 S. 454 and qualifies the affixes above-mentioned, wherever necessary. This debars the affix टाप् of IV. 1. 4 S. 454. We shall give examples of each seriatim. (1) Thus, m., कुरुचर, f., कुरुचरी; m., मद्रचर, f., मद्रचरी (चर + ई = चर् + ई; the final अ is elided by VI. 4. 148 S. 311). The word kuru-chara is formed by टट् (III. 2. 16 S. 2930), of which ट् is indicatory.
But if these words being the last members of a compound, are treated as upasarjana (I. 2. 43 S. 653), then they will not take the affix ङीप् in the feminine. Now in a Bahuvrîhi compound, all the component members are upasarjana, (II. 2. 35 S. 898); therefore, the feminine of such compounds will not take ङीप् ॥ Thus, बहुकुरुचरा ॥ So also the word नदट् is read with an indicatory ट् in the पचादि class of Gaṇapâṭha under sûtra III. 1. 134 S. 2896, it forms its feminine as नदी, because it has an indicatory ट् ॥
The word वक्ष्यमाण is formed with the affix शानच् (III. 3. 14. S. 3107), where the affix is the substitute of लृट् ॥ Therefore, this affix has an indicatory ट् as well as an indicatory ल्, and therefore, its feminine ought to be formed by the present sûtra, and so the Feminine ought to be वक्ष्यमाणी ॥ This is, however, not the case, because of the following Paribhâshâ.
Paribhâshâ:— 'The substitutes of ल् do not produce the effect which depends on the indicatory letters of ल् ॥' This paribhâshâ is derived from the jñâpaka of sûtra III. 4. 103 S. 2209 where the यासुट् the substitute of लिङ् is made expressly ङित् ॥ Or, we may infer this from the prohibition ‹?› of sûtra I. 1. 56. S. 49. So though in some places, the substitute ‹?› may produce the operations required by anubandhas, because they have an indicatory, yet it will not be so always.
(2) Of words ending in ढ we have, m., सौपर्णेय, f., सौपर्णेयी; so also f.,
The ढ stands for the affix ढक्; and it is replaced by एय् (VII. 1. 2, S. 475). Thus सुपर्णा + ढक् (IV. 1. 120 S. 1123) = सुपर्णा + एय = सौपर्णेय (VII. 2. 118 S. 1076).
Note:— There is no affix which is merely ढ without any indicatory letters, and denoting the feminine; the only affix as said above is ढक्.
