2238. There is luk-elision in the room of that tense affix (लिट्) which comes after आम् of the Perfect.

Thus एधाम् + त = एधाम् + 0

Then the following sutra appears.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2239. After a verb which ends with आम्, the verb 'to do' is annexed, when लिट् follows.

After the verbs formed by taking the आम् augment, the perfect tense of कृञ् is added, to form their Perfect. The word कृञ् includes also the verbs भू and अस्. This we infer from the next sûtra आम्प्रत्ययवत्कृञोऽनुप्रयोगस्य (I. 3. 63 § 2240) from the fact that root कृञ् is specifically mentioned in it as an anuprayoga or auxiliary verb. For the sûtra I. 3. 63 is confined to कृञ् anuprayoga, implying thereby that there are other anuprayoga verbs also which are not governed by that sûtra I. 3. 63. In fact, the word कृञ् of the present sûtra is a Pratyâhâra or a formula, formed with the कृ of the sûtra भूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे संपद्यकर्तरि च्विः (V. 4. 50) and the ञ् of the sûtra कृञः सातिदाचिष्वलोपः (V. 4. 58), and thus, as a pratyâhâra कृञ् means and includes कृ, भू and अस् also. The roots कृ, भू and अस् denote action in general, while the bases in आम् such as कास् denote a particular action; and hence when the auxiliary कृ, भू or अस् is combined with आम् ending base, the two senses, namely the general sense of the auxiliary and the particular sense of the आम् ending verb, coalesce into one and give one full indivisible sense. Thus the syntactical connection is indissoluble or abheda-anvaya.

Therefore, though the root संपद् is included in the Pratyâhâra कृञ् (for that pratyâhâra extends over eight sûtras V. 4. 50 to V. 4. 58 and संपद् is in sûtra V. 4. 53) yet that root is not applicable here, because it does not denote mere action and so can never form an abheda-anvaya with the main verb.

Now the auxiliary कृञ् because it has an indicatory ञ् would take the affixes of the Parasmaipada when the fruit of the action accrues to another, by force of I. 3. 72; but it is prevented by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2240. When the principal verb that takes the affix आम् is Âtmanepadî, then the verb कृञ् when subjoined thereto as an auxiliary, will similarly be Âtmanepadî, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent.

This sûtra applies where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The question is what conjugation, parasmai or âtmanepada, do the auxiliaries take, in forming the periphrastic perfect? This sûtra supplies the answer. The auxiliary कृ follows the conjugation of its principal, the other auxiliaries do not. Thus the root एध् (to increase, prosper) is âtmanepadî, therefore in forming the periphrastic perfect, the verb कृ will be also in the âtmanepada. But the other auxiliaries भू and अस् retain their own peculiar conjugation and are not influenced by the conjugation of their principal. Thus एधांबभूव, एधामास.

The word âm-pratyaya of the sûtra is a Bahuvrîhi, in which the force is that of atadguṇa-saṃvijñâna. That is, the root without the affix आम् is meant here, and not along with or qualified by the actual presence of आम्: it means 'that after which the affix आम् comes.' Of the verb kriñ, when subjoined to another as an auxiliary, the termination is that of the âtmanepada, like the verb that takes the affix आम् ॥

Note:—If this sûtra enjoined a rule of injunction (vidhi), then there would be the termination of the âtmanepada even in examples like ‹?› and ‹?› where the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. This is no valid objection to the present sûtra. It is to be interpreted in both ways, that is, both as a vidhi (a general injunction) and a niyama (a restrictive injunction). How is that to be done? Because the word "pûrvavat" of the immediately preceding Ashțâdhyâyî sûtra is to be read in the present aphorism also and thus there are two sentences. That is, there is âtmanepada of the auxiliary, when the Primary verb is âtmanepadî, but not the contrary. Thus चकास् (to appear with great splendour) is originally parasmaipadî and the auxiliary after it will be parasmaipada even when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, as चकासाञ्चकार (he appeared with great splendour). The second explanation, in that case, will be for the sake of establishing a niyama or restrictive rule.

It has already been said above, that the auxiliary verbs कृ, भू and अस् are used in forming the periphrastic perfect. This is done by force of the aphorism III. 1. 40 § 2239 कृञ्चानुप्रयुज्यते लिटि, meaning, the verb kriñ is annexed in the perfect tense, to verbs that take आम्. In this sûtra (III. 1. 40) the word kriñ is a pratyâhâra, implying the verbs भू and अस्. It might be asked how is this pratyâhâra formed? The word kri is taken from the fourth word of sûtra V. 4. 50, भूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे &c. and the letter ñ is taken from sûtra V. 4. 58 कृञः सातिदाचिष्वलोपः &c. This is the way in which the commentators explain, how not only the verb kriñ is used as an auxiliary in forming the periphrastic perfect, but also the verbs भू and अस्. These three verbs denoting absolute action, unmodified by any especial condition, have in all languages been fixed upon as the best auxiliaries.

It must, however, be noted that the word kriñ in this sûtra is not used as a pratyâhâra and consequently does not include the verbs भू and अस्. Therefore कृ requires here Âtmanepada termination.

Thus एधाम् + कृ + त

Now applies the following :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2241. The words 'eś' and 'irech' are the substitutes of 'ta' and 'jha' respectively in the Perfect tense.

The श् of एश् indicates that it replaces the whole of the affix त (I. 1. 55).

The च् of इरेच् is for the sake of accent (VI. 1. 165).

Thus एधे, एधाञ्चक्रे, एधाञ्चक्रिरे ।

Why are the substitutes taught here as एश् and इरेच् and not as ‹?› and ‹?›; for the would have become by III. 4. 79. § 2233? The very fact, that is uttered in these substitutes indicates by implication (jñâpaka) that the rule III. 4. 79, by which the of âtmanepada terminations are changed to , is not applicable to substitutes of Âtmanepada terminations. Therefore and which replace , and in are not governed by III. 4. 79, and is not changed to , nor to , nor to .

Thus एधाम् + कृ + त = एधाम् + कृ + ए . Now the लिट् affixes being ârdhadhâtuka, this requires that the should be gunated to . But this is prevented by the following :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2242. The affixes of Liṭ (Perfect Tense) not coming after a conjunct consonant, are as if they had an indicatory क (kit).

The terminations of लिट् (Perfect) not being पित् terminations, are कित्, after verbs that have no compound consonants. The phrase अपित् (not being marked with प्) qualifies this sûtra also, being drawn from the previous Ashțâdhyâyî sûtra.
Being the prohibition of I. 1. 5, S. 2217 applies and there is no guṇation, as otherwise would have been, by force of S. 2168.
Thus ‹?›. At this stage, two rules appear, one requiring the reduplication of ‹?› (लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य VI. 1. 8. S. 2177) and the other requiring ‹?› to be changed to ‹?› by इको यणचि (VI. 1. 77. S. 47). This last is subsequent in order of Ashṭâdhyâyî and therefore should take effect first. But if it took effect first, we have ‹?›. Then the reduplication will be ‹?›. Here no ‹?› is left for the application of VII. 4. 66 and we cannot get any form. Therefore ‹?› does not take place first, by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2243. When an affix beginning with a vowel follows, that is a cause of reduplication, a substitute shall not take the place of a preceding vowel, whilst the reduplication is yet to be made; but the reduplication having been made, the substitution may then take place.

NOTE:—This sûtra has been explained in different ways by the authors of the Kâśikâ and of the Siddhânta Kaumudî. According to the former, the sûtra means:—Before an affix having an initial vowel, which causes reduplication, the substitute which takes the place of a vowel is like the original vowel even in form, only for the purposes of reduplication and no further. The explanation given by Kâśikâ is more in harmony with the Great Commentary. For all practical purposes, the two explanations lead to the same conclusion. According to Kâśikâ, the vowel-substitute is sthânivat, in the sense, that it is exactly of the same form as the original, and retains this form only for a fixed time viz., so long as the reduplication is being made; but as soon as the reduplication has been made, the substitute takes its proper form.

Thus in ‹?› is a vowel affix, and it causes reduplication; therefore substitution for the preceding vowel will not take place whilst the reduplication is to be made. Thus ‹?›. Now the following applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2244. A short ‹?› (I. 1. 51) is substituted for the ‹?› or ‹?› of the reduplicate when an affix follows.

The ‹?› is always followed by ‹?› by उरण् रपरः ॥ Thus we have ‹?›. The ‹?› is elided by हलादिः शेषः S. 2179.

Why do we say "when an affix follows"? Observe ‹?› (page 101 S. 199).

Why have we used the word "when the affix follows" in the sûtra? For would not the word ‹?› limit the designation to that only after which there was actually an affix?

Ans. No. Because without the word the sûtra would have run thus "after whatsoever is an affix enjoined, that which begins therewith is called an Aṅga." In this view, we could not get the form ‹?› in the perfect (लिट्) of the root ‹?› 'to cut.'

This is thus formed:—
‹?› = ‹?› (VI. 1. 8. लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य)
= ‹?› (VI. 1. 17. ‹?›)
= ‹?› (VII. 4. 66. उरत् and उरण् रपरः)
= ‹?› (VII. 4. 60. हलादिः शेषः) = ‹?› the 3rd per. Sing.

If the word "pratyaye" did not exist, then the designation aṅga would be applied to the whole base plus the affix i.e. (‹?›) as a whole. That being so, ‹?› will assume the form of ‹?› for the ‹?› will be vocalised by VI. 1. 17; for the ‹?› in the place of ‹?› will not be sthânivat, by अचः परस्मिन् पूर्वविधौ, because to be sthânivat, there must be an efficient cause outside (‹?›), as of ‹?›; but this ‹?› was by hypothesis included in the aṅga designation. So there being no outside cause, the substitute of ‹?› in ‹?› will not be sthânivat; and not being so, it will not be considered as a samprasâraṇa vowel. The ‹?› of ‹?› not being a samprasâraṇa, the prohibition (न संप्रसारणे संप्रसारणम् &c. VI. 1. 37) when a semi-vowel has once been vocalised, there is no vocalisation of the other semi-vowel that precedes it; will not apply, and so ‹?› will be vocalised to ‹?›.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2245. For the Guttural and ह of a reduplicate there is substituted a Palatal.

Thus ‹?›. So also ‹?›.

Then we form 2nd. Pers. Sing. ‹?›.

Here the following sûtra prevents the insertion of इट् before थल्, which otherwise would have come by virtue of VII. 2. 35 S. 2184.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2246. The augment इट् is not added to that Ârdhadhâtuka affix, though beginning with a consonant except य, when it is joined to a root, which in the Grammatical system of Instruction (i.e. in the Dhâtupâṭha) is of one syllable, and is without accent (anudâtta).

The word upadeśe qualifies both words ekâc, and anudâtta. Why do we say "which is monosyllabic?" So that the present rule should not apply to the same root when it is Intensive, with the affix यङ् elided. The Intensive of every verb is included in the enunciation of its root; and as a general rule, all the sûtras specified for the simple root, will apply to the Intensive also, with certain exceptions, as contained in the following:—

शितपा शपानुबन्धेन निर्दिष्टं यद्गणेन च ।
यदेकाच् ग्रहणं चैव पञ्चैतानि न यङ्लुकि ॥

"These five sorts of operations will not apply to Intensive-yaṅ-luk forms:
1. When the simple root is exhibited in the sûtra with श्तिप् as भू in VII. 4. 73 is shown as भवति ॥ In the Intensive, the perfect will be बोभवाञ्चकार and not भवाञ्चकार. 2. Where the root is exhibited with श as the root ‹?› in VII. 2. 49 is shown as ‹?›. There is ‹?› after the Desiderative of simple root, but not in Intensive. 3. When a simple root is exhibited with an anubandha, as शीङ् VII. 1. 6. 4. Where a gaṇa is mentioned in a rule, as श्यन् is taught after Divâdi-roots (III. 1. 69). It will apply to simple roots of Divâdi gaṇa, and not to their Intensive. 5. Lastly, where the word एकाच् is used in a sûtra. As VII. 2. 10. That rule will apply to एकाच् simple roots and not to their Intensives.

This we infer because the word ekâc is used in the present sûtra. For had not this been the meaning, then there was no necessity of using the word "eka" in the sûtra, for the word अचः Abl. singular, by itself alone would have denoted one vowel; but by the additional use of the word "eka," the roots consisting of more than one vowel are excluded.
Therefore, since we find that the last statement in the above verse (‹?› &c.) is supported by the inference to be drawn from the present sutra, we may conclude that the other four statements of the above verse are also authoritative and approved by Panini. See also sûtra II. 2. 19.

Therefore the substitute root vadha (II. 4. 42) is not affected by the present rule; for though the root which replaces vadha in Dhatupatha is taught (upadesa) with one vowel, yet its substitute vadha is taught (upadesa) in the sutra II. 4. 42 with two vowels, hence it is not ekach: and so it gets the augment and we have vadhitum. But the prohibition applies to han as hantum and not hanitum.

The anudatta roots will be shown later on by giving a list of them.

Thus एधाम् + च + कृ + आ = एधाञ्चक्रे, and so also एधाञ्चक्राते ॥

The 2nd Pers. Pl. is एधाम् + चकृ + ध्वे

Here applies the next sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2247. The cerebral sound ‹?› is substituted in the room of the ध of षीध्वम्, and of the Personal-endings of the Aorist and the Perfect, after a stem ending in इण् (a vowel other than अ).

Therefore एधाम् + चकृ + ध्वे = एधाञ्चकृढ्वे ॥

एधाञ्चक्रे । एधाञ्चक्राते । एधाञ्चक्रिरे ॥

Similarly the perfect of एध् may be formed by the auxiliary भू as well as by अस्. But in the case of भू and अस्, though the Principal Verb is atmanepadi, the auxiliaries will be conjugated as Parasmaipadi. Thus एधाञ्चकार and एधामास &c. First person singular is एधाञ्चक्रे.

Now the perfect of अस् is formed by replacing अस् by भू; but here it is not so replaced, because then the rule about अस् being an auxiliary would be useless; as भू is already taught. Had it not been so, then instead of saying कृञ् चानुप्रयुज्यते &c., Panini would have used कृस चानुप्रयुज्यते or कृभूषानुप्रयुज्यते &c. But the fact that he uses the Pratyahara कृञ् shows that अस् must be conjugated as a distinct form, and not replaced by भू. Therefore though the Perfect of the Principal Verb is atmanepadi, yet the perfect of the Auxiliary Verb अस् is in parasmaipada. In other words, the forms आसाञ्चक्रे &c., can never stand alone, but must be used as auxiliaries. How is then अस् to be conjugated in the perfect? See below.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2248. A long vowel is substituted in the Perfect for the initial अ of a reduplicate.

This debars the single substitute of the form of the subsequent ordained by VI. 1. 97.

Thus अस् + णल् = आ + स् + णल् = आस ॥

Thus एधामासुः &c.

Singular Dual Plural
3rd. person एधाञ्चक्रे एधाञ्चक्राते एधाञ्चक्रिरे
2nd. person एधाञ्चकृषे एधाञ्चक्राथे एधाञ्चकृढ्वे
1st. person एधाञ्चक्रे एधाञ्चकृवहे एधाञ्चकृमहे

3rd. person एधांबभूव एधांबभूवतुः एधांबभूवुः
2nd. person एधांबभूविथ एधांबभूवथुः एधांबभूव
1st. person एधांबभूव एधांबभूविव एधांबभूविम

3rd. person एधामास एधामासतुः एधामासुः
2nd. person एधामासिथ एधामासथुः एधामास
1st. person एधामास एधामासिव एधामासिम

लुट् First Future.

The Periphrastic Future is regularly formed. Thus एध् + ता = एधिता ॥ So also एधितारौ, एधितारः, एधितासे, एधितासाथे । The second person plural is एध् + तास् + ध्वे

Here applies the following sûtra by which the स is elided.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2249. The स is dropped before an affix beginning with धि ॥

Thus एधि + तास् + ध्वे = एधिताध्वे ॥ The First person singular is एधि + तास् + इ ॥ Here the स is changed to ह by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2250. For the स of तास् and सास् there is substituted ह before the personal-ending ए ॥

Thus एधितास् + ए = एधिताहे ॥

First Future or लुट्

Singular Dual Plural
1st person एधिताहे एधितास्वहे एधितास्महे
2nd person एधितासे एधितासाथे एधिताध्वे
3rd person एधिता एधितारौ एधितारः

Second Future or लृट्

The second Future presents no irregularities. Thus we have,

Singular Dual Plural
1st person एधिष्ये एधिष्यावहे एधिष्यामहे
2nd person एधिष्यसे एधिष्येथे एधिष्यध्वे
3rd person एधिष्यते एधिष्येते एधिष्यन्ते

Imperative or लोट्

Thus एध् + शप् + ते = एध् + अ + ते ॥ Here applies the following rule by which ए is changed to आम् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2251. In the Imperative 'âm' is substituted for what would have substituted otherwise 'e' by III. 4. 79.

Thus एध + ते = एधताम् so also एधेताम् एधन्ताम् ॥ The 2nd person singular is एधसे ॥ Here applies the following, by which से is changed to स्व ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2252. For such an 'e' coming after 's' is substituted व, and for that coming after व is substituted अम् in the Imperative.

This supersedes the आम् substitution of the last sûtra. Thus for से we have एधस्व and for ध्वे we have ध्वम् ॥

Thus एध + से = एधस्व । एधेयाम् । एधध्वम् ॥ The 1st person singular is एध + इ Here by the following sûtra the इ is changed to ऐ
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2253. The 'ai' is substituted for 'e' forming part of the affixes of the first person of the Imperative. This debars ‹?› of the preceding but one sûtra. Thus ‹?› = — एधै, एधावहै, एधामहै ॥ लोट् or Imperative. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st person एधै एधावहै एधामहै 2nd person एधस्व एधेथाम् एधध्वम् 3rd person एधताम् एधेताम् एधन्ताम् -: 0 :- लङ् or Imperfect. Thus ‹?› + ‹?› + शप् + त ॥ Here the following sûtra causes the ‹?› to be replaced by ‹?›
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2254. आट् acutely accented is the augment of a verbal stem beginning with a vowel, in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional. This debars the augment अट् ॥ Thus आट् + एध् + त = ऐधत ॥ The vṛiddhi is by VI. 1. 90. S. 262. लङ् or Imperfect. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person. ऐधे ऐधावहि ऐधामहि 2nd Person. ऐधथाः ऐधेथाम् ऐधध्वम् 3rd Person. ऐधत ऐधेताम् ऐधन्त -: 0 :- लिङ् or Potential. Thus एध् + शप् + त ॥ Now the next sûtra ordains the augment सीयुट् to ‹?›
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2255. The personal endings of the Potential and the Benedictive take the augment 'sīyuṭ'. The ट् of सीयुट् is indicatory and shows that this augment is to be placed before the affixes (I. 1. 46 S. 38.) The उ is for the sake of pronunciation; this rule applies to the Ātmanepada affixes. In the Potential, the स of the augment is elided by VII. 2. 79. S. 2211. and the य् also, before a personal-ending beginning with a consonant, is dropped according to VI. 1. 66. S. 873. In the Benedictive, the augment retains its full form, only so far as it is not governed by VI. 1. 66. Thus एध् + सीयुट् + त = एध् + सीय् + त = एध् + ईय् + त (VII. 2. 79. S. 2211.) = एध् + ई + त (VI. 1. 66. S. 873) = एधेत ॥ So also एधेयाताम् ॥ The 3rd Person Plural is formed by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2256. The affix 'ran' is the substitute of 'jha' in the 'Liṅ' (Potential and Benedictive). The झ in other places, is replaced generally by अन्त (VII. 1. 3. S. 2169.) but in लिङ्, it is replaced by रन् ॥ Thus एध् + ईय् + रन् = एधेरन् ॥ So also 2nd Person singular &c. are एधेथाः, एधेयाथाम्, एधेध्वम् ॥ The 1st Person singular is formed by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2257. Short 'a' is the substitute of 'i' of the Ātmanepada first person singular in the Potential and Benedictive. Thus एध् + ईय् + अ = एध् + इय् + अ = एधेय ॥ So also एधेवहि, एधेमहि ॥ लिङ् or Potential. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person एधेय एधेवहि एधेमहि 2nd Person एधेथाः एधेयाथाम् एधेध्वम् 3rd Person एधेत एधेयाताम् एधेरन् आशीर्लिङ् or Benedictive. In the Benedictive, the affixes are Ārdhadhātuka and hence the स of सीयुट् is not elided. The इट् and सीयुट् though not strictly affixes, are yet parts of affixes, and hence their स् is changed to ष् ॥ Thus एध् + इट् + सीयुट् + त = एध् + इ + षीय् + त् + त = एधिषीष्ट ॥ So also एधिषीयास्ताम् ॥ Benedictive or आशीर्लिङ्. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st person एधिषीय एधिषीवहि एधिषीमहि 2nd Person एधिषीष्ठाः एधिषीयास्थाम् एधिषीध्वम् 3rd Person एधिषीष्ट एधिषीयास्ताम् एधिषीरन् लुङ् or Aorist. आट् + एध् + इट् + सिच् + त = ऐधिष्ट ॥ 3rd Person Dual is ऐधिषाताम् ॥ The 3rd Person Plural is ऐधि + स् + अत् ॥ Here applies the following sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2258. अत् is always substituted for the झ in the Atmanepada, when it is not preceded by a verbal stem ending in अ ॥ Thus ऐधिषत । The 2nd Person sing. is ऐधिष्ठाः, Dual ऐधिषाथाम् । In the Plural the ध of ध्वम् may be changed to ढ by applying VIII. 3. 78. S. 2247. Thus ऐधिढ्वम्. But some take the ‹?› of VIII. 3. 78. S. 2247 as not including the augment इट् and in that view the ध remains unchanged. Thus, ऐधिध्वम् । By doubling ध, and ढ we get sixteen forms. Thus ऐधिध्वम्, ऐधिढ्वम् &c. -: 0 :- लुङ् or AORIST. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person ऐधिषि ऐधिष्वहि ऐधिष्महि 2nd Person ऐधिष्ठाः ऐधिषाथाम् ऐधिध्वम् or ऐधिढ्वम् 3rd Person ऐधिष्ट ऐधिषाताम् ऐधिषत लृङ् or Conditional. The Conditional presents no irregularities, and is similar to the Second Future. Singular. Dual. Plural. 1st Person ऐधिष्ये ऐधिष्यावहि ऐधिष्यामहि 2nd Person ऐधिष्यथाः ऐधिष्येथाम् ऐधिष्यध्वम् 3rd Person ऐधिष्यत ऐधिष्येताम् ऐधिष्यन्त Here ends the conjugation of एध् in the Atmanepada. The rule of intermediate I It has been already taught before, that as a general rule the augment इट् is added to all affixes which begin with a consonant except (VII. 2. 85. S. 2184.) The roots that require this in their conjugation are Udâtta roots. It is desirable to collect together all roots which are anudatta and do not take this intermediate इ The following is a list of such roots :- 1. All monosyllabic roots ending in a vowel are anudâtta (nihata) and do not take इट् except roots ending in long ॠ or long ऌ, and except the following ‹?› ॥ The following consonant-ending roots are anit:— (1). शक्, 2. पच्, 3. मुच्, 4. रिच्, 5. वच्, 6. विच्, 7. प्रच्छ्, 8. भ्रस्ज्, 9. त्यज्, 10. निजिर्, 11. भज्, 12. भञ्ज्, 13. भुज्, 14. मस्ज्, 15. यज्, 16. युज्, 17. रुज्, 18. रञ्ज्, 19. विजिर्, 20. ष्वञ्ज्, 21. सञ्ज्, 22. सृज्, 23. अद्, 24. क्षुद्, 25. खिद्, 26. छिद्, 27. तुद्, 28. नुद्, 29. पद्, 30. भिद्, 31. विद्, 32. शद्, 33. षद्, 34. स्विद्, 35. स्कन्द्, 36. हद्, 37. क्रुध्, 38. क्षुध्, 39. बुध्, 40. बन्ध्, 41. युध्, 42. रुध्, 43. राध्, 44. व्यध्, 45. शुध्, 46. सिध्, 47. आप्, 48. क्षिप्, 49. छुप्, 50. तप्, 51. तिप्, 52. तृप्, 53. दृप्, 54. लिप्, 55. लुप्, 56. वप्, 57. शप्, 58. स्वप्, 59. सृप्, 60. यभ्, 61. रभ्, 62. लभ्, 63. गम्, 64. नम्, 65. यम्, 66. रम्, 67. मन्, 68. हन्, 69. क्रुश्, 70. दंश्, 71. दिश्, 72. दृश्, 73. मृश्, 74. रिश्, 75. रुश्, 76. लिश्र, 77. विश्, 78. स्पृश्, 79. कृष्, 80. त्वक्ष्, 81. द्विष्, 82. दुष्, 83. पिष्, 84. पु barb, 85. प्रुष्, 86. विष्, 87. शिष्, 88. शुष्, 89. श्लिष्, 90. तुष्, 91. द्विष्, 92. घस्, 93. वस्, 94. दह्, 95. दिह्, 96. दुह्, 97. नह्, 98. मिह्, 99. रुह्, 100. लिह्, 101. वह्. These 102 roots ending in consonants are anudatta. The roots तृप् and दृप् are optionally, according to some authors, read in the Churâdi class. They are not to be taken here, but the Divâdi तृप् and दृप् and hence these are shown above with the vikarana श्यन् ॥ Moreover :— The roots स्विद्, ष्विद्, क्ष्विद्, ‹?› are also shown with the vikarana श्यन् ॥ The root पत् is shown with the vikarana शप् ; and the root सु with ‹?›. This indicates that these roots when read in other classes are not Anit. Similarly रदिर् and जबिर् are exhibited with their anubandhas, to distinguish them from other roots of the same form, which have not these anubandhas. The root श्विति (श्वित्) should be included in this list, according to the opinion of Chandra and Durga. So also it is to be seen in the Bhashya. But Vyaghrabhuti has not read this root in Anit list. Hence it is not read. The nine roots रञ्ज्, भञ्ज्, मस्ज्, पद्, तुद्, बुध्, शुध्, पुष and शिष् are not enumerated by Patanjali in his Bhashya. But we have stated them here, according to the opinion of Vyâghrabhuti. NOTE:—As a general rule all monosyllabic roots ending in a vowel except long ऋ and long ऌ are anudatta, and do not take augment इट्: as यातु, यातः, यान्ति; पातु, पातः, पान्ति ॥ The following are the exceptions :— (1) All roots ending in short ऋ are Udâtta and take इट् ; as अरिष्यति ॥ (2) All roots ending in long ॠ are इट्, as तॄ—तरिता or तरीता ॥ (3) All roots ending in short ऌ are ‹?› except कॢप् (IX. 38 the references are to the class and number in the Dhatupatha) and ‹?› (V. 8, X. 271) : as ‹?› ॥ (4) All roots in short इ are Anit, except शि (I. 1059), 'to grow' and श्रि 'to attend' (I. 945), as शयिता, श्रयिता ॥ (5) All roots in long ई are Anit, except डी 'to rest' (II. 22), and डीङ् 'to fly' (I. 1017, IV. 27), as डयिता, ‹?› ॥ (6) All roots in long ऊ are इट्, as भविता, भाविता from भू and षू ॥ (7) All monosyllabic roots in short उ are Anit, except, यु 'to mix' (II. 23), रु 'to sound' (II. 24, I. 1008), ष्णु 'to sharpen' (II. 28), स्रु 'to flow' (II. 29), ष्टु 'to praise' (II. 26), द्रु 'to sound' (II. 27); and णु 'to cover' (II. 30, though consisting of more than one syllable, is treated like ‹?› for the purposes of इट्). Thus यविता, रोविता, स्नोविता, स्रोविता, स्तोविता, द्रोविता and ‹?› ॥ NOTE:—Of the roots ending in consonants, the following are anit. (1.) क—शक् 'to be able' (IV. 78, V. 15). शक्ता, शक्ष्यति ॥ (2) च—six roots :—पच् 'to cook' (I. 186) पक्ता, पक्ष्यति ; मुच् 'to loose' (VI. 137) मोक्ता ; रिच् 'to make empty' (VII. 4) रेक्ता ; वच् 'to speak' (II. 54) वक्ता ; विच् 'to separate' (VII. 5) वेक्ता ; सिच् 'to sprinkle' (VI. 140) सेक्ता ॥ (3.) छ—One root प्रच्छ् 'to ask' (VI. 120) प्रष्टा, प्रक्ष्यति ॥ (4.) ज—Fifteen roots :—रञ्ज् 'to colour' (I. 865, 1048) ; निजिर् 'to cleanse' (III. 11) नेक्ता, नेक्ष्यति ; अञ्ज् 'to honor' (I. 1047) अङ्क्ता ; भञ्ज् 'to break' (VII. 16) भङ्क्ता ; भ्रस्ज् 'to fry' (I. 181) भ्रष्टा or ‹?› ; त्यज् 'to quit' (I. 1035) ; यज् 'to sacrifice' (I. 1051) ; युज् 'to join' (IV. 68, VII. 7) ; रुज् 'to break' (VI. 123) ; ष्वञ्ज् 'to adhere' (I. 1036) ; सञ्ज् to
immersed, (VI. 122); 'to bend' (VI. 124) 'to enjoy' (VII. 17). भोक्ता, ष्वञ्ज 'to embrace' (I. 1025) परि-ष्वक्ता ; सृज 'to emit' 'to create' (IV. 60, VI. 121) ; मृज् 'to cleanse' (I. 269, II. 57), मार्ष्टा, मार्जिता ॥ The root मृज् is exhibited in the Dhâtupâṭha with a long indicatory ऊ, e.g. मृजूँ शुद्धौ (II. 57). It, therefore, optionally would take इट्. Nor does this root take augment अम्. The inclusion of this root in the above list is, therefore, questionable. Others read खिद् instead of मृज्. The भिद् root खिद् is Aniṭ (III. 12) i.e. खिद् 'to separate'. The खिद् of Rudhâdi takes इट्. (5.) Fifteen roots :— अद् 'to eat' [II. 1] अत्ता ; हद् 'to void excrement' (I. 1026) हत्ता ; स्कन्द् 'to leap' (I. 1028) स्कन्ता ; भिद् 'to break' (VII. 2) भेत्ता ; छिद् 'to cut' (VII. 3) छेत्ता ; क्षुद् 'to pound' (VII. 6) क्षोत्तान, क्षोत्स्यति ; शद् 'to perish' (I. 908, VI. 134) शत्ता ; सद् 'to sink' (I. 907, VI. 133) सत्ता ; स्विद् 'to sweat' (IV. 79) स्वेत्ता । The root स्विद् is exhibited as स्विद्यति in the kârikâ, showing that the Fourth class root is to be taken, and not the Bhuâdi (I. 780), which is udâtta and takes इट् ॥ पद् 'to go' (IV. 60), पत्ता ; खिद् 'to be troubled' (IV. 61, VI. 142, VII. 12) खेत्ता ; तुद् 'to strike' (VI. 1) तोत्ता ; णुद् 'to impel' (VI. 2) नोत्ता ; विद् (IV. 62) वेत्ता ॥ The root विद् is exhibited in the kârikâ, as विद्यति and विन्ते, therefore, the rule applies to दिवादि and रुधादि विद् ॥ The Adâdi (वेत्ति) and Tudâdi (विन्दति) विद् is सेट्, as वेदिता विज्ञानाय, वेदिता धनस्य ॥ (6.) Ten roots :— राध् with अप 'to offend' ; रुध् 'to obstruct' (IV. 65) रोद्धा ; युध् 'to fight' (IV. 64) योद्धा ; बन्ध् 'to bind' (I. 1022), बन्द्धा ; साध् 'to accomplish' (V. 17) साद्धा ; क्रुध् 'to be angry' (IV. 80) क्रोद्धा ; क्षुध् 'to be hungry' (IV. 81) क्षोत्धा ; शुध् 'to be pure' (IV. 82) शोद्धा ; बुध् 'to be aware' (IV. 63) बोद्धा ; व्यध् 'to pierce' (IV. 72) व्यद्धा ; सिध् 'to be accomplished' (IV. 83) सेद्धा । The roots शुध् and सिध् are exhibited in the Kârikâ with vikaraṇa (शुध्यति, सिध्यति) ; therefore शुध् and सिध् take इट् in other gaṇas than the Fourth ; as ‹?› and ‹?›. There is want of prohibition with regard to ‹?›, so we have सेधितव्यम् and सेधितोः ॥ राध् 'to accomplish' (IV. 71, V. 16) ; (7.) न्—Two roots : मन् 'to think' (IV. 67) मन्ता, हन् 'to kill' (II. 2), हन्ता ॥ The Divâdi should be taken, otherwise from मन्—मनिता (VIII. 9). (8.) प्—Thirteen roots : तप् 'to burn' (I. 1034, IV. 51) तप्ता तप्स्यति, तिप् 'to distil' (I. 885) तेप्ता ; आप् 'to obtain' (V. 14, X. 295) आप्ता ; वप् 'to sow' (I. 1052) वप्ता ; स्वप् 'to sleep' (II. 50) स्वप्ता ; लिप् 'to anoint' (VI. 139) लेप्ता ; लुप् (VI. 137) 'to break', The roots तृप् and दृप् optionally take इट्, as they belong to ‹?› class (VII. 2. 45, Divâdi 84-91). The special mention of these two roots in the kârikâ, is for the sake of indicating that these roots take ‹?› augment ; as त्रप्ता or तर्प्ता, or तर्पिता, दृप्ता, or दर्प्ता or दर्पिता ॥ The तृप् and दृप् belonging to the Tudâdi class, are Udâtta and सेट् ॥ सृप् (I. 1032) 'to creep' स्रप्ता ; शप् 'to curse' (I. 1049) शप्ता ; छुप 'to touch' (VI. 125) छोप्ता ; क्षिप् 'to throw' (IV. 14) क्षेप्ता ॥ (9.) भ्—Three roots : रभ् 'to desire' (I. 1028), as रब्धा, यभ् 'to coire' (I. 1020), यब्धा, लभ् 'to take' (I. 1024), लब्धा ॥ (10.) म्—Four roots : यम् 'to cease' (I. 1033), यन्ता ; रम् 'to play' (I. 908) रन्ता ; नम् 'to bow' (I. 887, 1030) नन्ता, गम् 'to go' (I. 1031) गन्ता ॥ (11.) श्—Ten roots :—दिश् 'to show' (VI. 3), दृश् 'to see' (I. 1037), दंश् 'to bite' (I. 1038), मृश् 'to rub' (VI. 131), स्पृश् 'to touch' (VI. 128), रिश् (VI. 126), रुश् (VI. 128) both meaning 'to hurt', क्रुश् (I. 909) 'to cry', विश् 'to enter' (VI. 130), लिश 'to be small' (IV. 70, VI. 127). As देष्टा, द्रष्टा, दंष्टा, म्रष्टा or मर्ष्टा, स्प्रष्टा or स्पर्ष्टा ॥ The roots with a penultimate short, which are anudâtta in the dhâtupâṭha, with the exception of ‹?› and ‹?›, take optionally the augment अम् (VI. 1. 59) ॥ रेश्टा, रोष्टा, क्रोष्टा, प्रवेष्टा, लेश्टा ॥ (12) Two roots : घस् 'to eat' (I. 747, and also substitute of अद्), as घस्ता ; वस् 'to dwell' (I. 1054), as वस्ता ॥ The वस् which takes Samprasâraṇa by VI. 1. 15 is meant here, and not वस् 'to cover' (II. 13), which does not vocalise, as वसित्वा वस्त्रेण, but उषित्वा from वस् 'to dwell' (VII. 2. 52). (13.) ष्—Ten roots : शिष् 'to distinguish' (VII. 14) शेष्टा ; पिष् 'to pound' (VII. 15) पेष्टा ; शुष् 'to become dry' (IV. 74) शोष्टा ; पुष् 'to be nourished' (IV. 73), पोष्टा ; त्विष् 'to shine' (I. 1050) त्वेष्टा ; विष् 'to pervade, to sprinkle' (I. 728, III. 13, IX. 51) वेष्टा ; श्लिष् 'to embrace' (I. 734, IV. 77) श्लेष्टा ; तुष् 'to be satisfied' (IV. 75) तोष्टा ; दुष् 'to be sinful' (IV. 76) दोष्टा दोषवति ; द्विष् 'to hate' (II. 3) द्वेष्टा, द्वेक्ष्यति ; कृष् 'to draw' (I. 1059, VI. 6 both Bhuâdi and Tudâdi are taken, as the kârikâ uses the two forms), क्रष्टा and कर्ष्टा ॥ (14.) Eight roots : दिह् 'to smear' (II. 5), देग्धा ; दुह् 'to milk' (II. 4), दोग्धा ; मिह् 'to sprinkle' (I. 1041) मेढा ; रुह् 'to grow' (I. 912) रोढा ; वह् 'to carry' (I. 1053) वोढा ; नह् 'to bind' (IV. 57) नद्धा ; दह् 'to burn' (I. 1041) दग्धा ; लिह् 'to lick' (II. 6) लेढा ॥ In other collections दृह् (I. 905, IV. 20), तृह् (IV. 89), स्निह् (VI. 23), ‹?›, are also enumerated; of these दृह् takes optionally इट् before affixes beginning with त, so also तृह् because it belongs to the ‹?› class (VII. 2. 45) the other two are not found (?) in root-collections hence the Kârikâ uses the words नह्यादयः ॥ We shall now conjugate all the roots of the Bhuâdi class, in their due order. We take the third root. 3. स्पर्ध 'to contend or vie with, to emulate, to compete.' Now we take up the conjugation of स्पर्ध्, the third root of Bhuâdi class. Its meaning given in the Dhâtupâṭha is "saṅgharṣa" which means "the desire to overcome another." This root is Intransitive, because the object is already included in the sense of the verb itself. It is Âtmanepadi. NOTE:—Thus it has been stated:— धातोरर्थान्तरे वृत्तेर्धात्वर्थेनोपसंग्रहात् । प्रसिद्ध्यविवक्षातः कर्मणोऽकर्मिका क्रिया ॥ लट् or Present Tense. स्पर्धते, स्पर्धेते, स्पर्धन्ते, स्पर्धसे, स्पर्धेथे, स्पर्धध्वे, स्पर्धे, स्पर्धावहे, स्पर्धामहे । लिट् or Perfect. स्पर्ध्+त=स्पर्ध्+ए (III. 4. 81. S. 2241) = स्पर्ध्+स्पर्ध्+ए Now applies the following sûtra :—

अभ्यासस्य शर्पूर्वाः खयः शिष्यन्ते । 'हलादिः शेषः' (२१७९) इत्यस्यापवादः । पस्पर्धे । स्पर्धिता । स्पर्धिष्यते । स्पर्धताम् । अस्पर्धत । स्पर्धेत । स्पर्धिषीष्ट । अस्पर्धिष्ट । अस्पर्धिष्यत । गाधृ । प्रतिष्ठा-लिप्सयोर्ग्रन्थे च । गाधते । जगाधे । 'बाधृ ५ लोडने' । लोडनं प्रतिघातः । बाधते । 'नाथृ ६ याचनोपतापैश्वर्याशीःषु' । *आशिषि नाथ इति वाच्यम्* । अस्याशिष्येवात्मनेपदं स्यात् । नाथते । अन्यत्र नाथति । नापते । 'दध धारणे' । दधते । 2259. Of a reduplicate, the hard consonants (aspirate and unaspirate) when preceded by a sibilant, are only retained, the other consonants are elided. This is an exception to हलादिशेषः (S. 2179.) NOTE:—It should be said rather, a hard consonant preceded by a hard consonant or a sibilant is only retained and the खर् consonants are elided as in ‹?› here ‹?› becomes ‹?› by the augment ‹?› (तुक्) ; in the reduplicate then ‹?› should be elided, and ‹?› retained out of ‹?› ; and not ‹?› retained and ‹?› elided ; for the च् represents ‹?›, and if this were retained, it would be ‹?› and not ‹?› that would be heard : for by VIII. 2. 1, the change of ‹?› to ‹?› is asiddha for the purposes of this rule. Vârt:—The verb नाथ् when meaning 'to bless,' takes âtmanepada terminations, as, सर्पिषो नाथते 'blesses with clarified butter.' मधुनो नाथते । Why do we say when meaning to bless? Observe, माणवकमुपनाथति । Thus स्पर्ध् स्पर्ध् + ए = पस्पर्धे ; and so पस्पर्धाते, पस्पर्धिरे &c. लुट् or First Future 3. स्पर्धिता, स्पर्धितारौ, स्पर्धितारः, 2nd S. 1. &c.
लृट् or Second Future 3. स्पर्धिष्यते, 2. स्पर्धिध्वे 1. स्पर्धिष्ये । लोट् or Imperative 3. स्पर्धताम् 2. स्पर्धस्व, 1. स्पर्धै । लङ् or Imperfect 3. अस्पर्धत, 2. अस्पर्धथाः, 1. अस्पर्धे । विधिलिङ् or Potential 3. स्पर्धेत, 2. स्पर्धेथाः, 1. स्पर्धेय । आशीर्लिङ् or Benedictive 3. स्पर्धिषीष्ट, 2. स्पर्धिषीष्ठाः, 1. स्पर्धिषीय । लुङ् or Aorist 3. अस्पर्धिष्ट, 2. अस्पर्धिष्ठाः, 1. अस्पर्धिषि । लृङ् or Conditional 3. अस्पर्धिष्यत, 2. अस्पर्धित्यथाः, 1. अस्पर्धिष्ये । - -:0: - 4. गाधृ "(1) to stand, stay, remain, (2) to seek, search or enquire, (3) to dive or plunge into, (4) to covet, (5) to compile, string or weave together." लट् or Present :— गाधते । लिट् or Perfect जगाधे &c. No peculiarity. Note: The indicatory ऋ is for VII. 4. 2. S. 2572 as लट् :— गाधते, गाधेते, गाधन्ते ॥ लिट् :— जगाधे ॥ लुट् :— गाधिता, गाधितारौ, गाधितारः ॥ लृट् — गाधिष्यते ॥ लोट् — गाधताम्, गाधस्व, गाधै ॥ लङ् — अगाधत, अगाधथाः, अगाधे ॥ विधिलिङ् — गाधेत, गाधेथाः, गाधेय ॥ आशीर्लिङ् — गाधिषीष्ट ॥ लुङ् — अगाधिष्ट, अगाधिष्ठाः, अगाधिषि ॥ लृङ् — अगाधिष्यत ॥ 5. बाधृ 'to harass, oppress, torment, press hard, annoy, trouble, disturb, vex, pain; 2. to resist, oppose, thwart, check, obstruct, arrest, interfere with. 3. to roll (लोडने) 4. to tempt. (विलोभने)' The word लोडन means to resist, or re-act. लट् :— बाधते ; लिट् :— बबाधे &c. Note :— From this root is derived the noun बाहु: "hand." By adding the Uṇâdi affix कु (u), and changing ध to ह (I. 27.) 6. णाथृ (नाथ), 7. णाधृ (नाध) 'to ask, beg, to solicit for anything, 2. to be sick, to harass, to trouble; 3. to have power, to be master, to prevail 4. to bless.' These roots are Âtmanepadî when meaning "to bless" and not when meaning “to ask" &c. (II. 3. 55 S. 616). लट् :— नाथते “he blesses" or नाथति “he begs” &c. Note:— उपताप means 'disease' (रोग) ; another reading is उपघात (Tarangini). Both these roots begin with a dental न. When meaning 'to bless,' it takes Âtmanepada, and the noun in construction is put in the sixth case by II. 3. 55. S. 616. As सर्पिषो नाथनम् । The sixth case affix is not elided in the compound. So we cannot have the form सर्पिर्नाथनम् । For here we have pratipada-vidhânâ sixth case. But when it is krid yoga shashṭhî, then there is compounding. When it does not mean 'to bless,' we have Parasmaipada. As, लट् — नाथति ; लिट् — ननाथ ; लुट् — नाशिता ; लृट् — नाशिष्यति ; लोट् — नाथतु ; लङ् — अनाथत् ; विधिलिङ् — नाथेत् ; आशीर्लिङ् — नाथ्यात्, अनाथीत् ; लृङ् — अनाशिष्यत् । Note: Maitreya and Âbharaṇakâra read the first root as णाट्; and they have the form प्रणाटते । On this Kâśyapa says "णाथते नोपदेवत्वनपुष्टं, गणरत्नमहोदधिवृत्तिकारादीनामनभिमतात्" ॥ 8. दध “1. to hold, 2. to have, possess, 3. to give, present.” लट् :— दधते, दधेते, दधन्ते ; दधसे ; दधावहे, दधामहे । लिट् = दध् + ए = ददध् + ए । Now apply the following sutras :-

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2260. ए is substituted for the short अ standing between two simple consonants of a verbal stem, before the personal endings of the Perfect which have an indicatory क् (I. 2. 5), provided that, at the beginning of the root, in the reduplication, no different consonant has been substituted; and when this ए is substituted, the reduplicate is elided.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2261. ए is substituted for अ, of a verbal stem standing between two simple consonants, the stem not having any different letter substituted in the reduplicate, when the ending थल् of the Perfect having the augment इट् follows, and thereby, the reduplicate is elided. By the phrase "no other consonant has been substituted" is meant "no other dissimilar in form consonant has been substituted". This we learn from the implication (jñâpaka) of sûtra VI. 4. 126 where exception is made in the case of ‹?› and ‹?›. Therefore, where the substitute is a different letter, then the reduplicate becomes âdeśâdi: otherwise not. If the form of the letter is not changed in the reduplicate, by substitution, then such substitution will not make the stem âdeśâdi. Thus by VIII. 4. 54, a letter (ग्, घ्, ड्, etc.) is substituted for a consonant (other than a nasal and a semi-vowel) in the reduplicate. Thus in the reduplicate is ‹?›, the first is also a substitute, for the substitute of ‹?› will be ‹?›. Such substitutes, however, are not meant here. Here, therefore, there will be the elision of the reduplicate and the ए substitution. Thus Similarly द + दध् + ए = देधे ॥ So also, 3. d. देधाते ; 3. p. देधिरे ; देधिषे, देथे, देधिवहे ॥ So also रेजतुः, रेजुः, येनतुः, येनुः, पेचतुः, पेचुः, देभतुः, देभुः ॥ Why 'for short अ'? Observe दिदिवतुः, दिदिवुः the इ is not replaced. Why do we say 'short अ'? Observe रासतुः, रासुः... Why do we say 'standing between two simple consonants'? Observe तस्तरतुः, तस्तरुः. Some say this example is not appropriate, for by I. 2. 5, the Perfect affixes are not कित् here, as they come after a conjunct consonant. The following is then more appropriate: सस्मरतुः ; and शशमतुः (Bhu. 586). Why do we say 'which has no substitute consonant in the reduplicate'? Observe चकाणतुः, चकाणुः, जघ्नतुः, जघ्नुः, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः ॥ The substitution referred to here must be caused by the affixes of the Perfect, therefore, the rule will apply to ‹?› and ‹?› though ‹?› and ‹?› are the roots, and ‹?› and ‹?› are changed to ‹?› and ‹?›. The substitution of a consonant or a consonant in the reduplicate, should not be here considered asiddha (VIII. 2. 54, read with VIII. 2. 1.). That substitution will be considered a substitution for the purposes of this sûtra and will make the stem, as is indicated by the special exception made in favor of ‹?› and ‹?› in sûtra VI. 4. 122. 8 दध लट् — दधते, दधेते, दधन्ते ; दधसे ; दधावहे, दधामहे । लिट् — देधे, देधाते, देधिरे ; देधिषे ; देथे, देधिवहे लुट् — दधिता, दधितारौ, दधितारः । लृट् — दधिष्यते । लोट् — दधताम्, दधस्व, दधै ॥
लङ्—अदधत, अदधाताम्, अदधन्त ; अदधथाः, अदध्वम् अदधावहि ।
विधिलिङ्—दधीत, दधीयाताम्, दधीध्वम्, दधीवहि ॥
आशीर्लिङ्—दधिषीष्ट ।
अददिष्ट, अदधिषाताम् ; अददिष्टः, अददिषि ।
लृङ्—अददिष्यत ॥

9. स्कुदि “to jump, to raise or lift.” The i in स्कुदि is indicatory and by the following न् is inserted.
Note :—According to Tarangini, the root means, 1. आप्लवनम्, or 2. उत्प्लवनम् or 3. उदयनम् ॥ According to Bhoja, it means उद्धरणम् also.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2262. न् is added after the vowel of the root, in a root which has an indicatory इ in the Dhatupatha.

Thus स्कुन्द + शप् + ते = स्कुन्दते, स्कुन्दसे, स्कुन्दे ॥ Perfect :—पुस्कुन्दे, पुस्कुन्दषे, पुस्कुन्दध्वे । लुट्—स्कुन्दिता । लृट्—स्कुन्दिष्यते ॥ लोट्—स्कुन्दताम् ॥ लङ्—अस्कुन्दत । विधिलिङ्—स्कुन्देत ॥ आशीर्लिङ्—स्कुन्दिषीष्ट ॥ लुङ्—अस्कुन्दिष्ट ॥ लृङ्—अस्कुन्दिष्यत ।

10. विदि “to become white.” It is an Intransitive verb. Thus Pres. विन्दते ; Per. विविन्दे ॥

11. वदि “to salute, to praise, to worship.” Pres. वन्दते, Per. ववन्दे ; लुट् वन्दिता &c.
Note :—प्रह्वतिपूर्वभाषणं is अभिवादनम् । Noun वन्दः = पूजकः ॥

12. भदि “to tell a good news, to be fortunate, to be glad, to honor, to shine.” Pres. भन्दते, Per. बभन्दे, लुट्—भन्दिता &c.
Note:—Noun भद्र “auspicious,” भद्रा “shaving.”

13. नदि 'to praise, to rejoice, be glad, to be drunk, or be proud, to sleep or be lazy, to shine, to move (slowly),' मदे 'to be languid,' and जये 'to be victorious.' It is Intransitive except when meaning 'to praise' or 'to move.'
Pres. नन्दते, Per. ननन्दे ॥ लुट् नन्दिता ॥ Nouns :—नन्दथुः ; नन्दनः, नन्दी, नन्दा ।

14. स्पदि “to throb, vibrate.” It is Intransitive.
Pres. स्पन्दते, Per. पस्पन्दे (VII. 4. 61 §. 2259); लुट् स्पन्दिता ॥ Nouns :—स्पन्दः, स्पन्दनः ॥

15. क्लिदि “to grieve, lament.” This is a Transitive verb. Pres. क्लिन्दते चैत्रम् 'he laments for Chaitra.' Per. चिक्लिन्दे ॥

16. मुद “to rejoice.” Pres. मोदते ॥ Per. मुमुदे । No guna because of (I. 2. 5).
मोदते, मोदसे, मोदे ।
लिट्—मुमुदे, मुमुदाते, मुमुदिषे, मुमुदिध्वे ॥
लुट्—मोदिता ॥ लृट्—मोदिष्यते ॥ लोट्—मोदताम् ।
लङ्—अमोदत । विधिलिङ्—मोदेत ॥ आशीर्लिङ्—मोदिषीष्ट ॥
लुङ्—अमोदिष्ट ॥ लृङ्—अमोदिष्यत ॥
Nouns :—मोदनः ; मोदः ; मोदिरः ; मोदमानः ; मोदा ।

17. दद 'to give, present.' Pres. ददते, Per. देदे — But this is a wrong form, as the following sutra applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2263. ए is not substituted for the अ of शस्, दद्, or of roots beginning with व्, or of such verbal stems in which the अ results through the substitution of Guna, though the affixes of the Perfect being कित् or ङित् follow, or the set थल्, nor is the reduplicate elided.

Thus (विशशसतुः, विशशसुः, विशशसिथ) दददे, दददाते, दददिरे ॥ लट् । ददते, ददेते, ददन्ते ॥ लिट्—दददे, दददाते, दददिरे, दददिषे ॥ लुट् ददिता । लृट् ददिष्यते ॥ लोट् ददताम् ॥ लङ् अददत । विधिलिङ् ददेत ॥ आशीर्लिङ् ददिषीष्ट । लुङ् अददिष्ट ॥ लृङ् अददिष्यत ॥
(Of roots beginning with व् :— ववनतुः, ववतुः, ववनिथ ॥ Of roots where अ is the result of guna, विववरतुः, विववरुः, विववरिथ, लुलविथ, पोपथिथ ॥ गुणशब्देन निर्वृत्तस्यात एवेह ग्रहणान्न तु सवर्णदीर्घे कृत आकारस्य चायमकार इति रत्वं प्रतिषिध्यते ॥)
The अ of Guna may result either from the guna of ऋ changed to अर्, or of उ changed to ओ again changed to अव् as—लव ॥

18. ष्वद, 19 ष्वर्द “to taste, to be liked, be sweet, be pleasant to the taste; to sweeten.” This root is Transitive when meaning “to experience” i. e. to taste, and it is Intransitive when meaning “liking” i. e. to be liked. According to Kshiraswami it means “to choose.” Transitive; as स्वदतेऽन्नम् 'he tastes food' ॥ It is Parasmaipadi here as a Vaidic Irregularity. Intransitive, as स्वदते सर्पिर्देवदत्ताय “curd is pleasant to the taste of Devadatta.”
It is conjugated regularly. The initial ष् in ष्वद् is changed to स् by the following :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2264. There is the substitution of स् in the room of the ष्, being the initial of a verbal root as enunciated in the Dhatupatha.

Therefore ष्वद् is changed to स्वद्, and this is not again changed to ष्, because of the prohibition of sutra VIII. 3. 111. §. 2128. Thus अनुस्वदते ।
लिट् :—तस्वदे ॥ Similarly स्वर्दते, तस्वर्दे ॥ Generally the root स्वद is preceded by the upasarga आ, as आस्वदते ‹?› ।

20. ऊर्द 'to measure, to play.' By force of च 'and,' this root also means 'to taste.' According to Sanmati, the word मान does not mean 'measure' but for happiness, and “to be cheerful or easy.”

Thus ऊर्द + शप् + ते ॥ Here applies the following sutra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2265. The short इ or उ of a root is lengthened, when the verb has र् or व् as its penultimate letter, and is followed by a consonant.

* The anuvritti of दीर्घः is current from the preceding Ashtadhyayi sutra.
The root must end in a consonant, and must have र् or व् as preceding such consonant, for the application of this rule.

Therefore the उ is lengthened. Thus we have.
ऊर्दते ; लिट् :—ऊर्दाञ्चक्रे । लुट् ऊर्दिता । लृट् ऊर्दिष्यते । लोट् ऊर्दताम् । लङ्—और्दत । विधिलिङ्—ऊर्देत । आशीर्लिङ्—ऊर्दिषीष्ट । लुङ्—और्दिष्ट । लृङ्—और्दिष्यत ॥
21. कूर्द, 22. खूर्द, 23. गूर्द, 24. गुद । In Kaiyyata, Purushakara and Maitreya the root ‹?› is not found. In Sanmati, Amogha, Vistara and Chandra all the first three roots are given. In Charaka ‹?› is taken as one word meaning 'free.' But according to Maitreya and Kasyapa, ‹?› is a separate root. So all the four roots mean "to play." The force of च here implies that roots have numerous meanings, but here one meaning alone is to be taken, namely "to play."

Thus कूर्दते, चकूर्दे ; खूर्दते ; गूर्दते ; गुदते, जुगुदे ॥

In future the words लट् &c. will often be omitted. It is to be understood that the words are arranged in that order. As, 1. कूर्दते, 2. चकूर्दे ; 3. कूर्दिता, 4. कूर्दिष्यते ; 5. कूर्दताम् ; 6. अकूर्दत, 7. कूर्देत, 8. कूर्दिषीष्ट, 9. अकूर्दिष्ट, 10. अकूर्दिष्यत ॥

25. षूदँ "to flow, effuse, pour out, distil." It is an Intransitive verb in these senses. When meaning 'to strike, hurt, wound, kill, destroy,' it is Transitive, as formed by घञ् of III. 1. 134. S. 2896. The causative has the additional sense of "to cook, dress, season, prepare." As सूदयति (संस्करोति) । So also अहोरात्राणि नस्तो विलिष्टं सूदन्तु (= द्राढं कुर्वन्तु) । Thus सूदते, Per. सुषूदे, ॥ लुट् = सूदिता । Noun सूद: "a cook, a morass."

NOTE:—Why do we say 'initial' in the preceding sutra 2264? Observe— कर्षति, कृषति ॥ Why have these roots been exhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial ष, when for all practical purposes this ष is to be replaced by स, would it not have been easier to spell at once these words with a स? This appears cumbersome no doubt, but the spelling of the roots with ष is for the sake of brevity. Certain roots change their स into ष when preceded by certain letters: those roots which thus change their letter for ष have been at once taught with an initial ष, and thus by VIII. 3. 59 their स is changed to ष. Thus from षिच् instead of ‹?› we have ‹?› । This root is exhibited in the Dhatupatha with a ष, and thus we know that the स must be changed to ष. Otherwise a list of such roots would have to be separately given. One must refer to the Dhatupatha for a list of the roots beginning with ष ; As a general rule, however, all monosyllabic roots beginning with a स and followed by a vowel or a dental letter have been taught in the Dhatupatha as beginning with an initial ष, as well as the following roots, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, and ‹?› though followed by ‹?› or ‹?›. The following roots though followed by a vowel or dental are not taught with an initial ष viz. ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?›, ‹?› ॥

The "dental" here means the dental pure and simple. i. e. त, थ, द, ध, न and not dento-labial व । This we infer from the inclusion of स्वद &c. in the list, which are followed by व । Had व been included in the terms "dental" there was no necessity of teaching स्वद &c. separately.

NOTE :—To complete the description of verbs, we shall anticipate matter and give under each root its various derivative roots also, such as the Passive stem, the Causative (णिच्), the Desiderative (सन्), the Intensive with यङ् and the Intensive without यङ्, (यङ् लुगन्त); as well as some Krit derivatives where necessary. In this we have followed the Madhaviya Dhatuvritti. We repeat therefore, the conjugation of the twenty five roots already taught.

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2266. The s is dropped after the augment iṭ, if after this s the augment īṭ follows.

Thus āt + iṣ + s + īt = āt + i + 0 + īt.

Now this s is elided by VIII. 2. 28 (the present sūtra) of the Tripādī (the last three sections or Pādas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī).

This elision would, therefore, be asiddha for the purposes of ekādeśa (VI. 1. 101 S. 85), and we could not combine the i of iṣ with the long ī as the zero intervenes. So the form would be ‹?› as in case of sūtra VIII. 3. 19 S. 67; for VIII. 2. 1 S. 12 applies. To prevent this anomaly, we have the following vārtika:—

Vārt:— When ekādeśa is to be done, the elision of sic is to be considered siddha or valid. As आतीत् । Here the sic is elided by ईटि (VIII. 2. 28). This elision is considered valid or siddha, and thus we have dīrgha single substitution of ī for i + 0 + ī in āt + i + 0 + īt = आतीत् ॥

This elision of s takes place when it is situated between iṣ on one side and īṭ on the other. When there is not īṭ following, there is no elision. आतीष्टाम्, अतिषुः ।

The above examples आतीत्, आतीष्टाम् and अतिषुः may be either with or without a. The question is what is the true form of the Aorist without the augment a; is it अतीत् or आतीत्? According to the next sūtra it might have been आतीत्, but that sūtra is set aside by the sūtra following it.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2267. In the Parasmaipada s-Aorist there is Vṛiddhi of the a of vad, and vraj, and of any vowel, without distinction, of the stems ending in a consonant.

Note:— As, अवादीत्, आव्राजीत् । This debars the option in the case of these two roots, which would have otherwise obtained by VII. 2. 7. So also of stems ending in consonants: as अयाक्षीत्, अभैत्सीत्, अच्छैत्सीत्, अरोत्सीत् ॥

The root अत is a हलन्त root and therefore, there would be Vṛiddhi of अ into आ. But the application of this sūtra is prevented by the following sūtra:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2268. The vowel of a stem, ending in a consonant, does not get Vṛiddhi, when the sic takes the augment iṭ.

Therefore we do not get the form आतीत्, but अतीत्; because the sic here takes the augment iṭ.

Thus without the augment we have the forms: मा भवानतीत् or मा भवान् अतिष्ट, मा भवान् अतिषुः । The augment a is elided after mā. The form is therefore really a + atīt and not a + ātīt.

Pre. अतति । Per. आत, आतुः, आतुः, अतिथ । I Fut. अतिता । II Fut. अतिषिष्यति । Imp. अततु । Imper. आतत् । Pot. अतेत् । Bene. अत्यात् । Aorist अतीत्, अतिष्टाम्, अतिषुः (without a). Condi. अतिष्यत् ।

Pass. Per. आते । I Fut. अतिता । II Fut. अतिषिष्यते । Imp. अतात । Imper. आतत । Pot. अतेत । Bene. s. अतिषीष्ट, d. अतिषीयास्ताम्, pl. अतिषीरन् । Caus. आतयति । Desi. अतिचिषति । Past. Part. Pass. अतितः । Nouns: आतिः 'a kind of bird', पत्तिः 'infantry', अश्विनी 'an asterism', अतिथिः 'a guest', अनिलः 'air', पतत्त्री 'bird'.

चिती ३९ संज्ञाने । विचेष्टितः ॥

39. √ Chiti, 'to perceive, see, notice, observe', 'to know', 'to understand', 'to remember'; 'to think'.

Pre. — चेतति । Per. चिचेत, चिचिततुः, चिचितुः ; चिचेतिथ, चिचिथ, चिचितथुः, चिचित । I Fut. चेतिता । II Fut. चेतिष्यति । Imp. चेततु । Imper. अचेतत् । Pot. चेतेत् । Bene. चित्यात् । Aor. अचेतीत्, अचेतिष्टाम्, अचेतिषुः । Condi. अचेतिष्यत् । Caus. चेतयति, Aor. अचीचितत् । Desi. चिचेतिषति or चिचितिषति
Inten. चेकेत्यते । Yan luk चेकेतीति or चेकेत्ति । Past Part. चित्तः, चित्तवान् । Ger. चित्त्वा or चेतित्वा । Nouns चेतनः, चित्, चेतः, चेतन्ती, चैतन्यम् ॥

च्युतिर् ४० आसेचने । सेचनमार्द्रीकरणम् । आङीषदर्थेऽभिव्याप्तौ च ॥
* इरित्संज्ञा वाच्या * । श्च्योतति । चुश्च्योत ॥

40. √ Chyutir, to sprinkle. सेचन means to sprinkle, to wet. The prefix आङ् has the force of 'a little,' or 'pervasion.' आसेचन therefore means to wet a little or 'to wet thoroughly.'

Vartika:—The whole portion इर् whenever it occurs at the end of a root is to be treated as इत् । Thus Pre. श्च्योतति । Per. चुश्च्योत ॥

As this root has an indicatory ‹?›, the effect of it is that in the Aorist, it has another form also, where च्लि is replaced by अङ् and there is consequently no guna. The Sutra which causes this is the following:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2269. अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि after that root which has an indicatory इर्, when the Parasmaipada terminations are employed.

NOTE:—Thus from छिदिर् (छिद्) 'to divide,' we derive, अच्छिदत्, or with सिच् अच्छैत्सीत् । But we have अच्छित्त in the Atmanepada. So from भिदिर्—अभिदत्, or अभैत्सीत् ।

Similarly च्युतिर्, has its Aorist either as अच्योतीत्, or अच्युतत्, with अङ् affix.

40. √ Chyutir, to sprinkle, to wet. Pre.—श्च्योतति । Per. चुश्च्योत । च्योतति । चुच्योति । I Fut. श्च्योतिता । II Fut. श्च्योतिष्यति । Imp. अश्च्योतत् । Pot. श्च्योतेत् । Bene. श्च्युत्यात् । Aorist अच्युतत्, or अच्योतीत् । Pass. श्च्युत्यते । Caus. श्च्योतयति । Aor. अचुश्च्योतत् । Desi. चुश्च्योतिषति or चुश्च्युतिषति । Inten. चोश्च्युत्यते । Yan luk चोश्च्योतीति or चोश्च्योत्ति । Past Part. Pass. श्च्युतितः or श्च्योतितः । Ger. श्च्योतित्वा ।

41. √ Schyutir, 'to trickle, ooze, exude, flow;' 'to shed, pour out, diffuse, scatter.' Pre. श्च्योतति । Per. चुश्च्योत &c. like च्युत् । Aor. अच्युतत्, with अङ्, or अच्योतीत् ॥

Some read this root without स्, namely as च्युतिर् । Then the conjugation will be च्योतति &c. As in मधुश्च्युतं घृतमिव सुपूतम् ॥

NOTE:—The whole portion इर् is indicatory, and not इ and र् separately. They can be made separately also by उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् (I. 3. 2. S. 3); which will make इ indicatory; and by हलन्त्यम् (I. 3. 3. S. 1) which will make र् indicatory. This is done actually by Madhava in his Dhatuvritti. But the objection to it is that if र् be taken separately as indicatory, then there should be an insertion of nasal by इदितो नुम् धातोः (VII. 1. 58. S. ‹?›).

42. [भासने 'to shine'].
Similarly should be conjugated the root ‹?› । This root is not given in the Siddhanta.

43. Mantha, 'to churn,' to agitate, shake, stir round or up, to crush, to grind down, oppress, afflict, destroy, kill. Pre. मन्थति । Per. ममन्थ, ममन्थिथ । I Fut. मन्थिना । II Fut. मन्थिष्यति । Imp. अमन्थत् । Imper. अमन्थत् । Pot. मन्येत् । Bene. मथ्यात् ॥

In the Benedictive, the n of मन्थ is elided, because the affix यासुट् is कित् by III. 4. 104 S. 2216; and because it is कित् it causes the elision of न् by VI. 4. 24 S. 415. Had the root been read as मथि, there would have been no elision of the nasal. In fact, there is such a root also, as given below. See Root 47.

Aor. अमन्थीत् । Cond. अमन्यिष्यत् । Passive मध्यते । Causative मन्धयति । Aor. अममन्थत् । Desiderative मिमन्थिषति । Inten. मामथ्यते । Yan luk मामन्थीति or मामन्ति । Imperfect अमामन् । Gerund मथित्वा or मन्धित्वा । Nouns:—मन्थः, मन्थनी ॥

This root takes two accusatives, as सुधां क्षीरनिधिं मथ्नाति ॥

44 √ Kuthi, 45 √ Puthi, 46 √ Luthi, 47 √ Mathi, 'to hurt, to suffer pain, to injure, to strike, to kill, to be afflicted, to crush, to grind down, to oppress.' Pre. कुन्थति । Per. चुकुन्थ &c. like मन्थ as given above. In the Benedictive (आशीर्लिङ्) however, there will be no elision of the nasal. As कुन्ध्यात् ; पुन्ध्यात् &c.

Similarly लुन्थति, पुन्थति and मन्थति । Both roots मथि and मन्थ are read here, according to Saumata. Kshiraswami reads it समन्थे and not मथि even here, and gives the example मन्थ्नाति । All these roots mean 'to injure.' As शत्रुमभिकुन्थति, मारयति ॥

48. √ Shidha, 'to go, to ward, to drive.' Some read this with an indicatory short उ । The initial ष् is changed to स् by धात्वादेः षः सः (VI. 1. 64 S. 2264). Pre. सेधति । Per. सिषेध, सिषिधिथ; सिषेधिथ । I Fut. सेधिता । II Fut. सेधिष्यति । Imp. असेधत् । Pot. सेधेत् । Ben. सिध्यात् । Aor. असेधीत् । Cond. असेधिष्यत् ।

Passive सिध्यते । Causative Pre. सेधयति, Aor. असीषिधत् । Desiderative सिषिधिषति or सिषेधिषति । Intensive सेषिध्यते । Yan luk सेषेधीति or सेषेत्ति । Gerund सेधित्वा or सिधित्वा । Nouns सेधः 'a kind of tree,' सिद्धम् and सिद्धयन्तः ।

When an upasarga like नि is added we have नि+सेधति । The question arises should स् be changed to ष after नि ? The Sutra VIII. 3. 111, S. 2125 requires that there should be no substitution, since सेधति is the beginning of a Pada. To this, however, the following sutra makes an exception. That sutra (VIII. 3. 65) and the five sutras that follow it in the order of Ashtadhyayi are given together here once for all, to show when स् should be changed to ष, not only in the case of षिध् but of other verbs also:

Thus नि+षेधति=निषेधति (see below).
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2270. ष is substituted for स, after an alterant इ and उ of an upasarga in the following verbs: षु (सुनोति), सू (सुवति), सो (स्यति VII. 3. 71), स्तु (स्तौति VII. 3. 89), स्तुभ् (स्तोभते), स्था, सेनय (Denominative), सिध् (सेधति), सिच्, सञ्ज् and स्वञ्ज् ॥

Thus सुषोति । सुषाव, प्रसुषाव । स्यति, अभिष्यति । स्तु, अभिष्टौति । स्तुभ्, अभिष्टोभते । स्था, अभिष्ठास्यति । सेनय, अभिषेणयति । सेध, अभिषेधति, परिषेधति, पर्यषेधत् । सिच्, अभिषिञ्चति । सञ्ज्, अभिषजति । स्वञ्ज्, परिष्वजते ॥

NOTE:—The root सिध् is exhibited in the sutra as सेध with vikarana, thus debarring षिधु—सिध्यति ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2271. The स of ष्वष्क is changed to ष after an Upasarga having an इ or उ, but not after प्रति ॥

Thus परिष्यष्कति, प्रणिष्यष्कति, निषष्वाष्क, सुष्वष्क । The second ष् remains unchanged in the Perfect by VIII. 3. 118.

Why do we say 'but not after प्रति' ? Observe प्रतिष्वष्कति ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2272. The s of स्तम्भ (read in sutra III. 1. 82 S. 2555.) is changed into ष after an upasarga, having an i or u. Thus अभिष्टम्भाति । परिष्टम्भाति । The word अप्रतेः of the last sûtra is not to be read here. Hence we have forms like:— प्रतिष्टम्भाति । ‹?› । ‹?› The present sûtra is made a separate rule, when it could well have been included in the immediately preceding one, as सदिस्तम्भोः for two reasons. First that the anuvritti of स्तम्भ alone should run into the next sûtra. Secondly that it should not be restricted by the word अप्रतेः । प्रतिष्टम्भनः ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2273. The स् of स्तम्भ is changed into ष after the preposition अव in the sense of 'support' and 'contiguity.'
Note:—The word 'आलम्बन' means 'support, refuge, that upon which anything depends or leans,' 'अविदूर' means 'the state of not being दूर or far off, i.e. to be contiguous.'
Thus अवष्टभ्यास्ते 'He remains leaning upon a staff &c.,' अवष्टभ्य तिष्ठति ।
So also in the sense of to be near, as अवष्टब्धा सेना 'the army near at hand,' ‹?› । See V. 2. 13.
अवष्टभ्यास्ते—मित्वा सन् समीपे चास्ते ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2274. The ष is substituted for the स of स्वन्, after वि and अव, when the sense is 'to smack while eating.'
Thus विष्टनति, विष्टणति, विष्टनायते, अवष्टनति, अवष्टणति, अवष्टनायते । That is, he makes sound while eating, he eats with a smack.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2275. [ष] is substituted for the स of सेव्, सित, सय, सिवु, सह, the augment सुट्, स्तु and स्वञ्ज्, after the prepositions परि, नि, and वि.
Thus निषेधति । The root षेवृ 'to serve' belongs to the Bhvâdi class. The सित is the Past Participle of षिञ् बन्धने, and सय is the noun derived from the same root with the affix अच्; सिवु is a Divâdi root.
Note:—The root सित of this rule is an important landmark. All roots enumerated in the sutras VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70 change their स to ष even when the augment अट् intervenes, but not so the root सित and those that follow it. This is taught in the next sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2276. (The substitution of ष, for स्, as taught hereinbefore will take place) for all roots up to सित exclusive in VIII. 3. 70 even when the augment अट् intervenes (between the स and the alterant letter).
This sûtra governs all the fifteen roots given in the preceding sutras from VIII. 3. 65. Thus with the augment अट् we have न्यषेधत् in the Imperfect, न्यषेधीत् in the Aorist and न्यषेधिष्यत् in the Conditional.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2277. In स्या &c. up to सित exclusive (VIII. 3. 65 to VIII. 3. 70), this ष substitution takes place then also, when the reduplicate intervenes, and the स of the reduplicate is also changed to ष.
Thus सिषेध, सिषिधतुः in the Perfect.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2278. The स् of the verb षेध is not changed to ष when the meaning is that of moving.
This is an exception to VIII. 3. 65 S. 2270. Thus गङ्गां विसेधति ।
षिधू ४९ शास्त्रे माङ्गल्ये च । शास्त्रं शासनम् ।
49. Şhidha, 'To ordain, command, instruct,' 'to turn out well or auspiciously'. शास्त्र means command, rule. This root has an indicatory long ऊ, the force of which is given in the next sûtra. It is conjugated like the preceding root ‹?› No. 48 except in so far as the effect of the indicatory ऊ makes the change.
लुट्—सेधिता । लृट्—सेधिष्यति ।
In the 2nd Person Dual we have सिषिधथुः with the augment इट् added to थुस्.
But this augment is optional, owing to the root having an indicatory ऊ as given below.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2279. A Valâdi-Ârdhadhâtuka affix optionally takes 'iṭ' after svṛi, after the two roots 'sû' (sûti and sûyati), after 'dhûñ' and after a root which has an indicatory long 'û'.
Thus सिषेध् + थ । Now applies the next sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2280. 'Dha' is substituted for 'ta' or 'tha' coming after 'jha', 'bha', 'gha', 'ḍha' or 'dha' (jhash), but not after the root dhâ (dadh).
Note:—Thus from लभ्, we have लब्धा, लब्धुम्, लब्धव्यम्, अलब्ध, अलप्सत ॥
Thus सिषेध् + थ = सिषेध् + ध = सिषेद्ध । The other form is सिषेधिथ । सिषिधतुः or सिषिध्यतुः । लुट्—सेधिता or सोद्धा । लृट्—सेधिष्यति or सेत्स्यति । लोट्—सेधतु । लुङ्—असैत्सीत् ।
In the 3rd Person Dual we have असेध् + स् + ताम् । Now applies the next sûtra, which causes the elision of स् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2281. The 's' is elided when it is preceded by a jhal consonant (any consonant except semi-vowels and nasals), and is followed by an affix beginning with a jhal consonant.
Thus असेध् + स् + ताम् = असेद्धाम् ॥
Therefore the full conjugation in Aorist is:—
Singular Dual Plural.
Third Person असेत्सीत् असेद्धाम् असेत्सुः
Second Person असेत्सीः असेद्धम् असेद्ध
First Person असेत्सम् असेत्स्व असेत्स्म
Second Form.
Third Person असेधीत् असेधिष्टाम् असेधिषुः
Second Person असेधीः असेधिष्टम् असेधिष्ट
First Person असेधिषम् असेधिष्व असेधिष्म
The Desiderative is सिषेधिषति ॥
50. 'to eat. The ‹?› is indicatory.
51.
The force of the indicatory ‹?› is that we have no shortening of the penultimate in ‹?› ॥ Desiderative : चिखादिषति । Intensive : चाखाद्यते । Yaṅ-luk चाखादीति or ‹?› । Causative : खादयति । Past Participle खादितः । Noun खादकः ॥ 51. खद् 'to be steady, firm,' 'to strike, hurt, kill.' By the force of the word 'and,' it means 'to eat' also. It is Intransitive when meaning 'to be firm,' — लट्—खदति । लिट्—चखाद । Here we have caused the Vṛiddhi of the अ of खद् by the following sūtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2282. In a stem ending in a consonant with an 'a' immediately preceding it, the Vṛiddhi is substituted for such 'a' when an affix having an indicatory 'ñ' or 'ṇ' follows. Therefore खद् + णल् = चखाद ॥ In the First Person singular, however, this Vṛiddhi is optional by the next sūtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2283. The ending of the First Person Singular in the Perfect optionally acts as ṇit. The Vṛiddhi is optional, as चखाद or चखद ॥ The other Tenses are conjugated like खाद । In the Aorist (लुङ्) there are two forms caused by the following :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2284. Before an 'iṭ' beginning 's'-Aorist of the Parasmaipada, the short 'a' of the root gets optionally Vṛiddhi, when the stem begins with a consonant, and the 'a' is prosodially short by being followed by a simple consonant. Thus अखादीत् or अखदीत् ॥ Causative : खादयति । Intensive अशाखाद्यते । Nouns : खादिः ॥ 52. बद (ब्) 'to be steady, firm.' The ब is the labial b, and not व or v. लिट्—बबाद, बेदतुः, बेदिथ, बबाद or बबद । लुङ्—अबादीत् or अबदीत् ॥ Its conjugation is like खाद । In the Perfect we have ‹?› as the root in reduplication retains ब without any change. So there is एत्त्व as well as the reduplication elision. Nouns :— बदरं, बदरी ॥ Maitreya reads this root as बन्द । He forms बेदतुः by eliding न, and then एत्त्व and elision of reduplication. This is incorrect, according to Mādhava : because the root being संयोगान्त (ending in a conjunct consonant) like अञ्च् &c., the endings of the perfect are not कित् । There is another root ‹?› given further on. 53. गद 'to speak.' लट्—गदति । लिट्—जगाद । लुट्—गदिता &c. like खाद । But in प्र+नि+गदति, we have the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2285. The 'ṇ' is the substitute of 'n' of the prefix 'ni' following a cause for such change standing in an upasarga, when these verbs follow, namely, 1. gad 'to speak,' 2. nad 'to be happy,' 3. pat 'to fall,' 4. pad 'to go,' 5. the six ghu verbs, 6. mā 'to measure,' 7. sho 'to destroy,' 8. han 'to kill,' 9. yā 'to go,' 10. vā 'to blow,' 11. drā 'to flee,' 12. psā 'to eat,' 13. vap 'to weave,' 14. vah 'to bear,' 15. śam 'to be tranquil,' 16. chi 'to collect' and 17. dih 'to anoint.' Thus 1. गद्, प्रणिगदति । 2. नद्, प्रणिनदति । 3. पत्, प्रणिपतति । 4. पद्, प्रणिपद्यते । 5. The six roots called ghu. प्रणिददाति, प्रणिदधाति, प्रणिदेति, प्रणिद्यति, प्रणिधयति, प्रणिधायति । 6. माङ्, प्रणिमिमीते । मेङ्, प्रणिमयते । Iṣhṭi :—By the word मा in the sūtra, both verbs माङ् and मेङ् are to be taken and not the roots सो or मि or मा माने, for they also take the form मा by VI. 1. 50. 7. स्यति, प्रणिष्यति । 8. हन्ति, प्रणिहन्ति । 9. याति, प्राणियाति । 10. वाति, प्रणिवाति । 11. द्राति, प्रणिद्राति । 12. प्साति, प्रणिप्साति । The last five roots belong to the Adādi class. 13. वपति, प्रणिवपति । 14. वहति, प्रणिवहति । 15. शाम्यति, प्राणिशाम्यति (VII. 3. 74). 16. चिनोति, प्रणिचिनोति । 17. देग्धि, प्रणिदेग्धि । Iṣhṭi :—The above change takes place even when the augment अट् intervenes, as प्राण्यगदत्, प्राणिनदत् ॥ The root स्यति &c., are exhibited in their conjugated form in the sūtra, in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to yaṅ-luk form of these roots (VII. 4. 85). Therefore not here :—प्रनिखागदीति, प्रनिमामदीति, प्रनिलेढीति &c. Thus जगदतुः । लिट्—जगदतुः &c. Noun :—गदः, निगदः, निगादः ॥ 54. रद 'To split, rend, scratch, gnaw, dig.' Vilekhana means 'division' or 'breaking.' लट्—रदति । लिट्—रराद, रेदतुः, रेदिथ &c., like the preceding. Noun :—रदः ॥ 55. णद 'To utter inarticulate sound.' The root is exhibited with an initial ण । This nasal is changed to n by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2286. There is the substitution of 'n' for the initial 'ṇ' of the root in the Dhātupāṭha. All roots beginning with n should be understood to have been so taught with the exception of the following eight roots नर्द, नाटि, नाथ, नाधृ, नन्द, नक्क, नॄ and नृत् ॥ Note :—The roots नर्द शब्द (I. 57) and नर्द अवस्यन्दने (X. 12) belong to the Bhvādi and Churādi class respectively. The root नट नृत्तौ (I. 818) belonging to the ghaṭādi (VI. 4. 92, S. 2568) is not to be taken; as the root is exhibited with a long ā as nāṭi in the above verse, while the ghaṭādi naṭ being mit is incapable of assuming the lengthened form nāṭi in the Causative by VI. 4. 92, S. 2568. Therefore that naṭ should be taken which can assume the form nāṭi. Note :—The roots नाथ् and नाध् 'to beg' &c. have already been mentioned before. ‹?› are the other roots. According to some the root ‹?› is to be read as ‹?›; and so also the roots ‹?› as ‹?›. Only five roots are thus left, which begin with न in the Dhātupāṭha, namely नर्द, नट्, नाट्, नाथ and ‹?› ॥ Conjugation of णद 'to sound, resound, thunder.' लट्—नदति ॥ लिट्—ननाद, नेदतुः, नेदुः । नेदिथ, नेदथुः, नेद, ननाद or ननद, नेदिव, नेदिम ॥ लुट्—नदिता । लृट्—नदिष्यति । लेट्—नादिषति, नादिति । लोट्—नदतु, अनदत् । विधिलिङ्—नदेत् । लुङ्—अनादीत् or अनदीत् ॥ When preceded by an upasarga, the न is changed to ण by the following :—

Because by the context, the anuvṛitti of the word pûrvapada which is current throughout this sub-division, would have been understood in this sûtra also, and the rule would have applied to samâsas only, for there only we have pûrvapada. 2290. इयङ् and उवङ् are substituted for the इ and उ of a reduplicate, before a non-homogenous vowel.
Therefore उ+ओख+अ = उव्+ओख+अ = उवोख । When by Guṇa, the root assumes the form ओख्, it becomes a heavy vowelled root : and the Perfect ought to be formed by the addition of आम् periphrastically by III. 1. 36 S. 2237 but this is not so because of the maxim संनिपात &c. ("that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination." See VII. 1. 9 S. 203). Here उ was changed to ओ by the presence of णल्; and if आम् be added, it will cause the elision of its progenitor अच् by II. 4. 81 S. 2238 which the maxim prevents.
The dual is formed thus उख+उख+अतुस् = उ+उख+अतुस् = ऊखतुः । The Plural is ऊखुः । The affixes being कित्, there is no guṇa, and consequently no उवङ् substitution, as the vowels are now homogenous. This single substitute long ऊ (उ+उ=ऊ) may be considered as the final of the first or the beginning of the second (VI. 1. 85. S. 75). Considering it as final of the first, namely, as the long of the reduplicate (abhyāsa), it requires to be shortened by VII. 4. 59. S. 2180.
[But because the rule of shortening depends upon abhyāsa alone and is therefore antaraṅga, while the savarṇa-lengthening is Bahiraṅga ; as it depends upon two, namely the precedent and the subsequent letters— the maxim "नाजानन्तर्ये बहिष्ट्वप्रक्लृप्तिः" applies (see Vol I. p. 30) : and so it is not shortened. Or].
Pass. Part. कुचितः । कुचितवान् । Gerund कुचित्वा । Similarly is conjugated kruñcha, as क्रुञ्चति &c. Nouns: ‹?›, क्रौञ्चः । The nasal is elided in the Benedictive by VI. 4. 24 S. 415 as कुच्यात् and क्रुच्यात्.

2291. And, optionally aṅ is the substitute of cli after
It is not shortened, because it had already been once shortened before, and "an operation once performed on a stem &c., is not repeated again"—is the maxim that would apply.

Note:—When was the first u shortened? It was shortened by VII. 4. 59, S. 2180 as soon as was reduplicated to उ + उ । But it was already short, how could it be shortened?

Ans. Rules of grammar act like clouds (which rain both on sea and on land though raining on sea is useless). The rule of ह्रस्वः S. 2180 therefore substitutes a short in the place of the already existing short उ. Thus उ + उख + अतुः = उ + उख + अतुः (VII. 4. 59 S. 2180) =

But why should Rule S. 2180 apply first and not the rule of lengthening? In other words, why should we not make उ + उख = ऊख first and then apply the rule of shortening?

The rule of shortening being a rule applicable to anga (or stem) is stronger than the rule of lengthening (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः) on the maxim:

Paribhasha: A rule relating to a stem (anga) is stronger than a rule relating to letters.

Therefore, the ह्रस्वः (S. 2180) applies first.

Another reason for its applying first is that it is subsequent in order to the rule of lengthening.

Thus उ + उ + ख् + अतुः = उ + उख + अतुः (S. 2180 short for short उ) = ऊखतुः (lengthening). Similarly कख् : कखतुः ॥
