शिषि १७४ आघ्राणे । शिङ्घति ॥

170. घघ (गघ्, वघ्) हसने 'to laugh.' As घघति । जघाघ । घघिता । 171. दधि पालने 'to protect.' 172. तधि शोषणे 'to dry.' 173. मधि मण्डने 'to dress.' मंघते (मघ्) । 174. शिषि to smell. शिङ्घति ।

Here end Parasmaipadi roots whose final is a guttural.

SUB-SECTION VI.

Now we take up the roots ending in ch. There are twenty one Atmanepadi roots.

चर्च १७५ दीप्तौ । चर्चते ॥

175. चर्च 'To shine.' लट्—चर्चते । लिट्—चचर्चे । लुट्—चर्चिता । लृट्—चर्चिष्यते । लोट्—चर्चताम् । लङ्—अचर्चत । विधिलिङ्—चर्चेत । आशीर्लिङ्—चर्चिषीष्ट । लुङ्—अचर्चिष्ट । लृङ्—अचर्चिष्यत । Caus. चर्चयति । Aor. अचचर्चत् । Des. चिचर्चिषते । Inten. चाचर्च्यते । Yan luk. चाचर्कीति or चाचर्ति । Aor. अचाचर्कीत्, अचाचर्त् ॥ Noun चर्चः 'vigour,' 'faeces.' ब्रह्मवर्चसम् । Adjective चर्च्यम् ॥

सच १७६ सेचने च । सचते । सेचे । सचिता ॥

176. सच 'to sprinkle, to serve.' लट्—सचते । लिट्—सेचे । लुट्—सचिता । लृट्—सचिष्यते । लोट्—सचताम् । लङ्—असचत । विधिलिङ्—सचेत । आशीर्लिङ्—सचिषीष्ट । लुङ्—असचिष्ट । Caus. सचयति । Aor. अससचत् । Des. सिषाधयिषते (VIII. 3. 61. S. 2627). Yan. सासच्यते । Yan luk. सासक्ति । Noun सक्तुः । सक्तुकः । सचिवः ॥

लोच १७७ दर्शने । लोचते । लुलोचे ॥

177. दर्शने To see. लोचते । लुलोचे । लोचिता । Des. लुलोचिषते । Inten. लोलोच्यते, लोलोचीति, लोलोक्ति ॥ Caus. लोचयति । Aor. अलुलोचत् ॥

शच १७८ व्यक्तायां वाचि । शेचे ॥

178. व्यक्तायां वाचि to speak distinctly. शेचे । शचिता । N. शची ॥

त्वच १७९ श्वचि १८० गतौ । त्वचते ।

179. त्वच \ गतौ To go. त्वचते । चत्वचे । त्वचिता । N. त्वक् ॥
180. श्वचि / श्वञ्चते । शश्वञ्चे । श्वञ्चिता ॥

कच १८१ बन्धने । कचते ॥

181. कच 'to bind.' कचते । चकचे । कचिता । N. कचः, कचाः ॥

कच १८२, काचि १८३, दीप्तिबन्धनयोः । कञ्चते । चकाचे ॥

182. कच \ दीप्तिबन्धनयोः to shine, to bind. कञ्चते । चकचे । कचिता ।
183. काचि / काञ्चते । चकाञ्चे &c. Nouns : कञ्चुकः । काञ्ची । काञ्चनम् ।

मच १८४, मुचि १८५, कल्कने । कल्कनं दम्भः शाठ्यं च । कात्थनम् इत्यन्ये । मञ्चते । मुमुञ्चे ॥

184. मच \ कल्कने to cheat, to be vain. Some say it means to brag or boast
185. मुचि / also. Thus मञ्चते । मेचे । मचिता । मुञ्चते । मुमुञ्चे । मुञ्चिता । According to Chandra the root is मोच—मोचते ॥

मचि १८६ धारणेच्छायपूजनेषु । ममचे ॥

186. मचि (मञ्चते) धारणेच्छायपूजनेषु also दीप्तौ 'to wear, exalt, worship, also glitter.' As मञ्चते &c. Noun मञ्चः । Sakatayana does not read मुचि, but मच and मचि only.

पचि १८७ व्यक्तीकरणे । पञ्चते ॥

187. पचि । To explain. The root डुपचष् 'to cook,' will be taught further on. This is also Churadi. लट्—पञ्चते । Noun पङ्कः 'marsh.' पञ्चन् 'five.'

ष्टुच १८८ प्रसादे । स्तोचते । तुष्टुचे ॥

188. ष्टुच प्रसादे । To be pleased. लट्—स्तोचते । लिट्—तुष्टुचे । लुट्—स्तोचिता । Caus. स्तोचयति । Aor. अतुष्टुचत् । Des. तुष्टुचिषते or तुस्तोचिषते । Inten. तोष्टुच्यते । Yan luk. तोष्टोचीति or तोष्टोक्ति । Noun स्तोकः । Gerund स्तुचित्वा or स्तोचित्वा (I. 2. 26 S. 2617).

ऋजू १८९ गतिस्थानार्जनोपार्जनेषु । भर्जते । नुट्-विधावकारेरेफयोरेकहलत्वेन ज्ञेयम् । तेन द्विहलत्वादिट् । आनृजे ॥

189. ऋजू । To go. 2. stand or be firm, strong, earn or obtain or get. Maitreya gives the meaning of वर्जन also.
लट्—ऋर्जते । लिट्—आनृजे । ऋज् + ऋज् + ए = ऋ + ऋज् + ए (VII. 4. 60. S. 2179) = अर् + ऋज् + ए (VII. 4. 66 S. 2344 read with I. 1. 51). The अ is then elided by VII. 4. 60, S. 2179 and we have आ + [ अ ] + र्ज् + ए = आर्ज् + ए + नुट् (The lengthening by VII. 4. 70. S. 2248, and नुट् by VII. 4. 71. S. 2288) = आनर्जे ॥ For the purposes of adding नुट्, the ऋ is considered to have र् in it so that ऋज् becomes equivalent to र्ज्, so the root is considered to be one which ends in a double-consonant, and thus makes S. 2288 applicable. लुट्—अर्जिता । अर्जिष्यते । लोट्—ऋर्जताम् । लङ्—आर्जत । आशीर्लिङ्—अर्जिषीष्ट । लुङ्—आर्जिष्ट । Inten. अरार्यते । Caus. अर्जयति । Aor. आर्जिजत् । Des. अर्जिजिषते । Gerund अर्जित्वा । Adjective अर्ज्यम् ॥

आजि १९०, भृञी १९१ भर्जने ।
'उपसर्गादृति—' (९४) इति वृद्धिः । प्राजते । प्राञ्चे । प्रानिष्ट । भर्जते । बभ्रज्जे ॥

190 आजि, 191 भृञी । To parch. The root भृञ् has a long ऋ as indicatory.
प्र + आजते = प्राजते, with प्र, the vriddhi is by VI. 1. 91. S. 74. लिट्—प्राञ्चे । Or प्रावृञ्चे according to Sammata and Tarangini. But this is wrong. नुट् लट्—भर्जते । लिट्—बभ्रज्जे ।
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
अजेर्वीत्ययमादेशः स्यादार्धधातुकविषये घञमपं च वर्जयित्वा । विवाय । विव्यतुः । विव्युः । अत्र वकारस्य हल्परत्वात् 'उपधायां च' (२२४५) इति दीर्घे प्राप्ते— 'अचः परस्मिन्—' (५०) इति स्थानिवद्भावेनाच्परत्वम् । न च 'न पदान्त—' (५१) इति प्रतिषेधे प्राप्ते— 'स्वरदीर्घयलोपेषु लोपाजादेश एव न स्थानिवत्' इत्युक्तेः न प्रतिषेधः । 'एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्' (२२६५) इति दीर्घे प्राप्ते— 'इडादावर्धधातुके वेष्यते' । 2292. वी is the substitute of the verb अज् 'to drive, lead,' when an Ārdhadhātuka affix follows, with the exception of the affixes घञ् (III. 3. 18) and अप् (III. 3. 69).
Ishti:—The substitution is optional before ârdhadhâtukas beginning with a letter of Pratyâhâra val (all consonants except y). As ‹?›

In viyatuḥ and viyuḥ the ‹?› is changed to ‹?› before atuḥ and us. The equation now stands thus viy + atuḥ. Here the root has a penultimate letter य which is followed by a consonant; therefore the i of viy ought to be lengthened by VIII. 2. 78 S. 2265. But it is not so, because the y, substitute for ‹?›, is considered sthânivat to ‹?›, by I. 1. 51, S. 50, for the purposes of S. 2265. y being as ‹?›, the penultimate is not considered to be followed by a consonant but by a vowel, and hence S. 2265 cannot apply. Obj.:—But the rule VIII. 2. 78, S. 2265 is a dīrgha-vidhi, as it ordains lengthening and therefore the substitute of ‹?› will not be sthânivat by I. 1. 51. S. 50; because that rule must be read with the proviso of I. 1. 58 S. 51 which declares inter alia that for the purposes of dīrgha-vidhi the âdeśa is not sthânivat, so there ought to be lengthening of viy.

Ans:—The following vârttika makes a counter-exception to that rule of S. 51.

Vârt:—For the application of the rules of accent (svara-vidhi), or the rules of lengthening (dīrgha-vidhi) or the rule of the elision of ya (ya-lopa-vidhi), the lopa-substitute only of a vowel is to be considered as not sthânivat, and not any other substitute. Here the substitute is y and not lopa; and so is considered sthânivat to ‹?›.

In forming the Second Person Singular, we have aj + thal = vi + â + thal = ‹?›. Now applies the prohibition of S. 2246 debarring the augment इट्. But the following sûtra makes an exception.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2293. The Personal endings of the Perfect do not get the augment इट् after कृ, सृ, भृ, वृ, स्तु, द्रु, स्रु, श्रु ॥

The four roots, कृ, सृ, भृ, and वृ are taken in order to make a restriction with regard to them. Every prohibition of इट् augment whether depending on any particular final, or depending on any particular affix, if that prohibition is to apply to the Perfect, then it applies only to the four roots kṛ &c. mentioned here, and not to other roots.

As regards the remaining four roots स्तु, द्रु, स्रु, and श्रु, the present sûtra prohibits the इट् which would have come before the affix थल् by the rule of Bhâradvâja (VII. 2. 63 S. 2296) and the इट् which would have come before the affixes व or म &c. by the present rule of Krâdi (i.e., the affixes व, म, महिङ् and महिङ्);

Note:—Thus कृ—चक्रे, चक्रिवहे; चकृमहे; भू—बभूव, बभूविव &c. ‹?›

These roots with the exception of ‹?› are Aniṭ by VII. 2. 10 S. 2243; their special mention here is for the sake of niyama, namely these roots alone are aniṭ in the Perfect, other roots are all Seṭ in the Perfect. Thus ‹?› All anudâtta roots of the Dhâtupâṭha are to be understood, by this rule, to get इट्. The affix थल् of the Perfect gets इट् after भू, as the irregular form बभूविथ in VII. 2. 64, indicates that in the Vedic it does not get इट् after भू, but in the classical literature it does. By VII. 2. 63, S. 2296 the थल् would have got इट् after द्रु and स्रु; that also is prohibited by the present sûtra. As तुष्टोथ, दुद्रोथ, सुस्रोथ, शुश्रोथ ॥

Vârt:—इट् is added when कृ takes the सुट् augment: as संचस्करिथ, संचस्करिम । The sûtra VII. 2. 63, S. 2296 applies here also, as संस्करिथ ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2294. After a root, which in the Dhâtupâṭha, ends in a vowel, and after which the First Fut. affix tâsi is always devoid of the augment इट्; (after such a root) थल् the personal ending of the Perfect, like tâsi, does not also get the augment इट् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2295. After a root which possesses a short 'a' as its root vowel in the original enunciation (the Dhâtupâṭha), and after which the First Fut. affix तासि is always devoid of the augment इट्, थल् the Personal ending of the Perfect, like तासि, does not get the augment इट् ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2296. In the opinion of Bharadvaja, it is only after a root which ends in a short ऋ, and after which the First Fut. तासि is always devoid of the augment इट् that थल् also, like तासि, does not take the augment इट्.

Therefore, the other affixes do take इट्. On this there is the following verse (saṅgraha), which sums up the last three sûtras:—

That root which ends in a vowel, or which has a short अ in the Dhâtupâṭha, and which is aniṭ before तास् affix, is optionally सेट् before थल् affix. But if such root ends in short ऋ, then it is invariably aniṭ before थल् affix. Roots other than कृ &c. are सेट् in the Perfect.

One should not, however, think that the four roots स्तु, द्रु, स्रु and श्रु will also be optionally aniṭ in थल् as they are not ṛi-ending roots. The rule made by Bharadvâja removes the prohibition with regard to the addition of इट् made by the two immediately preceding sûtras S. 2294 and 2295 : and not the इट् of S. 2293. This is on the maxim 'a rule, may it enjoin or forbid anything, either enjoins or forbids only that which is nearest to it in some other rule.' (see Vol I. 203)

Therefore वि + अ + आज् + थ = विवजिथ or विव्यजिथ or विव्याजिथ ।

In forming the Aorist, the following sûtra applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2297. Before the Aorist-characteristic सिच् (चि), Vṛiddhi is substituted in the Parasmaipada, for the final of a stem ending in इ, उ, ऋ (long or short, I. 1. 3).

Thus अवैषीत् or आजीत् &c. The Conditional is अवैष्यत् or आजिष्यत् ।

तेज २४९ पालने । तेजति ॥
249. √ Teja, 'to protect.'
लट्—तेजति । लिट्—सितेज । लुट्—तेजिता । Noun:—तेजः ॥

खज २५० मन्थे । खजति ॥
250. √ Khaja, 'to churn', 'to stir.'
लट्—खजति । लिट्—चखाज । लुट्—खजिता । लुङ्—अखासीत्, ‹?› । Noun:—खलाकः ॥

कज २५१ मदे ।
251. √ Kaja, 'to be drunk.' This root is not given in the Siddhânta.
लट्—कजति ॥

खजि २५२ गतिवैकल्ये । खञ्जति ॥
252. √ Khaji, 'to go lame, limp.'
लट्—खञ्जति । लिट्—चखञ्ज । लुट्—खञ्जिता ॥

एज २५३ कम्पने । एजांचकार ॥
253. √ Ejṛ, 'to tremble.' The root एज् 'to shine,' has already been taught before.
लट्—एजति । लिट्—एजाञ्चकार । लुट्—एजिता । लृट्—एजिष्यति । णिच्—एजयति । Aorist मा भवानेजित् । सन्—एजिजिषति ॥

टुओस्फूर्जा २५४ वज्रनिर्घोषे । स्फूर्जति । पुस्फूर्ज ॥
254. √ Ṭuo sphûrjâ, 'to thunder.'
लट्—स्फूर्जति । लिट्—पुस्फूर्ज । लुट्—स्फूर्जिता । णिच्—स्फूर्जयति । Aorist अस्फूर्जीत् । सन्—पुस्फूर्जिषति । यङ्—पोस्फूर्ज्यते । Yaṅ-luk पोस्फूर्ति । Imperfect अपोस्फूर्त् । Passive Participle स्फूर्तः or स्फूर्जितः । Active Participle स्फूर्तवान् । Noun:—स्फूर्जथुः ॥
दि २५५ क्षये । अकर्मकः । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थस्तु सकर्मकः । क्षयति । क्षिताय । चिक्षियतुः । चिक्षियुः । चिक्षयिथ-चिक्षेथ । चिक्षियिव । चिक्षियिम । क्षेता ।
255. kshi, to waste, to decay. The root is intransitive; it is transitive when it is used in a causative sense.

लट् । लिट् – चिक्षाय । चिक्षियतुः । चिक्षियुः । चिक्षयिथ or चिक्षेथ । चिक्षियथुः । चिक्षिय । चिक्षयाव or चिक्षिव । चिक्षियाम or चिक्षिम । लुट्, क्षेता । लृट् - क्षेष्यति । लोट् - क्षयतु । -- अक्षीयत् । विधिलिङ् - क्षयेत् । In forming the Benedictive the following Sutra i.e., 2298 applies. आशीर्लिङ् - क्षीयात् । लुङ् अक्षेषीत् । सन् - चिक्षीषति । यङ् - चेक्षीयते । यङ्लुक् :- चेक्षेति । Passive Participle, क्षीणः Active Participle, क्षीणवान् ।
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
अजन्तस्याङ्गस्य दीर्घः स्यात्यादौ प्रत्यये परे न तु कत्सार्वधातुकयोः । चीयात् । षो ।
2298. A long is substituted for the final vowel of the stem before an affix beginning with a य् having an indicatory ‹?› when it is not either a Krit or a Sarvadhatuka affix.
Thus क्षीयात् ॥

The second root ends in ड, its being read here along with roots ending in ट is because it has the same meaning as म्लेट्. Just as नर्द was read with नाथ. This root meṭṛ is not given in the Siddhânta. sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2299. The Vṛiddhi of the vowel of the following stems does not take place before the इट्-augmented s-Aorist in the Parasmaipada ; namely—the stems ending in ह्, म् or य्, the roots क्षण, श्वस् and जागृ, a stem formed with णि, the root श्वि, and the roots having an indicatory ॠ in the Dhâtupâṭha. Note:—Thus ग्रह, 'to catch' अग्रहीत् ; श्यम्, 'to sound' अशमीत् । वम्, 'to vomit' अवमीत् । व्यय, 'to expend' अव्ययीत् । क्षण, 'to hurt' अक्षणीत् । श्वस्, 'to breathe' अण्वसीत् । जागृ, 'to be awake' अजागरीत् । णि, ऊन (churâdi), 'to lessen' अनवीत् ; ईष, 'to send' ऐषीत् ॥ श्वि, अश्रयीत् । ॠदिताम्, कट, 'to cover' अकाटीत्, अचाटीत् ॥ Therefore there is no Vṛiddhi. Thus we have अकाटीत् and अचाटीत् ॥ अट ३१७, पट ३१८ गतौ । आट । आटतुः । आटुः । पपाट । पेटतुः । पेतुः ॥ 317. ✓ Aṭa, 318. ✓ paṭa 'to go, to wander, to roam.' Pre. - अटति । Per. - आट । आटतुः । 3. गण्ड: 'cheek.' According to some the last five roots (including gaṇḍa) are incapable of conjugation. Nouns only are formed from them.

Here end the roots whose final is a letter of the palatal class.

अथ पवगीयान्ताः । तत्रानुदात्तेतः स्तोभत्यन्ताश्चतुस्त्रिंशत् ॥

Now we give the roots ending in a labial. Of these, thirty-four up to Stubha are anudāttet.

तिपृ ३८५ तेपृ ३८६, टिपृ ३८७, ष्टेपृ ३८८ क्षरणार्थाः । ‹?› अनुदात्तः । क्षीरस्वामी स्वयं सेडिति बभ्राम । तेपते । तितिपे । क्रादिनियमादिट् । तितिषिषे । तेप्ता । तेप्स्यते ॥

The first of these roots is anudātta also and hence अनिट् । Kshīrasvāmī mistook it as सेट् ।

Thus Pre. तेपते । Per. तितिपे । Though this is aniṭ, yet in the Second and First Person would be added by the rule of kryādi (VII. 2. 15, S. 2293). Therefore, we have तितिषिषे and तितिषिवहे ॥ The First Future is तेप्ता । The Second Future is तेप्स्यते ।

In forming the Benedictive the following rule applies:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2301. ए is substituted for the अ of तृ, फल, भज and त्रप, and the reduplicate is elided, when the affixes of the Perfect having an indicatory क् (or ङ्) follow, as well as when थल् with the इट् augment follows.

Thus (तेतुः, तेतु, तेतिथ; फेलतुः, फेलुः, फेलिथ; भेजतुः, भेजुः, भेजिथ), त्रेपे, त्रेपाते, त्रेपिरे ॥

Note:— In the case of तृ the rule applies to the vowel obtained by Guṇa contrary to VI. 4. 126, in फल and भज् the rule, that no different substitute should be in the reduplicate, is not adhered to, and in त्रप् the अ does not stand between the two simple consonants.

The root त्रपूष being exhibited with an indicatory ष् shows that the addition of the augment is optional (VII. 2. 44 S. 2279 and VII. 2. 15. S. 3025). Thus the First Future is त्रपिता or त्रप्ता । Benedictive त्रपिषीष्ट or त्रप्सीष्ट । The indicatory ष् shows that the feminine noun from this root is formed by ‹?› (III. 3. 104 S. 3281). As त्रपा ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
एतयोर्नुमागमः स्यादचि । जम्भते । अजम्भिष्ट । जम्भिता । जम्भिषीष्ट । जृम्भते ॥ 2302. The augment 'num' is added after the root-vowel in 'radh' and 'jabh,' before the affixes beginning with a vowel. Note:—Thus रन्धयति, रन्धकः, साधुरन्धी, रन्धो वर्तते । जम्भयति, जम्भकः साधुजम्भो जम्भं जम्भं जम्भी वर्तते । Though the वृद्धि rule is subsequent, it is superseded by
the augment. Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with vowel ? Observe रखा, जभ्यम् ॥
Pre. जम्भते । Per. जजम्भे । I Fut. जम्भिता । II Fut. जम्भिष्यते । Imper. जम्भताम् । Imperf. अजम्भत । Pot. जम्भे॑त । Bene. जम्भिषीष्ट । Aorist अजम्भिष्ट । Condi. अजम्भिष्यत । Caus. जम्भयते or ति । Aorist अजजम्भत् । Desi. जिजम्भिषते । Inten. जञ्जभ्यते (VII. 1. 24. S. 2635 and VII. 4. 88. S. 2638), यङ् लुक् जञ्जभीति, or जञ्जब्धि । Dual जञ्जब्धः । Pl. जञ्जम्भति । Noun जम्भः tooth. Maitreya makes it aniṭ as जब्धम् ॥
416. √ Jṛmbhi, 'To copulate,' ('To gape, yawn'). Pre. जृम्भते । Per. जेजेम्भे । I Fut. जृम्भिता । Aorist अजृम्भिष्ट । Caus. जृम्भयते or ति । Aorist अजजृम्भत् । Desi. जिजृम्भिषते ॥
शल्भ ४१७ कत्थने ।
417. Śalbha, 'To praise,' 'to boast.' Pre. शलभते । Per. शशलभे । I Fut. शलभिता । Aorist अशलभिष्ट । Caus. शलभयते । Desi. शिशलभिषते । Inten. शाशलभ्यते ॥
वल्भ ४१८ भोजने ।
418. Valbha, 'To eat.' This root begins with the dento-labial व ॥

गल्भ ४१९ धाष्ट्यें ।
419. √ Galbha, To be bold or confident, or arrogant.
Pre. गल्भते । Per. जगल्भे । I Fut. गल्भिता । Aorist अगल्भिष्ट । Caus. गल्भयते । Desi. जिगल्भिषते । Inten. जागल्भ्यते । Noun: प्रगल्भः 'daring, brave, audacious.'
श्रम्भु ४२० प्रमादे । तालव्यादिर्दन्त्यादिश्च । श्रम्भते । स्रम्भते वा ।

Now we give Parasmaipadi roots ending in a labial.
422. गुपू रक्षणे 'to protect.' In its conjugation the following sūtra applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2303. The affix आय comes without changing the sense, after गुपू 'to protect,' धूप 'to heat,' विच्छ 'to approach,' पण 'to praise' and पन् 'to praise.'
(
NOTE:— Thus गोपायति 'he protects'; धूपायति 'he heats'; so also, विच्छायति, पणायति, and पनायति.

NOTE.— The verb being read along with 'to praise,' has here the sense of praise only; so that the affix does not come after the verb ‹?› when it means 'to make a contract'; as शतस्य पणते, सहस्रस्य पणते.

NOTE:— The verbs in ‹?› do not take Âtmanepada affixes, as there is no indicatory letter to show that.

Thus गुप् + आय् ।

Now applies S. 2189 and we get the guna of उ; as, गोपाय ।

This is now the root, for it gets the designation of Dhâtu or root by the following sutra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2304. All the words ending with the affixes ‹?› and the rest are called Dhâtus.

NOTE:— This extends the sphere of Dhâtus or roots already defined in Sûtra I. 3. 1. These roots may be called derivative roots. They are separate independent roots, and have all the functions of a root, as taking tense-affixes &c. as shown in the above examples. Thus चिकीर्षति 'to wish to do,' कारयति 'to cause to do'; चेक्रियते 'to do repeatedly' are separate roots and not the same as कृ, 'to do'; and thus take लट् &c.

The stems that take the affixes beginning with ‹?› and ending with ‹?› namely, the following 1. ‹?› (III. 1. 5, 6, 7) 2. ‹?› (III. 1. 8) 3. ‹?› (III. 1. 9), 4. ‹?› (III. 1. 11) 5. ‹?› (III. 1. 13), 6. ‹?› (III. 1. 20) 7. ‹?› (III. 1. 21), 8. ‹?› (III. 1. 22) 9. ‹?› (III. 1. 25) 10. ‹?› (III. 1. 27), 11. ‹?› (III. 1. 28), 12. ‹?› (III. 1. 29), and 13. ‹?›, (III. 1. 30) are called also roots. Being roots they are conjugated in लट्, लिट् &c.

Thus Pres. ‹?› sutras apply:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2306. आम् is the affix of the verb कास् 'to cough,' and of those roots that are formed by affixes (i. e. the derivative verbs), when लिट् follows, except in the Mantra.

NOTE:— This forms the Periphrastic Perfect. The perfect of कास् will be कासाम्, after which the terminations of the Perfect are all elided (II. 4. 81) and instead, the perfect tense of the auxiliary verb कृ or भू or अस् is added. As कासाञ्चक्रे 'he coughed'; चोरयाञ्चकार 'he stole.' So also ‹?›.

This rule however does not apply to the Vedas; as Rig Veda I. 79. 2.

Vârt:— This rule only applies where the root is polysyllabic consisting of more than one vowel; as चुलुम्पाञ्चकार, दरिद्राञ्चकार । The force of this vartika is that even of non-derivative roots, the Perfect will be formed periphrastically if the root consists of more than one syllable. In fact, the vârtika would substitute the word anekâchaḥ in the room of pratyayât. The sutra would then run thus: "kâsânekâcha âm amantre liṭi": "आम् is added to the root kâs and to roots of more than one syllable in the Perfect; but not in the Vedas."
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2307. From this upto VI. 4. 68 inclusive, is always to be supplied "before an affix called ârdhadhâtuka (III. 4. 114 &c)."

NOTE:— This is an adhikâra sûtra and extends upto VI. 4. 69 (exclusive). In all the sûtras upto VI. 4. 68 should be supplied the phrase "before an affix called ârdhadhâtuka." Thus VI. 4. 48 teaches "the अ standing at the end of a verbal stem is elided." To complete the sense we should add: "before an ârdhadhâtuka affix." Thus the final अ of the verbal stem चिकीर्ष is elided before the ârdhadhâtuka affix तृच्, as चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्; but the final is not elided before a sârvadhâtuka affix, as the अ of भू in भवति, भवतः. The luk-elision of शप् after roots of अदादि class, implies that there is never lopa of अकार.

Kârikâ:—
लोपो यलोपोऽथ णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् ।
आल्लोप ईत्वमेत्वं च चिण्वद्भावश्च सेधुटि ॥

The following purposes are served by this sutra, i. e. an ârdhadhâtuka affix causes the following special changes: (1) अलोपः—The elision of अ of a stem, as shown above, in चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्. (2) यलोपश्च । The elision of य by VI. 4. 49, 50: as बेभिदिता, बेभिदितुम्, बेभिदितव्यम् from the intensive stem. Before Sârvadhâtuka, we have बेभिद्यते, चेच्छिद्यते । (3) णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् । The elision of णि by VI. 4. 51, as कारणा, हारणा, पाच्यते (पाचि + यक् + ते = पाच + य + ते), पाक्यते । In Sârvadhâtuka, पाचयति, याजयति, कारयति, हारयति । (4) आल्लोपः—the elision of आकार, VI. 4. 64: पपतुः, पपुः, ववतुः, वपुः । In Sârvadhâtuka, यान्ति, वान्ति । (5) ईत्वम्—The substitution of long ई for आकार in some roots, VI. 4. 65: as दीयेताम्, दीयेरन्; in Sârvadhâtuka प्रदाताम्, प्रधाताम् । (6) एत्वम्—The substitution of ए for आकार, VI. 4. 68; as म्लेयात्, ग्लेयात्; in Sârvadhâtuka, स्नायात्, ग्लायात् । This is confined to the Precative (âśîrliṅ). (7) चिण्वद्भावश्च सेधुटि—The treatment of the Precative like Aorist Passive in चिण् by VI. 4. 62, as कारिषीष्ट, हारिषीष्ट । In Sârvadhâtuka क्रियेत, ह्रियेत ।
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2308. The अ standing at the end of a stem is elided before an Ârdhadhâtuka affix.

NOTE:— Thus चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम् and चिकीर्षितव्यम्, from the Desiderative stem चिकीर्ष । So also धिनुतः and कृणुतः from the roots धिन्व् and कृण्व्; thus धिन्व् + उ (III. 1. 80) = धिन् + अ + उ (III. 1. 80) = धिन् + उ (अ being elided before the ârdhadhâtuka उ) = धिनु, the 3rd Personal dual of it is धिनुतः । The addition of अ by III. 1. 80 and its subsequent elision by the present sûtra, may appear a redundancy, but the elided अ being sthânivat, prevents guṇa of धि । So also कृणुतः । See sûtra III. 1. 80. Why do we say 'the अ is elided'? Observe चेता, स्तोता here इ and उ have not been elided. Why do we say 'तः with a त'? The long आकार will not be elided: as याता, वाता । Why do we say 'before an Ârdhadhâtuka'? Before Sârvadhâtuka there will be no elision of अ, nor before a Taddhita: as पचथम् and वृक्षता ॥

Vârt:— The elision of such अ takes place even to the supersession of the subsequent rules relating to Vṛiddhi and lengthening. As चिकीर्षकः, जिहीर्षकः, चिकीर्ष्यते and जिहीर्ष्यते ॥

Thus गोपाय + आम् + चकार = गोपायाञ्चकार or गोपायां बभूव or गोपायामास । The affix आय being optional before लिट् (III. 1. 31. S. 2305) we have the alternative forms जुगोप, जुगुपतुः । The root गुपू has an indicatory ऌ and so the इट् augment is optional (VII. 2. 44. S. 2279). As जुगोपिथ or जुगोप्थ । The लुट् is गोपायिता or गोपिता or गोप्ता । The लिङ् is गोपाय्यात् or गुप्यात् । The लुङ् is अगोपायीत् or अगोपीत् or अगौप्सीत् ॥

गुपू ४२२ रक्षणे ।
422. Gupû, to protect. Pre. गोपायति । Per. जुगोप । जुगुपतुः । जुगोपिथ or जुगोप्थ । जुगुपिथ or जुगुप्थ । I Fut. गोपिता or गोप्ता । II Fut. गोपिष्यति or गोप्स्यति । Imperative गोपायतु । Imper. अगोपायत् । Pote. गोपायेत् । Bene. गुप्यात् । Aorist अगौप्सीत् or अगोपीत् । Condi. अगोपिष्यत् or अगोप्स्यत् । Caus. गोपयति । Aorist अजीगुपत् । Desi. जुगुप्सति or जुगोपिषति or जुगोपिषति । Inten. जोगुप्यते । This yaṅ is never elided. 427. Shapa, To connect, to know completely. Samavâya means 'connection,' or 'thorough understanding.' Pre. षपति । Per. शशाप । I Fut. षपिता । Aorist अशापीत् । Caus. शापयति । Aorist अशीषपत् । Desi. शिषपिषति । Inten. शाषप्यते । Nouns सप्तिः 'a yoke,' 'a horse.' सप्तन् 'seven.'

Nouns: चोपनः, चोपकः, क्षुद्रम् ॥

तुप ४३१, तुम्प ४३२, त्रुप ४३३, त्रुम्प ४३४, तुफ ४३५, तुम्फ ४३६, त्रुफ ४३७, त्रुम्फ ४३८, हिंसार्थाः । तोपति । तुतोष । तुम्पति ।
Now we give the roots whose final is a nasal. Of these the ten ending with kami are Anudātteta.

461. Ghiṇi, to take; to receive. Pre. ‹?› । Per. ‹?› । I Fut. ‹?› । II Fut. ‹?› । Impera. ‹?› । Imper. ‹?› । Pot. ‹?› । Bene. ‹?› । Aor. ‹?› । Con. ‹?› । Caus. ‹?› । Aor. ‹?› । Desi. ‹?› । Intens. ‹?› । yaṅ luk, ‹?› । Imperfect ‹?› । Ger. ‹?› ॥

463. Ghṛṇi, to take, to receive to seize. Pre. ‹?› । Per. ‹?› । Intens. ‹?› । yaṅ luk, ‹?› or ‹?› । Imper. ‹?› ॥

४६४, घूर्ण ४६५, भ्रमणे । ‹?› । घूर्णते । मेोदादेः परस्मैपदिनी ॥

464. Ghuṇa, 465 ghūrṇa, to roll, stagger, reel.

464. Ghuṇa. Pre. ‹?› । Per. ‹?› । I Fut. ‹?› । Caus. ‹?› । Aorist. ‹?› । Desi. ‹?› or ‹?› । Intens. ‹?› । yaṅ luk ‹?› or ‹?› । Dual ‹?› । Noun ‹?› । Ger. ‹?› or ‹?› ॥

465. Ghūrṇa, to roll &c. These two roots Ghuṇa and Ghūrṇa are Parasmaipadī also in the Tudādi class.
Pre. घूर्णते । The Imperfect in yaṅ luk is अजीघूर्णत् (VIII. 2. 24. § 280).

पण ४६६ व्यवहारे, स्तुतौ च । पन ४६७, च । स्तुतावित्येव संबध्यते पृथङ्निर्देशात् । पनिसाहचर्यात्पणेरपि स्तुतावेवायप्रत्ययः । व्यवहारे तु पणते । पेणे । पणितेत्यादि । स्तुतावनुबन्धस्य केवले चरितार्थत्वादायप्रत्ययान्ताश्चात्मनेपदम् । पणायति । पणायाञ्चकार । पेणे । पणायितासि । पणितासे । पणाय्यात् । पणिषीष्ट । पनायति । पनायाञ्चकार । पेने ॥

466. Paṇa and 467. Pana.
The first root means 'to transact business' 'to buy' as well as 'to praise.' The second root पन means only to praise. The 'च' draws in the anuvṛtti of स्तुतौ only and not that of व्यवहारे because it has been exhibited separately and not as पण-पनौ व्यवहारे स्तुतौ च.
These two roots take आय by III. 1. 28, § 2303, but पण must then mean 'to praise' only, for it has been read along with पन in that sūtra. But when पण means 'to deal or barter &c.' the form is पणते । Per. पेणे । First Fut. पणिता.
The anudātta indicatory final vowel in पण and पन finds its scope only when the roots mean 'to praise,' therefore when the roots take the affix आय, they will be Parasmaipadī and not Ātmanepadī. As पणायति । Per. पणायाञ्चकार । First Future पणायिता or पणितासे । Ben. पणाय्यात् or पणिषीष्ट ॥

466. Paṇa, 'To transact business, to buy,' (2. 'To praise.') The following conjugation is valid in the sense of transacting business only.
Pre. पणते । Per. पेणे । I Fut. पणिता । II Fut. पणिष्यते । Imperative पणताम् । Imper. आपणत । Pote. पणेत । Bene. पणिषीष्ट । Aorist अपणिष्ट । Condi. अपणिष्यत । Caus. पाणयति । Aorist अपपाणत् or अपीपणत् । Desi. पिपणिषते । Inten. पम्पण्यते । Yaṅ luk पम्पणीति or पम्पण्टि, Dual, पम्पण्ढः । Imperfect अपम्पण् । Past Part. Pass. पणितम् । Adjective, पण्यम् । पाण्यन् Nouns, पणः 'trade.' पाणिः 'a trader.' पणिकाः (Uṇ. II. 20) — पणित्रीः पणिकान् ॥

466 A. Paṇa, to praise. In this sense आय is added and the conjugation is then Parasmaipadī. When आय is not added, then the forms are as given before.
Pre. पणायति । As पणायति राजानम् 'He praises the king.' Per. पणायाञ्चकार । I Fut. पणायिता । पणायितासि । पणायिष्यति । Pote. पणायेत् । Bene. पणाय्यात् or पणायिषीष्ट । Aorist अपणायीत् or अपणिष्ट । Condi. अपणायिष्यत् or अपणिष्यत् ॥

467. Pana, to praise. Pre. पनायति । Per. पनायाञ्चकार or पेने । Noun पनः ॥

भाम ४६८ क्रोधे । भामते । बभामे ॥

468. Bhāma, to be angry. Pre. भामते । Per. बभामे । I Fut. भामिता । Desi. बिभामिषते । Inten. 3. S. बाभाम्यते 1st. S. बाभाम्ये 1. D. बाभाम्यावहे । 1. P. बाभाम्यामहे ॥ Aorist अभामिष्ट । Nouns भामः, भामिनी ॥

क्षमूष् ४६९ सहने । क्षमते । उत्तमे । चक्षमिषे । चक्षंसे । चक्षमिध्वे । चक्षन्ध्वे । चक्षमिध्व ॥

469. Kṣamūṣ, 'to endure, to suffer.' The indicatory long ū makes it optionally aniṭ (VII. 2. 44 and 15, § 2279 and 3025); the ष् is for feminine ‹?› (III. 3. 104, § 3281).
Thus the Present is क्षमते.
The Perfect is 3. S. चक्षमे, 2. S. चक्षमिषे or चक्षंसे, 2. P. चक्षमिध्वे or चक्षन्ध्वे ॥ In the First Person, the form is चक्षमे । But in the aniṭ form, the म् will be changed to न् by the following sūtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2309. म् is substituted for the म् of a root before the affixes beginning with म and व ॥

NOTE:—As the Imperfect of भ्रम्, as in the sentence ‹?›. The व् is elided as a Vedic diversity. So also with क्षम्, the augment इट् is not added by the option allowed, owing to VII. 2. 44. This sūtra applies to those cases where the म् is not at the end of a word, as it was in the last sūtra.

Thus from the root क्षम् we have in the perfect 1st person dual चक्षन्वहे । But when the intermediate इट् is not added, then the म् is changed to न् and then to अनुस्वार. As चक्षमिषे or चक्षंसे; so also in the plural, चक्षमिध्वे or चक्षन्ध्वे ॥

469 A. Kṣamūṣ, to endure to suffer. Pre. क्षमते । Per. चक्षमे । I Fut. क्षमिता or चक्षमिता । II Fut. क्षमिष्यते or क्षंस्यते । Imperative क्षमताम् । Imperf. अक्षमत । Pote. क्षमेत । Bene. क्षमिषीष्ट or क्षंसीष्ट or क्षामिषीष्ट । Aorist अक्षमिष्ट or अक्षंस्त । Condi. अक्षमिष्यत or अक्षंस्यत । Pass. क्षम्यते । Aorist अक्षमि or अक्षापि । अक्षामि । Caus. क्षामयति । Aorist अचिक्षमत् (VI. 4. 92, § 2568). I. F. क्षामयिता । Ben. क्षामयिषीष्ट । Desi. चिक्षमिषते or चिक्षंसते । Inten. चङ्क्षम्यते । Yaṅ luk चङ्क्षमीति or चङ्क्षन्ति । The nasal is added to the reduplicate by VII. 4. 85, § 2613. Aorist अचङ्क्षमीत् । Past Part. Pass. क्षान्तः । Ger. क्षमित्वा or क्षान्त्वा । Infini. क्षमितुम् or क्षन्तुम् । Nouns क्षमः । F. क्षमा, क्षमकः ॥

470. कम् कान्तौ । The word Kānti here means 'desire.' The root therefore means 'to desire, long for, wish.' The following sūtra applies to its conjugation.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2310. The affix णिङ् comes without changing the sense after the root कम् 'to desire.'

The ङ् indicates vṛddhi (VII. 2. 115) and ङ् shows that the root takes the affixes of the Ātmanepada; as, कामयते 'he desires'; so also कामयेते and कामयन्ते ॥

The Perfect is formed periphrastically by आम् which being an ārdhadhātuka affix required the elision of णि of the root by VI. 4. 51, § 2313. But the following sūtra prevents the elision:—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2311. अय् is substituted for the णि of णिङ्, before the affixes आम्, अन्त, आलु, आय्य, इत्स्नु, and ष्णुक ॥

Note:—Thus कारयाञ्चकार, हारयाञ्चकार, मण्डयन्तः मण्डयन्तः (formed by the Jhac affix झ = अन्त; added to the roots मण्ड and मन्त्र) धातु । पहयालुः । आय्य—उपायाय्यः सहायाय्यः । इत्स्नुः—स्तनयित्स्नुः । ष्णुक—पोषयिष्णुकः ॥

Note:—This sūtra could have been well dispensed with for the affix णि would take guṇa ए which will be changed to अय् by the rules of Sandhi, before these affixes. The substitution of अय् for णि is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra VI. 4. 56, § 2336 however, because there णि could not be changed to अय् by any sandhi-rules.

The णि is always changed to अय्; therefore the अय् substitution of the present sūtra would have been redundant, but it is taught here in order to supersede the elision declared hereafter in VI. 4. 51, § 2313. Thus कामयां ‹?›

The addition of आय being optional (III. 1. 31, § 2305) we have the alternative form चकमे also.

The Future forms are:—कामयिता or कमिता । कामयिष्यते or कमिष्यते ॥

In forming the Aorist, the following sūtra applies.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2312. After a root which ends in णि (III. 1. 20, 21, 44, &c.) and after the verb श्रि 'to service,' द्रु 'to run,' and स्रु 'to drop,' चङ् is the substitute of च्लि, when लुङ् follows signifying an agent. NOTE:— The ङ् prevents guṇa and vṛiddhi: अ is to distinguish it from ‹?›. When चङ् is added there is reduplication (VI. 1. 11). The usual terminations of the Imperfect are employed after the root, when चङ् is used; as, अचीकरत् 'he caused to make'; अशिश्रियत् 'he served or went'; अदुद्रुवत् 'he ran'; असुस्रुवत् 'it flowed.' This form is not used in Passive; as, ‹?›. Thus ‹?›. Now applies the following sûtra, by which the (णि) is elided.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2313. The णि of the verbal stem formed with the affix णि, is elided before an ârdhadhâtuka affix which does not take the augment इट् ॥ NOTE:— This debars the semi-vowel य्, the guṇa, vṛiddhi and the long substitutions. Thus अशशमत्, अशीशमत्, आटिटत्, कारणा, हारणा, कारकः, हारकः, कार्यते, हार्यते and कारयिता (see VII. 4. 1 for the shortening of the stem of the Aorists in these). Why do we say 'not having the augment इट्'? Observe कारयिता and हारयिता ॥ The sûtra VI. 4. 82, S. 272 (a semi-vowel is substituted for the final इ or ई of a root before a vowel-beginning affix &c.) being subsequent in order of Ashṭâdhyâyî would debar the present sûtra and prevent the elision of णि and cause य् to be substituted instead. This however is prevented by the following. Vârtika:— The rule ordaining the elision of णि (S. 2313) and that teaching the elision of अ (VI. 4. 48, S. 2308) take effect even to the supersession of the subsequent rules ordaining इयङ् (VI. 4. 78, S. 2290), or semi-vowel (VI. 4. 82, S. 272), or guṇa, (VII. 3. 84, S. 2168 &c.) or vṛiddhi, (VII. 2. 115, S. 254), or lengthening. NOTE:— The elision of अ supersedes only the two rules of vṛiddhi, lengthening and not the others. The elision of (णि) supersedes all the above five rules of iyaṅ, yaṇ, guṇa, vṛiddhi and lengthening. Q. There is no necessity for this vârtika with regard to णि, for if the five rules mentioned above were not to be superseded by णि-elision, then this rule will find no scope anywhere. And as scope must be given to every rule, the present sûtra inferentially and necessarily supersedes the above rules. Ans. The vârtika is not unnecessary. The णि elision finds its unrestricted scope before the ârdhadhâtuka affixes like क्तिन् (III. 3. 174, S. 3313). Thus from शमि we have शान्तिः, from √ तमि तन्तिः. The intermediate इट् is prevented there by VII. 2. 9, S. 3163. Hence if this vârtika were not taught, the णि would be elided only before the ârdhadhâtuka kṛit affix क्तिन् and no where else. As a matter of fact, the force of the word अनिटि in the sûtra is that the rule of the elision of णि applies to all ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and not only to a single affix क्तिन्. NOTE:— Had the present sûtra not superseded इयङ् &c., then it would have been more proper to draft it as णेः only without the word अनिटि । For the sûtra with the anuvṛitti of आर्धधातुके read into it, would apply to the affix क्तिन्, only after the rules yaṇ &c. had restricted its scope. So there would be no necessity of adding अनिटि. The very fact that the word अनिटि is added shows that the sûtra has for its scope all ârdhadhâtuka affixes, and therefore it is an exception by anticipation to the rules of iyaṅ &c. Thus, इयङ् is superseded in अशिश्रियत्. It is a चङ् Aorist. There is no scope for guṇa here, as चङ् is ङित् and yaṇ of sûtra VI. 4. 82, S. 272 has also no scope, as the इ (णि) in श्रि is preceded by a conjunct consonant. The only rule left that would have applied to this णि is इयङ्. The present vârtika debars इयङ् but causes the elision of इ (णि) ॥ Similarly यण् (semivowel) substitution is superseded in आटिटत् । Guṇa is superseded in अशशमत् and vṛiddhi in कारकः and lengthening in कार्यते ॥ Now applies the following. Thus ‹?›
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2314. A short is substituted for the vowel, standing in a penultimate position, in the णि-formed stem; when the affix चङ् (of the Reduplicate Aorist) follows. Thus ‹?› (VI. 4. 51, S. 2313) = ‹?› (VII. 4. 1, S. 2314). Now applies the following sûtra which causes reduplication.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2315. Of a non-reduplicate root there is reduplication when the affix चङ् of the Aorist follows. Dr. Ballantyne translates it this:— "When चङ् follows, there are two in the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel, of an unreduplicated root; but the reduplication is of the second portion of a root that begins with a vowel." The first syllable is reduplicated if the first portion of the root begins with a consonant; the second syllable is reduplicated if the first portion begins with a vowel. Thus ‹?› Now applies the following atideśa sûtra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2316. In the reduplicated Aorist of the णि-stems, the reduplicate adapts itself to that of the Desiderative, when the vowel of the root is light, and the root has not lost its end-vowel before the णि affix. The word चङ्परे is a Bahuvrîhi compound and therefore it means णि. This word णि so qualified, as well as the word अङ्गस्य should both be twice employed in this sûtra, in order to give the full meaning. We explain therefore the sûtra thus:— "that णि which is followed by that affix which gives the designation of अङ्ग to the root"—this is one portion. The next part is—"a short vowel which follows such णि, and the abhyâsa of the aṅga which follows such short vowel of that abhyâsa, the operations are like those of the Desiderative, before the णि, when no अक्-vowel is elided." Or the word अङ्गस्य is not repeated. Then the sûtra would mean 'that aṅga which stands before that णि which is followed by चङ्; the abhyâsa of such an aṅga, when followed by a short vowel,—on that abhyâsa, the operations are like those of the Desiderative &c.' NOTE:— Dr. Ballantyne has translated this sûtra as follows:— "Let the effect be like as if सन् (III. 1. 7, S. 2608) had followed, on the reduplicate, if followed by a light vowel of an inflective base to which णि followed by चङ् is affixed provided there is not the elision of any letter in the pratyâhâra अक् occasioned by the affixing of णि (as, for example under the provisions of VI. 4. 48, S. 2308)." NOTE:— The words of this sûtra require a little detailed explanation. The word सन्वत् means "like unto सन् or Desiderative"; i. e. as the Desiderative is treated, so should the चङ् Aorist of the णि stems. The words लघुनि and चङ्परे are both in the Locative case, but not in apposition with each other, but refer to different objects. लघुनि means 'when a light vowel follows,' namely that reduplicate which is followed by the light root-vowel. The operations to be performed on such a reduplicate, in the चङ् Aorist, after the णि, are the same, as on the reduplicate of the Desiderative, अनग्लोपे "provided that a simple vowel of the Pratyâhâra अक् has not been elided." We read the word णि into this sûtra, because there can be no other root which will form a चङ् Aorist. णि stems form such Aorist, (III. 1. 48), as well as the simple roots श्रि, द्रु and स्रु. The word चङ्परे is a Bahuvrîhi and qualifies the word णि understood: that stem which is followed by चङ्; therefore, it refers to the णि stem, and not to the simple roots śri, dru and sru. The light vowel, therefore, refers to the light vowel of the णि-stem before चङ्. The word अनग्लोपे is in apposition with चङ्परे । Thus कम् + णिच्, (III. 1. 30) = चकाम् + णिच् + अत् (III. 1. 48) = अकाम् + अत् (VI. 4. 51) = अकमत् (VII. 4. 1) = अचकम् + अत् (VI. 1. 11). Then applies the next sûtra. NOTE:— Thus VII. 4. 79 teaches the substitution of ‹?› for ‹?› in the reduplicate of the Desiderative. The same substitution will take place in the reduplicate of the Aorist: as ‹?› Thus by VII. 4. 80, is substituted for
the ‹?› of the reduplicate in the Desiderative, the same will be the case in the reduplicate of the Aorist, as प्रपोपवत् and अलीलवत्, and अजीजवत् । Thus by VII. 4. 81, ‹?› is optionally substituted for उ in the Desiderative reduplicate of सु &c., the same will hold good in the Aorist-reduplicate, as ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?›, ‹?› or ‹?› । Why do we say 'having a light vowel' ? Observe प्रततक्षत्, अजागरत् ॥
By sûtra III. 1. 48 : 2313 the roots श्वि, ‹?› and सु also form चङ् aorist. The sanvadbhâva however does not take place with regard to these roots: because these roots do not get the designation of अङ्ग before चङ् । The rule is therefore confined to णि-roots, for these are the roots which get the designation अङ्ग before the affix चङ् । Moreover the reduplicate must be that of the ‹?›, which can be of णि-roots only.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2317. ‹?› is substituted for the final short अ of the reduplicate in the Desiderative.

NOTE:—As पिपचिषति, विवक्षिषति, (VIII. 2. 36, 41) चिखादिषति, विविदिषति ॥ Why do we say in the Desiderative ? Observe पपाच ॥ Why do we say 'for the ‹?›' ? Observe लुलूषति ॥ Why do we say 'short ‹?›' ? Observe पापचिषते the Desiderative of the Intensive पापच्यते ॥
Therefore अचिकम् + अत, अचिकम् + अत, because चङ् is considered like सन् ॥
Now applies the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2318. In the reduplicative syllable, a prosodially short vowel is lengthened in the Reduplicated Aorist of the णि-stem when the vowel of the root is light, and the root has not lost its end-vowel before the Causative णि ॥

Therefore अचिकम् + अत = अचीकमत ॥
The affix णि being optional, when it is not added, then applies the following vārtika:—"The aorist of Kam is formed by चङ् even when it does not take णि". As there is absence of णि, so we have neither lengthening nor sanvadbhâva. Thus अचकमत ॥

NOTE:—In Grammar there are two opinions as regards rules of definition (संज्ञा); one is expressed by the maxim कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् and the other by यथोद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् ॥ The first means that a rule defining a term (i.e. a saṁjñā rule) or giving a maxim of interpretation (paribhâshâ) manifests itself at the time of application. Whenever an occasion arises to apply such rule, it appears there anew. The other means that the saṁjñās and paribhâshâs remain where they have been originally taught, and do not appear anew each time when a particular operation is to be performed. They exert their influence from the place where they are, and do not require to be recited afresh each time that an operation is to be performed.

Now the abhyâsa is defined in the sûtra पूर्वेऽभ्यासः (VI. 1. 4. S. 2178) and the word abhyâsa occurs in the sûtra 2316. In both views of the function of a definition, the sûtras पूर्वेऽभ्यासः and सन्यल्लघुनि &c., will become one sentence. But in the first view of kâryakâla paksha the one-sentence will be of different padas or words; in the second view the one-sentence will be of different sentences. Mâdhava favours the view of kâryakâla paksha with regard to the sûtra 2316: which opinion the author has summarised in the following two verses :—

Verse 1. "According to Mâdhava, the rules of lengthening (2318) and sanvadbhâva (2316) apply there only where the kâryakâla function of a rule of definition being taken as valid, the aṅga or inflective base is reduplicated: and not where there are many-syllabled stems."

NOTE:—The sense is that in the sûtras 2316 and 2318 there is the anuvṛitti of the words aṅgasya and abhyâsasya. Here the designation of abhyâsa (reduplicate) will be given to the first portion of the doublet aṅga. Therefore the lengthening (2318) and sanvadbhâva (2316) will take place in that abhyâsa only which is the abhyâsa of an aṅga—that is where an aṅga has been reiterated, there the first portion will get the designation of abhyâsa for the purposes of the application of 2316 and 2318. As अचिकमत and अचीकमत ॥

Verse 2. "But in the roots चकस्, अर्थापय and ‹?› &c. there is no reduplication of an aṅga but only a portion of an aṅga is reduplicated. Therefore the two rules 2316 and 2318 are confined to monosyllabic roots."

NOTE:—Thus we have अचकासत्, आर्तिधपत् and और्णुनवत् without the application of S. 2316 and 2318. Here the whole aṅga chakâs &c. has not been reduplicated, but only a part of it, namely the first consonant in the case of chakâs and the second consonant in the case of vowel-beginning roots.
The result is that it is only in monosyllabic roots that the whole of aṅga is reduplicated, and not only a part of it (for there can be no such part), and consequently the dîrgha and sanvadbhâva apply to monosyllabic roots. Moreover, in this view (kâryakâla paksha), the word ekâchaḥ in the sûtra ekâcho dve prathamasya (VI. 1. 1. S. 2175), qualifies the word aṅgasya understood therein.

Obj. Let it be so, that the dîrgha and sanvadbhâva rules apply to the reduplicate of monosyllabic roots only. Then stretching this argument further the other rules that apply to reduplicates will also be restricted in their scope such as the rules of shortening (VII. 4. 59 S. 2180), retention of first consonant (VII. 4. 60. S. 2179) and substitution of a palatal (VII. 4. 62. S. 2245), &c. and these will not apply to polysyllabic roots.

Verses 3 and 4. As a matter of fact, if we explained the sûtra by saying aṅgasya avayavo yo' bhyâsa—'the reduplicate which is a portion of an aṅga'—then we opine that there must be lengthening in the case of ॠणु, and both (lengthening and sanvadbhâva) in the case of अर्थापयति: while in the case of chakâs none of these two will apply, or if they apply, it would be under restrictions. They will not apply when laghuni is qualified by णि by being in proximity to it, but will apply when aṅga is so qualified.

NOTE:—Thus instead of और्णुनवत् we would get और्णूनवत् । The sanvadbhâva is inappropriate here, for when it is doubled, there is no अ in the reduplicate, and so there can be no change of अ to इ ॥
The root अर्थापय is derived from अर्थ, in the sense of अर्थं चाचष्टे । The पुक् and णि augments are added before चङ् । Here both the dîrgha and sanvadbhâva will apply, and we should get the form आतिथिपत् instead of अतिथपत् । In the case of the root अर्थ (उपयाच्ञायाम्), of the churâdi class, the aorist is अतिथपत्: neither the dîrgha nor sanvadbhâva apply there.
In the root chakâs both will not apply or will apply with qualifications. If we explain the sûtra by saying chaṅpare ṇau yal laghu—'the reduplicate, if followed by a light vowel, in the case of a root to which णि followed by चङ् is affixed'—then there will be no application of these two rules. But if we explain the sûtra by chaṅpare ṇau yad aṅgam 'the reduplicate of an inflective base to which णि followed by chaṅ is affixed'—then these two rules will apply to chakâs. Thus in the first case we have अचकासत्, in the second अचीकसत् ॥

Verse 5. Because Kaiyyaṭa alone has given these two alternative explanations, the rules become applicable even where an ak-vowel of णि is elided so as to make them applicable to aglope roots also.

NOTE:—There are two conflicting views, one of Haradatta and another of Kaiyyaṭa. They can be harmonised by giving them different scopes.

कमु ४७० कान्तौ । कान्तिरिच्छा ॥

Now the thirty roots upto ‹?› inclusive are Parasmaipadî.

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2320. Before any other Present character ( शित् ), the root vowel of ष्ठिव्, क्रम्, and आचम् is lengthened.
Vartika :—It should be stated that the rule applies to cham, only then, when it is preceded by the preposition आ, and not otherwise.
Thus आचामति । Why do we say 'when preceded by आ'? Observe चमति, विचमति । The Aorist is अचमीत् । Some read जिमि also here. Thus जेमति ॥
Note:—The Kasika reads this sutra as stivuklamy-achamam siti, having inserted the आ from the vartika. Kram lengthens its vowel before syan by VII. 3. 76 S. 2319, the present rule produces this change before the affix sap also, which it gets by III. 1. 70.

498. Chhamu, to eat. Pre. छमति । Per. चच्छाम । I Fut. छमिता । Caus. छामयति । Pass. Aor. अच्छमि or अच्छापि । Nvul छामकामम् । Fut. छमिष्यते or छामिष्यते or छमियिष्यते । Desi. विच्छमिषति । Intens. चंछम्यते । Yan luk चंचमीति or चंछन्ति । P. P. Pass. छान्तः ॥

क्रमु ५०२ पादविक्षेपे ।
Now we take up the conjugation of 502. √ Kramu, 'to walk, to step.' This root takes श्यन् vikarana also by the following sutra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2321. The affix श्यन् is optionally employed in the active voice before a sarvadhatuka affix after the following verbs ; भ्राश् 'to shine,' भ्लाश् 'to shine,' भ्रम् 'to whirl,' क्रम् 'to walk,' क्लम् 'to be sad,' त्रस् 'to fear,' त्रुट् 'to cut,' and लष् 'to desire.'
Note:—Thus भ्राशते or भ्राश्यते 'he shines' ; भ्लाशते or भ्लाश्यते, 'he shines,' भ्रमति or भ्राम्यति 'he whirls' ; क्रामति or क्राम्यति 'he walks' ; क्लामति or क्लाम्यति 'he is sad.' So also त्रस्यति or त्रसति ; त्रुट्यति or त्रुटति ; लष्यति or लषति ॥
Thus क्रम् + शप् + ति or क्रम् + श्यन् + ति । Now applies the following sutra.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2322. The long is substituted in क्रम्, before a शित् affix, in the Parasmaipada.
As क्रामति, क्रामतः, क्रामन्ति or क्राम्यति &c. Per. चक्राम । Imperative क्राम्यतु or क्रामतु &c.
Why in the Parasmaipada ? Observe आक्रमते आदित्यः ॥
How do you explain the lengthening in उत्क्राम and संक्राम ( Imperative 2nd Per. Sg.) For when हि is elided by लुक्, (VI. 4. 105 ) then by I. 1. 63. the affix being dropped by a l-elision, it would produce no effect and so there ought to have been no lengthening ? This is no valid objection. The prohibition of I. 1. 63, applies to the अङ्ग stem after which the affix is elided. Here क्रम् is not a stem or anga with regard to हि, but it is a stem with regard to शप् as क्रम् + शप् + हि । Therefore, though हि is elided, the lengthening will take place by I. 1. 62, (प्रत्ययलक्षणम्) ॥
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2323. The augment इट् is added to ardhadhatuka valadi affixes after स्रु and क्रम्, only then when they do not occasion the taking of the Personal endings of the Atmanepada.
The roots स्रु and क्रम्, are udatta, and will get इट् augment naturally, the sutra makes a restriction or niyama. The restriction is that when the roots themselves occasion atmanepada affixes, then they do not take इट्, otherwise they will.
Thus अक्रमीत् ॥
502. Kramu, To walk, step. अय ५०३, वय ५०४, पय ५०५, मय ५०६, चय ५०७, तय ५०८, तय ५०९, गतौ । अयते ॥
The Present is अयते । In forming the Perfect the following sutra applies :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2324. After the verbs दय् 'to give,' 'to go,' and 'to protect,' अय् 'to go' and आस् 'to sit,' there is the affix आम्, when लिट् follows.
Thus अयाञ्चक्रे । First Future अयिता । Pot. अयेत । Benedictive अयिषीष्ट । Before the affix ध्वम् of the Perfect and Aorist, the following rule applies :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2325. The cerebral sound is optionally substituted for the ध of ध्वीध्वम् and of the Aorist and the Perfect after the augment इट् when the stem ends in इण् ॥
Thus अयिषीढ्वम् or अयिषीध्वम् । Aorist : आविष्ट ; आयिढ्वम् or आयिध्वम् ॥
When upasargas ending in r such as nir, dur, or pra precede √ aya, the r is changed to l by the following.
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text:
2326. ल् is substituted for the र् of a Preposition, when अय् follows.
Thus पलायते, प्लायते । The स्, of the Prepositions दुर् and निर्, is changed to र्, but this is not changed to ल्, because it is asiddha thus we have the forms निरयते, दुरयते । But there is a preposition निलि also, the र् of which is changed to ल्, as निलयते । See VII. 2. 46. So also there is a Preposition दुर् which forms दुलयते ॥
The word प्रत्ययः is not formed from प्रति + अय् but from प्रति + इण् ॥
If the root अय् is Atmanepadi why is it conjugated as Parasmaipadi in the following line of Magha :—"udayati vitatordhva rasmi rajjau." ? The word udayati is not formed by ud+√ay but from ud + √ i ; the √ i is obtained by the analysis of कटो as we have already shown. See कटो No. 342. Or the following maxim applies :
Maxim : The atmanepada, which a root may take because it is enunciated in the Dhatupatha as anudatteta is not of universal application. This maxim we infer from the jnapaka of चक्षिङ् which is shown with an indicatory ङ्. This root is of Adadi class No. 7. It is read as anudattet. It would have been conjugated in the Atmanepada by the mere fact of its being called anudattet, the further adding of ङ् shows that the anudattet atmanepada is not universally valid.
In the Perfect of √ aya, the rule VI. 4. 126 S. 2263 applies, because the root begins with a व and so we have ववये and not येये. But पेये, मेये, चेये, तेये । प्रणयते and नेये ॥

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2327. There is substitution of पी for प्याय्, when the affixes of the Perfect (लिट्) and the Intensive (यङ्) follow. The anuvritti of the word विभाषा ceases. The phrase प्यायः पी of the preceding Ashtadhyayi sutra is drawn into this by force of the word च 'and'; thus आपिप्ये, आपिप्याते, आपिप्यिरे । The rule of substitution of पी being a subsequent rule, would have debarred reduplication which precedes it in order. The reduplication, however, takes place after the substitution, by force of the maxim of पुनः प्रसङ्ग "occasionally the formation of a particular form is accounted for by the fact that a preceding rule is allowed to apply again, after it had previously been superseded by a subsequent rule." Thus आ + प्याय् + लिट् = पि + पी + ए = पि + प्य् + ए (VI. 4. 82. S. 272 the य् being substituted) = आपिप्ये with the affix आङ् । So also in the Intensive, as आपेपीयते, आपेपीयेते, आपेपीयन्ते ॥ In the Aorist, the following rule applies :—
sk_items.author: Śrīśa Chandra Vasu

sk_items.sanskrit_text: 2328. चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्लि, when त, the third person singular of the Atmanepada follows, after the verbs दीप, 'to shine,' जन 'to be produced', बुध 'to teach or know', पूर 'to be full', ताय् 'to extend or protect' and प्याय् 'to swell'. NOTE :—Thus अदीपि or अदीपिष्ट 'he shone' ; अजनि or अजनिष्ट 'he was produced' ; अबोधि or अबोधिष्ट 'he knew' ; अपूरि or अपूरिष्ट 'he was full' ; अतायि or अतायिष्ट 'he extended' ; अप्यायि or अप्यायिष्ट 'he grew'. Then applies the following.
